items.quote: Despite this increase in other expenses, we have reported an EBITDA margin of 11 plus percentage in this quarter.

items.statement: Margin dip attributed to non-recurring expenses; margin would have been better without ECL provision and anniversary costs
items.quote: So, because of that margin was a littl e thin, but still we have achieved an EBITDA margin similar in line with our earlier quarter.

items.statement: Strong traction in cyber security with continuing demand and growing customer logos; recognized by Equity Masters as one of three key Indian cyber security companies
items.quote: We see a lot of exciting opportunities. As you know, this quarter also we closed a couple of deals on Cyber Security, which we see there is a continuing demand, and we are also growing in our custom er's logos and we see that sector growing more and more over time.

items.statement: Data centre business seeing strong traction with government budget of Rs. 30,000 crore for data centres in India; responding to MIT RFP for AI and cloud
items.quote: Even the government of India, if you have seen, has also given out a budget of about Rs. 30,000 crore for making data centres in India to make sure that the data of Indians are kept inside.

items.statement: Opened Dubai office and hired 65 people for Middle East expansion; first BFSI customer in Abu Dhabi with service delivery started
items.quote: What we have done is opened up our office in Middle Ea st that is in Dubai for expanding our business there. And we are glad to share that we've got our first customer for which service delivery has already started and we have hired about 65 people there

items.statement: Hiring strategy includes proactive hiring for anticipatory projects which incurs initial expense but becomes recoverable quickly upon winning projects
items.quote: The other is to proactively hire base d on anticipatory projects where we are reasonably confident of winnin g them. And so there you incur an initial expense, but that becomes recoverable very quickly as soon as we win those projects

items.statement: Net cash balance increased to Rs. 115 crore as of September 30, 2024 from Rs. 99 crore a year ago; added Bank of Baroda as third banking partner
items.quote: Hence on a net basis our net cash balance has risen meaningfully to Rs. 115 crore.

items.statement: Debtor days improved to 72 days as of September 30, 2024 from 87 days a year ago; continue efforts to improve further
items.quote: Our DSOs continue to improve further, and we are at 72 days as of September 30, 2024 compared to 87 days at the same time last year.

items.statement: Return on capital employed reached double-digit 10%; would increase 3-4% if real estate properties excluded from net worth
items.quote: return on capital employed we have reached around two digit number, 10% we have achieved, but as earlier also we have pointed out our denominator, the networth figure is almost Rs. 600 crore.

items.statement: Expanding into application support and AI roadmap for better margins; engaging more in app support projects
items.quote: We are also engaging more into app support. We have an AI roadmap. So, we see that there are better margins also to be looked into areas where we can flourish more.

items.statement: Five or six large government tenders up for bidding; evaluating which to pursue; multiple advanced stage negotiations with private enterprise customers
items.quote: pipeline front, Q2 & H1 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript there are about five or six large tenders that are up for bidding. We are evaluating them. We will soon be fi guring out which are the ones that you want to go after and bid for it

items.statement: H1 margins are at the bottom; second half margins should be better and next year better than current year
items.quote: You should assume that the H1 margins are at the bottom and the second half should be better than the first half and the next year should be better than the current year.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM count to reach 700 by end of FY25 from 585 currently
items.quote: We are looking to go from 585 RM to 700 RM by the end of the year and this addition will happen across HNI as well as ultra HNI.

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution team to double from 400 to 800 over next 2 years
items.quote: the idea is to double the manpower count from here over the next 2 years. And we have currently a 400-member dedicated distribution team, which is going to scale up to garner more assets.

items.statement: Housing Finance RM count to grow strongly for rest of FY25 and FY26 driving disbursement and AUM growth
items.quote: we will continue to invest in our RM capacity for the coming 4 quarters at least and for FY25 & FY26 this should result in a very good momentum in terms of disbursement volume growth and which will then result into a good growth in our AUM.

items.statement: AMC to launch one new product per month to fill gaps in mutual fund suite and create first-of-kind passive products
items.quote: As we go forward, one should expect to see a product launch on the passive side or on the active side every month i.e., one in a month.

items.statement: Private Equity Fund 2 series exit expected in FY26, Real Estate Fund series 2 exit in FY28, then nearly annual exits
items.quote: You should look at the private equity fund 2 series exit in FY26. You should expect the real estate fund series 2 exit in FY28. And from there on, almost on an annual basis, you will have one exit.

items.statement: Investing ~15% of wealth management top line in RM additions with vintage under 3 years
items.quote: We have an investment of nearly 15% of the wealth management top line in these RMs in terms of a drag, which we expect to recoup over the course of the next couple of years.

items.statement: Investment Banking completed 22 deals with issue size Rs 25,000+ cr in H1FY25; second half pipeline is a multiple of first half
items.quote: Our Investment Banking business has successfully completed 22 deals with an issue si ze of Rs. 25,000+ cr during H1FY25. The second half pipeline is a multiple of the first half, and we see very strong outlook of this business for the second half

items.statement: Wealth Management NIMs up marginally due to ~40 bps cost of funds reduction in last 6 months and improved MTF yields
items.quote: The NIMs have marginally gone up because our cost of funds has come down incrementally in last 6 months by almost around 40 basis points. Also, yields have improved marginally on our MTF book because it is a diversified book across retail and HNI segment.

items.statement: Housing Finance yield moderation due to retail housing loan mix increase (yields lower than LAP/construction finance)
items.quote: the overall yield is lower because we are increasing the retail housing book mix. If you look at our numbers on a YoY basis and QoQ basis, our retail housing loan book has gone up YoY by almost about 82% and that is resulting in the overall mix tilted towards the retail home loans where the yields are marginally lower than the segments of LAP and construction finance.

items.statement: AMC October gross sales and net flows meaningfully higher than September quarter; strong growth across all channels
items.quote: Importantly, October has been a record month again in all the channels and in terms of the overall sales.

items.statement: Alternates monthly gross sales near Rs 1,000 cr in October alone
items.quote: In alternates, we should be at nearly Rs. 1,000 cr monthly gross sales for the month of October alone.

items.statement: Wealth Management revenue split 50-50 direct vs external broking; profit mix 60% from indirect segment
items.quote: In the Wealth Management segment, revenue-wise, both are equal. The direct broking and the external wealth management segment , we are almost 50-50. In terms of the profit mix, the indirect segment would be almost about 60%.

items.statement: Housing Finance book 78% housing loans, 9% LAP, 13% construction finance; fully secured
items.quote: Overall, from the mix perspective, 78% of the book is housing loans, 9% of the book is LAP an d almost 13% of the book is construction finance in entire secured book

items.statement: F&O volumes may moderate from 20 Nov due to regulatory changes reducing expiries, especially Bank Nifty
items.quote: There could be a bit of moderation, which could happen as far as the F&O volumes are concerned, given that the new regulat ory changes, which are going to come into effect from 20th of November because of the reduction of the expiries, especially Bank Nifty

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance Rs. 260-280 crore consolidated; Q3 Rs. 68-72 crore, Q4 Rs. 80 crore
items.quote: Based on the current order inflow and the strong demand outlook, we reiterate our revenue guidance for FY25 targeting around Rs. 260 to Rs. 280 crore s with Quarter 3, at around Rs. 68 to Rs. 72 crore s and Quarter 4 will be at around Rs. 80 crores

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expected 14-15% average
items.quote: This year the total turnover what we are expecting is in the range of Rs. 260 to 280 crore s on a consolidated basis with an average margin of EBITDA of 14% to 15

items.statement: India operations next 6 months revenue Rs. 42-45 crore at 14-15% EBITDA
items.quote: The India operation now in the next six months would be Rs. 42 crores to Rs. 45 crores and EBITDA level of around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: UAE order book 40 million Dirham; India project Rs. 25 crore over 5-6 months, daily bookings Rs. 25-30 lakh
items.quote: In the UAE our current order book stands to 40 million D irham with the order coming from the UAE and other GCC countries including Africa. In India we have a project worth of around Rs. 25 crore s that will be executed over the next 5 -6 months, and we are currently seeing daily booking of around 25 to 30 lakhs per day

items.statement: No UAE capex planned yet; evaluating expansion next quarter based on demand and new markets
items.quote: Right now, no. We are planning. We will plan in the next quarter that what kind of expansion is required in UAE looking to the demand. But as on today we have not planned yet.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 13.96%; Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 14%; expect ~1% improvement in current quarter
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margin improvement in the current quarter by around 1%.

items.statement: Bulletproof glass in testing at UAE plant; market launch by December/January after UAE Defense and Netherlands testing
items.quote: Particularly on the bulletproof right now we started seeding the market, approaching the customer. At the same time our sample is getting ready for the UAE Defense for first round of testing. And most probably by November end we will get the result from UAE and then it will go to Netherland for further testing and by December end that test will be completed. Most probably in January we will be in

items.statement: GCC war may delay some project dispatches 3-4 months; no impact expected next financial year
items.quote: No, we don't see any slowdown as on today. But yes because of war, certain orders, which are in pipeline, maybe some of the project, can get delay for 3 to 4 months which will impact our supply.

items.statement: Targeting 30+ GW capacity by FY30 with debt-light strategy funded by internal cash flows
items.quote: Our diverse capabilities and financial resilience provide a solid foundation for growth in our quest to reach 30+ GW of capacity by FY30. Our existing operations will generate sufficient cash flow s to enable us to reach our targets without excessive

items.statement: Capex estimate INR 6,000 crores for FY25 and INR 20,000 crores for FY26 for ongoing projects and organic expansion
items.quote: For this year, we are expecting that apart from the already concluded acquisitions, considering our own internal benchmark for further acquisitions as well as our ongoing project and further organic expansion, it will be near about INR 6,000 crores. And for next year, we are expecting that for the same projects, it will be around INR 20,000 crores.

items.statement: Received Letter of Award for 1,496 MW supply to Maharashtra DISCOM under 25-year PPA from new 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical plant in Chhattisgarh
items.quote: We have also received a Letter of Award from the Maharashtra DISCOM for the supply of 1,496 MW power on a net basis under a 25 -year Power Supply Agreement. This power will be supplied from a new 1,600 MW Ultra-Supercritical Thermal Power Project to be set up in Chhattisgarh.

items.statement: Long-term tie-ups for 3 GW capacity out of targeted 12.5 GW organic capacity addition
items.quote: With this, we now have long-term tie-ups for 3 GW capacity out of our targeted organic capacity addition of 12.5

items.statement: Advance orders placed for 11.2 GW BTG equipment with BHEL for phase-wise commissioning by FY30
items.quote: We have given advance orders to the Main Plant Supplier for 11.2 gigawatt of capacity, which will be commissioned in a phase-wise manner by FY30.

items.statement: Continuing EBITDA grew 38.3% YoY to INR 11,692 crores in H1 FY25 and 24.6% YoY to INR 5,402 crores in Q2 FY25 due to higher revenues and lower fuel and operating costs
items.quote: Our Continuing EBITDA for H1 FY25 grew by 38.3% to INR 11,692 crores, up from INR 8,457 crores in H1 FY 24. Similarly, Continuing EBITDA for Q2 FY25 grew by 24.6% to INR 5,402 crores, up from INR 4,336 crores in Q2 FY24.

items.statement: Merchant volume sold in Q2 FY25 was 4,886 million units at average realization of INR 6 per unit
items.quote: So, merchant volume we sold this time is 4,886 million units. And the realization is almost INR 6 per unit.

items.statement: Peak power demand reached 249 GW, government estimates 296 GW by FY27 and 388 GW by FY32; thermal capacity addition target raised to 80 GW by FY32
items.quote: Peak power demand, which was 203 GW in FY '22, is already at 249 GW now. The government estimates that it will reach 296 GW by FY '27 and 388 GW by FY '32. This has prompted the government to raise its targeted thermal power capacity addition requirement to 80 GW by FY32.

items.statement: Acquired 2,300 MW capacity (500 MW Dahanu, 600 MW Lanco Amarkantak, 1,200 MW Coastal Energen) taking operational capacity to 17,550 MW
items.quote: We have recently acquired and added 2,300 MW of capacity, taking our operational capacity to 17,550 MW at the end of September 2024. These additions include 500 MW from Adani Dahanu Thermal Power Station, 600 MW from Lanco Amarkantak Power Limited and 1,200 MW from Coastal Energen Private Limited.

items.statement: Debt per MW reduced significantly; CARE Ratings assigned AA/Stable rating in August 2024; finance costs lower at INR 1,618 crores in H1 FY25 vs INR 1,772 crores in H1 FY24
items.quote: We have utilized the proceeds for regulatory recovery judiciously to deleverage and to fund capex. As a result, the debt per megawatt has come down significantly, and our credit rating has improved further. In this quarter, CARE ratings had assigned AA/Stable rating to APL's debt facilities in August 2024.

items.statement: Lanco Amarkantak (Korba Power) has INR 1,800 crores debt on balance sheet; Coastal Energen acquisition cost INR 3,336 crores paid from accruals
items.quote: Now, actually, we have taken some debt on the balance sheet of Korba Power. So, we have INR 1,800 crores of debt over there. The other amount that Mr. Jha quoted was actually paid from our accruals. So, the total addition of debt rather is only INR 1,800 crores.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue guidance to INR 1,250-1,275 crores, implying 25-27.5% growth; margins to grow 2-3% faster than sales
items.quote: We are pleased to revise our top-line guidance for this financial year from INR 1,200 crores to INR 1,250-1,275 crores which will result in an overall growth of 25% to 27.5% compared to the previous year. Margins will grow faster than sales due to operational leverage. Margin growth will be around 2% to 3% more than the sales growth.

items.statement: FY26 top-line growth expected to exceed previous 17-18% CAGR guidance; firm guidance in February
items.quote: FY'26, we have not yet given the initial guidance. We will give the guidance in February, but tentatively in earlier calls we have given 17% to 18% top line growth as being the compounded growth. I think we will definitely exceed that.

items.statement: Manufacturing order book at INR 12.34 billion: regular INR 8.33B, railway INR 3.7B, spares INR 0.14B, Turkey INR 0.17B; exports 71% excluding railways
items.quote: The order book for manufacturing segment is Rs. 12.34 billion, regular manufacturing business is Rs. 8.33 billion, Rs. 3.7 billion in the railway business, spares and aftermarket is Rs. 0.14 billion and Rs. 0.17 billion in the Turkey business. Export and deemed export constitutes about 71% of the order book excluding the railways.

items.statement: Q2 order inflow INR 3.6 billion, highest ever; up 41% YoY and 33% H1 YoY; H1 total INR 6.58B vs INR 4.93B prior year
items.quote: The order inflow for the quarter is INR 3.6 billion. This is the highest ever order booking in the history of the company. Order inflow has increased 41% on a Q2 to Q2 comparison basis and 33% over H1 -to-H1 comparison basis. The H1 order inflow total for the c urrent year is INR 6.58 billion versus the previous year INR 4.93 billion

items.statement: Domestic market flat Q2 YoY, reversing Q1 shrinkage; factoring 3-4% growth for FY26; two large railway tenders expected soon, revenue from FY27
items.quote: Overall, we are factoring 3% to 4% growth on domestic market for the next year, that is FY'26. We are expecting new tenders, four railways and we are certain to see two large tenders in the upcoming months. However, business for these railways tenders will be realized only in FY'27.

items.statement: Export order inflow doubled to INR 4.78B in H1 (73% of total); strong across gas turbines, gas engines, motors, hydro, traction; driven by data centers, fracking, grid stabilization, Ukraine
items.quote: Order inflow from direct and deemed exports for the first half is INR 4.78 billion compared to INR 2.36 billion in the previous year, which is more than double. Exports and deemed exports order inflow is 73% of the total order inflow.

items.statement: Geothermal order won: 3x43 MW US phase-I; same customer targeting 1,000 MW phase-II with PPAs signed with major IT companies; better margins than hydro
items.quote: Geothermal plants is another area of huge growth potential. We have received an order this year for 3x43 MW for a large geothermal power plant in the US for phase-I. Now, the same company is in the market for 1,000 MW in phase-II. We have signed PPAs with major IT companies and have indicated a 1,000 MW a year demand.

items.statement: Traction motor: 5-year contract signed with major international co; another contract under negotiation, expected announcement by end of Q3 or Q4; Indian Railways qualification expected next year, volumes FY27
items.quote: As announced, TDPS has signed a five-year contract for the supply of traction motors to a major international company. There's another such contract under negotiation in which TDPS is very well placed and we hope to announce this order early by the end of this quarter, Q3 or definitely in Q4.

items.statement: Motor business targeting INR 80 crores FY25, INR 160 crores FY26; further big increase expected FY27; export-focused with Middle East and India pipeline
items.quote: In the motor business, we are on track to achieve the numbers that we have indicated earlier. We have a plan of INR 80 crores this year and INR 160 crores next year. Once again, the markets are mainly exports and we see a big pipeline of orders from the Middle East and India.

items.statement: Traction motor export order: INR 18 crores trial order Apr-May 2025, then INR 20 crores FY26, INR 60-70 crores/year FY27 onward for 5 years; second similar contract close to signing
items.quote: We have mentioned INR 18 crores as the first trial order in April or May next year, and then they'll be sent for qualification and then we'll ramp up to start somewhere around Q2 or even Q3 next year and we are lookin g at something like INR 60-70 crores per year business for around five years

items.statement: Waste-to-energy orders from Japan and Singapore (Google data center); data center backup power enquiries in India but market immature, mostly diesel 1-2MW not core area
items.quote: These are the same waste to energy power plants. Basically, now we have got one order from Singapore for a waste to energy plant. This is also mainly for a data center which is being put up by Google. There are many such power plants are going to come in the market because everybody is moving towards carbon net zero.

items.statement: Aftermarket growing 20-25%; winning orders to replace competitor machines (BHEL, Chinese) in India and abroad; executing 3-machine hydro refurbishment
items.quote: If you see, our aftermarket business is also growing at 20% to 25% and recently we have got some very good orders outside India for replacing our competitors machines that we do on regular basis and there are very good number of enquiries, we have already participated in the tenders, there are some government jobs, one big hydro project we are now executing, there are three machines in that projec

items.statement: FY25 sales volume target 4.4-4.5 lakh tons with 25-30% annual growth
items.quote: we will easily able to reach our aforementioned target of reaching 4.4 lakh tons to 4.5 lakh tons range for the year ending. Furthermore, as next year progresses, our DFT, as we mentioned, will be up and running by the end of this quarter. Therefore, as the volumes increase, the numbers will also increase , and the volumes in the next financial year will improve.

items.statement: FY26 sales volume growth target 25-30% year-on-year
items.quote: our yearly target to achieve a 25%-30% growth every year in volumes is still on target.

items.statement: FY25 value-added product target 40% of sales mix
items.quote: our year-ending target for the VAP is 40%, and as the DFT will commence, as I mentioned, by the end of this quarter, the produce from DFT is entirely value added.

items.statement: FY26 value-added product target 45% of sales mix
items.quote: The product mix will be as such: the VAP products will be 45% for the next year and 55% will be general products.

items.statement: Long-term VAP target 50-55% at 2 million ton capacity by 2027
items.quote: My target for VAP is 50% once the full capacity install of 2 million tons. On that production, the target is to have a 50% mix of VAP and the remaining general products.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex expected Rs. 140-150 crores, may stretch to Rs. 200 crores
items.quote: Around Rs. 140 crores-Rs. 150 crores is something that is expected. It can further stretch up to Rs. 200 crores as well.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex expected Rs. 250-300 crores
items.quote: So, if we add up the Rs. 90 odd Cr. this year, it could be around Rs. 250 Cr. to Rs. 300 Cr for the full year, right? Pranav Singla: Yes, that's right

items.statement: Good export order book for H2 FY25
items.quote: You can expect another all-time high export in H2, given that our DFT will start as well and our galvanizing has already anyway started. So, our exports can have a good increase from what we have. And we have a good order book as well for exports.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 inventory loss Rs. 900-930 per ton
items.quote: Inventory loss was to the tune of Rs. 900 to Rs. 930 this quarter. Sneha Talreja: Per ton

items.statement: Current EBITDA per ton 4,200-4,300, expect 4,500+ next quarter
items.quote: we were already at the 4,200-4,300 mark. We expect these things to normalize in the coming quarter, and we'll be able to maintain a healthy EBITDA per ton.

items.statement: DFT product EBITDA per ton Rs. 7,000-8,000+
items.quote: that product will be having an EBITDA per ton of Rs. 7,000-Rs. 8,000 plus. So, given that calculation, you can see maybe a 10% increase in the total EBITDA per ton in Q4.

items.statement: Primary/secondary mix shifting from 50-50 to 80-20 primary
items.quote: our major expansion is happening in primary segment. So, what primary and secondary is 50%-50% right now; it will eventually be 20% secondary and the remaining will be the primary use.

items.statement: SKU count increasing from 1,200 to 2,000 with DFT and Raipur expansion
items.quote: I have close to 1200 SKUs right now. With the added capacity today and with the added DFT line, which will be added by the end of this quarter, I will be having 2000 SKUs.

items.statement: October realizations showing upward shift
items.quote: For the month of October, we have seen a further upward shift in realisation.

items.statement: Steel demand bottomed out, expecting government orders and export growth
items.quote: We don't see any further correction happening as of now. I think the market has bottomed out. The demand should be picking up. We should be expecting government orders coming in soon as well.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 disbursement target of INR 350 crore and AUM target of around INR 750 crore
items.quote: We have a disbursement target of INR 350 crore for the full year, ending in March.

items.statement: FY26 disbursement target of INR 400-450 crore with AUM crossing INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: Next year our disbursement target is around INR 400 crore, INR450 crore. Hence our AUM will cross INR 1,000 crore.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR 50 crore equity by March FY25 to fund branch expansion to 100 branches
items.quote: Sir, we plan to raise an additional INR 50 crores by March, as we need funds to open new branches next year.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 85 branches with 23 new branches opened in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The total number of branches is now 85, which was 62 in the last quarter 2 FY24. We have opened 23 new branches.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to reduce from ~65% to 60% as new branches mature
items.quote: So as soon as this branch starts working our costing will reduce by around 4% to 5%, when the branch comes into our system. I can give an estimate but our cost-to-income ratio will become 60%.

items.statement: All loans are fixed rate; repo rate cuts would immediately increase profit without passing benefit to borrowers
items.quote: Look sir, the first question was, if our repo rate is cut, all our loans, all of them are fixed rate loans. If the rate is cut, then our profit will increase immediately. We won't have to serve it anywhere else.

items.statement: NHB guidelines require 70% housing loan mix, reducing LAP focus and slowing disbursements temporarily
items.quote: We used to get 2%, 3% extra money in the LAP, so now we will have to cut the rates a bit in housing loan, so if borrowing rate will cut down, we will benefit there and we will be able to do better business.

items.statement: Housing loans at 71% of book, LAP at 29%; salaried 26%, self-employed 74%
items.quote: Housing loan has increased to 71% and loan against property is at 29% and salaried loan has been 26% and self -employed loan is 74%.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 1.96% from 2.40% YoY; net NPA at 0.59%; 100% book secured with property at 40% avg LTV
items.quote: Gross NPA is 1.96% which was 2.40% in Q2FY24. Net NPA is 0.59% as against 0.56% in the previous quarter 2 FY24.

items.statement: Raised INR 50 crore in Q2 FY25 (40% banks, 60% FIs); outstanding borrowings INR 542 crore
items.quote: In quarter 2 FY25, we have done a total fundraise of INR 50 crores, in which 40% was taken from bank and the rest from FI.

items.statement: New branches in Maharashtra and South to start contributing from Q3 FY25 after 6-month setup period
items.quote: It was implemented this month, in November, and we will see the impact in the next quarter.

items.statement: Target turnaround time of 10 days for loan processing; can extend to 45 days in states with registered mortgages
items.quote: Shivan ji, our targeted turnaround time (TAT) is 10 days. However, the TAT can vary depending on the involvement of physical property documents.

items.statement: EMI-to-income ratio for rural customers at 50-60% minimum (INR 15,000 on INR 30,000 income)
5-year vision: business could grow 5x from current levels as pan-India team scales
items.quote: What I see in the next 5 years, if my business grows 5 times from here, then it will not be an

items.statement: Expect demand and margins to see slight uptick in current quarter and trend going forward with festivities
items.quote: Demand and margins both are seeing a slight uptick in current quarter and we believe that it would be a trend going forward with the festivities kicking in.

items.statement: Expect cotton prices to stay at current levels or slightly lower for longer period
items.quote: We believe that cotton prices are going to stay at these levels or slightly lower going forward. We are here with low cotton prices I think for a longer period of time.

items.statement: Expect cotton prices in range of INR53,000 to INR57,000 per candy for foreseeable future
items.quote: And we expect the prices to stay in the range of INR53,000 to INR57,000 for the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Expect to be back at 97% utilization in current quarter after 94% in Q2
items.quote: But most of that is over and we expect to be back at 97% utilization in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect export volumes around 100,000 tons per month for next quarter average
items.quote: As a country, we exported about 100,000 tons in September, the latest month which went by. And we expect this number to be there and thereabouts for the next quarter average.

items.statement: Proposed investment of INR12 crores for 26% equity in Evincea Renewables SPV for 40 MW solar plant
items.quote: We have also proposed an investment of 26% of equity share capital in M/S Evincea Renewables Pvt Ltd. It's a special purpose vehicle for a cash consideration of INR12 crores.

items.statement: Looking at expansion opportunities in spinning business aggressively, announcement expected in couple of months
items.quote: So, hopefully, in the next couple of months, we will be announcing some expansion in our spinning business.

items.statement: Gross profit margin expanded 263 bps Y-o-Y to 21.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Gross profit margin expanded by 263 basis points Y-o-Y. Gross margin for the quarter stood at 21.4%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 257 bps Y-o-Y to 10.2% in H1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by about 257 basis Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Merged entities operating at 12-13% EBITDA, expected to go higher after re-engineering
items.quote: So, they are already operating at 12%-13% EBITDA level, which I think will go further up once we re-engineer the capacity.

items.statement: Expect marginal EBITDA accretion of 1-2% for whole company from merged entities
items.quote: So, we expect a bump up of around 1% to 2%. So, it's really very early for me to comment on these. But we expect marginal accretion for the whole company, definitely.

items.statement: In-principle approval for amalgamation of Sobhagia Sales (garments) and Marvel Dyers (dyeing/printing) for forward integration
items.quote: An important strategic update for the company is the in-principle approval for amalgamation of manufacturing facilities of the group company Sobhagia Sales and Marvel Dyers & Processors with the company.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA stable with marginal 0.2% increase to INR145 crores; India Security EBITDA 5.5%, FM EBITDA 4.3% (up 30 bps YoY), International Security EBITDA 3.3% (down from 3.4% QoQ)
items.quote: So on a consol basis, the EBITDA was stable with a very marginal increase of 0.2% to INR145 crores. India Security reported an EBITDA of 5.5%. Facility Management reported an EBITDA of 4.3%, which is 30 basis points higher Y-o-Y.

items.statement: International Security EBITDA impacted by 3.75% Fair Work Australia minimum wage revision effective July 1; full price increase effect visible Q4 onwards
items.quote: EBITDA was marginally impacted because of 3.75% minimum grade revision by Fair Works, Australia, which has gone effective 1 st of July. So generally, all price increases are implemented by Q3 with the full quarter effect which will be visible Q4

items.statement: India Security margin target 6%+ (pre-COVID level), currently 5.8% standalone; FM margin target 6%+ (pre-COVID), currently ~4.5%, confident of reaching ~5% by year-end
items.quote: We are very confident that we can get back to that 6% pre-COVID level for Security and FM in India. It has taken a little bit more time than one would have liked. But fundamentally, there is nothing that has changed the margin profile of the business overall.

items.statement: India Security monthly billing up 3.5% QoQ, FM monthly revenue up 4.3% QoQ; expecting mid-double-digit organic growth for Indian businesses on current trajectory
items.quote: If you look at our monthly revenues or monthly billing, in just the security solutions part of India, compared to April to June period in Q2, 3.5% increase. In Facility Management al so compared to previous quarter, 4.3% increase in monthly revenue. So I think we are looking at a mid-double-digit type organic growth from the Indian businesses basis this current trajectory

items.statement: No formal guidance policy; historical 15.8% revenue CAGR and 15% EBITDA CAGR since listing; current trajectory suggests similar growth this year
items.quote: I think SIS has never done guidance. We don't do that as a matter of policy. But I'll tell you what, if you look at the earnings note, since our listing, we do a revenue CAGR report and EBITDA CAGR report. So since our listing in Q2 of FY '18, we have maintained a 15.8% revenue CAGR and EBITDA growth CAGR of the last 8 years, quarter-on-quarter is 15%.

items.statement: Australian wage hike effective July 1 creates temporary margin compression; price catch-up mostly by December (end Q3), full effect Q4; no customer loss expected
items.quote: This takes anywhere between 3 to 6 months. And mostly by the month of December, all the price changes come through, which is the end of Q3. So this is not an unusual event. This is a routine practice. This has no bearing on long-term profitability or margin profile or continuity of clients.

items.statement: International operations have close to $100 million work orders to execute mostly in Q4; Indian business has good order line-up for Q3
items.quote: Our international operations have in hand close to $100 million worth of work orders to be executed in Q4 mostly. Our Indian business also has a very good line-up of orders for Q3.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR166 crores to INR857 crores; net debt-to-EBITDA down to 1.47 from 1.76; OCF/EBITDA 167%; DSO improved 4 days to 70 days
items.quote: Overall, we're very happy to report that net debt is down by INR166 crores. Now net debt is INR857 crores, which was at INR1,223 crores at end of the last quarter. This brings the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio down to 1.47, which was 1.76 in the last quarter.

items.statement: VProtect contributes INR10 crores of ~INR450 crores India Security revenue at 19% EBITDA margin; too small to move needle currently
items.quote: So the India Security business consolidated revenue would be close to INR450 crores or thereabouts. And the VProtect business contributes INR10 crores out of the INR450 crores. In terms of EBITDA margin, the EBITDA margin of the INR10 crores is 19%.

items.statement: Target ROE/ROCE >15% by end FY25, back to pre-COVID 20% over next 2 years via working capital release and goodwill charge reduction
items.quote: And our return on equity and return on capital employed will move ahead of 15%, hopefully, at the end of this financial year. Our objective will be to take it back to the pre-COVID level of 20% over the next 2 financial years.

items.statement: No immediate M&A plans; M&A limited to strategic reasons (~10% of growth); focused on organic growth, margin improvement, working capital
items.quote: Not in the immediate month or so. I think M&A is a part of our growth strategy. If you look at SIS's performance over the last 8 years of listing, you will see that we have always been a very organic growth-oriented company. M&A is limited. And even when it happens, it may be contribute to 10% of the overall growth.

items.statement: Indian Security industry growing ~1.5x GDP (down from 2x pre-COVID) due to muted minimum wage revisions; price growth component subdued
items.quote: the Indian Security industry is growing at ballpark 1.5x GDP. Obviously, GDP growth plus some price change. Over the last two years, especially since COVID, the price growth has been a little muted because the minimum wage revisions have been muted

items.statement: FM gross margins intact at ~10%+; SG&A cuts done; low-margin contracts (3-year with penalties) rolling off by March 31 will naturally lift gross and EBITDA margins
items.quote: The gross margin is intact because the blended average gross margin is in the same range of around 12% for Security, 12% to 13% for Security and for FM around 10% plus as it was before. SG&A cuts have happened. Now some of the contracts which are actua lly yielding lower than average margin, which are actually a drag on the gross margin line, those we haven't been able to step out of because the c

items.statement: Singapore acquisition annualized revenue grown from $30M to ~$50M; profitable, breakeven, $20M+ cash reserves; self-sufficient but small vs $1.5B group
items.quote: Singapore acquisition is performing better than ever before. The business is growing. The annualized revenue is moving from $30 million a year range to close to $50 million a year range over the last year. Profitability also is stable now. It's a breakeven business. In terms of cash in the bank, it has more than $20 million of cash reserves in the bank, so it is self-sufficient.

items.statement: Indian effective tax rate 0% (80JJAA benefit); Australian tax rate 30% (no equivalent benefit); Indian business 60-65% of profits/revenues
items.quote: So the effective tax rate for Australia is the Aussie tax rate. Yash Darak: Sorry? Rituraj Sinha: 30% that's the Australian tax rate. There is no equivalent of 80JJAA provision in Australian taxation. So the Australian business pays taxes at 30%. Indian business, which is now 60%, 65% of profits and revenues, pays zero effective tax

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement target of 100 basis points per year for next 3 years
items.quote: Our guidance is that we want to improve our EBITDA margin by 100 basis points every year. We've been doing better than that, but we still see juice available for us for the next 3 years to grow.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 12% to 15% for key brands as market improves
items.quote: So they should continue to grow at our guidance of 12% to 15%. Markets are clearly muted, but as the market improves and as the like-to-like improves a little more, I think all these 3 brands which are market leaders will continue to grow.

items.statement: Capex range of INR 90-100 crores annually with asset-light FOFO model
items.quote: We have cited in the past that our capex will be in the range of INR 90 crores to INR 100 crores. And as Shailesh mentioned earlier in the call, we always have an asset-light model.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 19% with 110 bps margin expansion to 13.3% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Q2FY25 saw the highest ever quarterly sales, the highest ever quarterly EBI TDA and the highest ever operating PAT for AFL. NSV in Q2 was INR1,273 crores backed by accelerating store expansion and healthy retail like -to-like growth of 4.6

items.statement: COGS efficiency of nearly 50 bps offset by channel mix changes, GP stable at 50.4%
items.quote: There was a COGS efficiency in Q2 of nearly 50 basis points, but it was offset by changes in channel mix, for example, higher revenue mix of online business in Q2, resulting in stable GP at 50.4%.

items.statement: Festival season and wedding calendar in H2 expected to continue growth momentum
items.quote: With the ongoing festival season and a strong wedding calendar in H2, we remain hopeful that the growth momentum will continue.

items.statement: Adjacent categories growing faster with U.S. Polo women's wear doubling, kids, footwear, innerwear growing
items.quote: The adjacent categories continue to grow faster with encouraging doubling of business in U.S. Polo women's wear on a small base with continued growth in kids' wear, footwear and innerwear.

items.statement: Wholesale channel growth muted due to market conditions and pruning of low-margin distribution points
items.quote: The growth in wholesale channels was lower because of muted market conditions but mainly due to continuous pruning down of long tail, low-margin distribution points in wholesale network.

items.statement: Priority to fund growth then pay down debt, targeting near-zero debt in 2-3 years
items.quote: And at the current level of the net debt that we have, I think in 2 to 3 years, surely in 3 years, we will sort of se e a point where we'll be either 0 debt or a nearly 0 debt company

items.statement: Digital business grew ~20% with 40% growth in online B2C direct channel
items.quote: Digital business has grown around 20% with fantastic growth of 40% in online B2C direct channel with improved channel margins.

items.statement: Flying Machine online growth >50% in H1 FY25, MBO counters expanding
items.quote: If I talk about quarter 1 and quarter 2 of this financial year, the online growth in FM has been more than 50%. Now, this is an important channel, which we believe will be 30% of our revenue in Flying Machine.

items.statement: Inventory turns >4x, gross working capital stable at ~140 days, net working capital at 60 days
items.value: >4x inventory turns, GWC ~140 days, NWC 60 days
items.quote: Stock turns have stayed healthy at more than 4 turns. While inventory went down by 4 days, the receivables went up slightly due to the fact that Q2 was a billing quarter for festival season. But overall, GWC stayed stable at around 140 days, NWC stable at 60 days.

items.statement: ROCE moving towards 20% mark with healthy reduction in borrowing
items.quote: resulting in healthy reduction in borrowing and movement of ROCE towards 20% mark.

items.statement: Advertising spend increased by 50 bps in Q2 to support premiumization and innovation
items.quote: We increased advertising spend in Q2 by 50 basis points to support our premiumization and innovation drive in order to fuel growth.

items.statement: Committed to 15% CAGR square foot expansion with focus on large format stores and new formats
items.quote: We are committed to this 15% CAGR every year on square foot expansion. And this will only accelerate because we have put a lot more fuel.

items.statement: Management expects domestic revenue growth of 9-10% for full year FY25
items.quote: Probably I would look at about 9% to 10% growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: Management targets full-year EBITDA margin in the 18-20% range for FY25
items.quote: We would think -- would like to believe that our EBITDA level margins should, I think, continue in the same range, 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 capex planned at INR300 crores after receiving environmental clearance
items.quote: Yes, that is what we have planned.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 construction expected to begin in FY26 after finalizing product clusters and board approval
items.quote: So if your question was that whether we'll start construction in 26, the answer will be definitely yes, that would be our endeavor.

items.statement: Export revenue grew significantly in H1 FY25 with South America up 167% and Japan up 122% year-over-year
items.quote: H1 FY '24-25 sales to South America and Japan increased by 167% and 122%, respectively, as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 421 bps YoY to 42.6% in Q2 FY25 driven by new products, export normalization and procurement cost optimization
items.quote: Our gross profit margin expanded by 421 basis points year-over-year to 42.6%, driven by introduction of new products, normalization of export markets to some extent, and which has been impacted by high inventories last year and rigorous cost optimization in procurement.

items.statement: Management believes current margins are sustainable within a range due to strategy on purchases, sales, product positioning and mix improvement
items.quote: We feel that with the kind of strategy that we have taken on both purchases and sales and positioning our products and improving the product mix, we feel that the margins are sustainable within a range.

items.statement: Management is very optimistic about H2 FY25 domestic demand due to high reservoir levels (87% capacity) and soil moisture supporting higher Rabi acreage
items.quote: We are very optimistic about the second season. As I mentioned earlier, there is enough water, and there is even a lot of moisture in the soil, which is very conducive for the second crop.

items.statement: Export demand outlook for next 12 months is optimistic with volume growth expected though prices may decline slightly
items.quote: The inventory situation is easing out in those markets, and we expect to continue the volume growth. Of course, price may not grow, probably may take a slight beating also. But overall, it looks optimistic, I would say.

items.statement: Domestic prices declined 10-15% on average in H1 FY25 but no further price drop expected in H2; all price declines factored in
items.quote: Yes, that is true. Yes. That is what our Managing Director also commented at the beginning in his opening comments or during the question and answer. Yes, all are factored in, and we don't expect any further price drop in the second half.

items.statement: New products launched in last 2-3 years contribute 8-9% of revenue in current year, up from 3-4% last year
items.quote: And these products are contributing something between 8% t0 9% of our revenue in the current year

items.statement: Six new products launched in H1 FY25 including Portion, Ormie, Meshi, Yunico (2 formulations) and Tribasic Copper (2 brands)
items.quote: We have launched this Portion. I mean it's there in the, I think, investor presentation. Portion, Ormie we launched. These are the 2 products that we launched. And towards the end of last year, we launched Tribasic Copper in the name of 2 brands. And also this year, we launched insecticide Yunico in 2 different formulations. So about 6 products we launched in H1.

items.statement: Cotton acreage decline in North India (nearly 40%) due to pink bollworm infestation and low commodity prices may not bounce back
items.quote: In north, I don' really see north cotton bouncing back. The area continues to decline, or maybe at the current year level.

items.statement: China excess capacity continues to supply market but company pursues premium positioning strategy to counter
items.quote: Yes. I mean I think that what's happening in China, only the Chinese would know. But really, whatever we understand is that there has been excess capacity, and they are continuing to supply to the market depending on the situation.

items.statement: Barrix acquisition expected to achieve significant growth and good profitability on standalone basis in FY25 but not material to consolidated SCIL numbers for next 2-3 years
items.quote: So by end of this year, we believe that as a stand-alone entity, Barrix would have completed this year with a significant growth over last year with good profitability levels and much higher the profitability level would also be at a very, very decent level. But in the overall numbers of SCIL, they will not be material for the next 2 or 3 years.

name: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd

items.statement: Full-year cost-to-income guidance maintained at 55% range
items.quote: We have given a guidance, which is where we always ask to look at the full year opex number, cost-to-income number instead of looking at it quarter-on-quarter which we said will be in that 55% range.

items.statement: Spend growth guidance 20-23% YoY, asset growth 17-20% annualized
items.quote: We had, in earlier calls also stated, that we should look at the spend growth at anywhere between 20% to 23% on a year-on-year basis going further and asset growth of around close to 17% to 20% on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Interest-bearing assets expected to grow 15-19% in line with overall asset growth
items.quote: So, we see that the interest-bearing assets would also grow probably between 15% to 19% in line.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 7.4%, peaked out and will decline when rate easing cycle begins
items.quote: Cost of funds is stable at 7.4%. In our assessment at this stage, the Cost of funds has peaked out and will start coming down once interest rate easing cycle begins.

items.statement: Gross NPAs increased to 3.27% from 3.06% in Q1 FY25; gross credit cost rose to 9% from 8.5%
items.quote: The gross NPAs have increased to 3.27% from 3.06% in Q1 FY '25. Gross credit cost for the current quarter has increased to 9% from 8.5% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain elevated around current levels for next 1-2 quarters, improvement expected end of year onwards
items.quote: We have stated that, we expect it to remain elevated around these levels. But then simultaneously, we have also stated that there are other indicators that help us in estimating that there will be some downward gradient in times to come.

items.statement: Early delinquency flows improved over last six months; prime and above prime share in new acquisitions improved ~15% over 15 months
items.quote: We are seeing a drop in early delinquency of new acquisitions. In addition, the proportion of prime and above prime customers in our new acquisition has improved by ~15% over the last 15 months.

items.statement: Revolver share stabilized at 23-25% range for foreseeable 2-3 quarters; absolute revolver balance continues to increase
items.quote: It should continue to be in that range at least for a foreseeable two to three quarters. What we are also seeing is that on absolute amount, the revolver balance has continued to increase.

items.statement: Retail spends grew 24% YoY to ₹76,398 crore; total card spends up 3% YoY to ₹81,893 crore
items.quote: Retail spends witnessed strong growth and reached ₹ 76,398 crore with a 24% YoY growth. Total card spends stand at ₹ 81,893 crore, with around 3% YoY growth.

items.statement: Cards-in-force at 1.96 crore with 10% YoY growth; new account acquisition at over 9 lakhs in Q2
items.quote: Our cards-in-force (CIF) stand at 1.96 crore, with 10% YoY growth. New account acquisition during Q2 is at over 9 lakhs.

items.statement: Banca channel share temporarily at 41%, expected to return to standard 55% mix as new underwriting model implemented
items.quote: We should see the mix coming back to our standard mix of around 55 from Banca and 45 from open sourcing.

items.statement: RuPay card spends at UPI terminals grew 40% QoQ; Tier II+ customers driving adoption
items.quote: RuPay card spends at UPI terminals continues to grow and have shown a growth of 40% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Reduced credit limits for around 10 lakh customers in H1 FY25 as part of portfolio management
items.quote: So, in this half of the financial year, we've actually reduced limits for around 10 lakh customers and total limits of course, going down.

items.statement: Capital Adequacy Ratio at 22%+, Liquidity Coverage Ratio at 108% vs 85% requirement
items.quote: Our Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is at 22%+ Our Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) is at 108% vs statutory requirement of 85%.

items.statement: Order backlog reached a record high of Rs 8,910 crores, providing revenue visibility for approximately 26 months.
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, the order backlog stood at a record high of Rs.8,910 crores, providing revenue visibility for the coming several quarters.

items.statement: Management reiterated previous guidance of achieving double-digit margins by end of the fiscal year with no change to the plan.
items.quote: No, at this point in time, no change in the in our plan of action. So, what we said previously stays.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin improved to 8.1% in Q2 FY25, driven by favorable mix and operational efficiency.
items.quote: Operational EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.126.3 crores, resulting in a margin of 8.1%, reiterating our continuous efforts towards improving margins and enhancing overall operational efficiency.

items.statement: Expansion work started at Maneja for transformer and interrupter facilities to strengthen manufacturing infrastructure.
items.quote: This included starting expansion work of our transformers and interrupter facilities in Maneja to strengthen our manufacturing infrastructure.

items.statement: Data center segment grew 346% YoY and renewable segment grew 135% YoY in Q2 FY25, driving strong order inflow.
items.quote: To provide more color, this quarter, data center segment emerged as a high-growth segment with a year-on-year growth of 346%, followed by renewable which is up by 135% year-on-year.

items.statement: More than 60% of contracts have price escalation clauses to mitigate CRGO price fluctuations; supply secured via global frame agreements.
items.quote: More than 60% of our contracts, we have price escalation clauses.

items.statement: Exports accounted for 22% of total orders in Q2 FY25, with significant share from high-voltage products and grid integration orders from Europe and Africa.
items.quote: On the right-hand side of Slide, you see that exports accounted for 22% of total orders booked in Q2 FY '25, the significant share from a high-voltage products and grid integration orders from European and African market.

items.statement: TSA agreement with ABB for IT services will conclude by December next quarter; IT costs expected to hover around 2.7%-3% range.
items.quote: We believe that the IT cost that is factored in this particular it will be in the same range. So, that is the overall setup. So, the TSA agreement finally the last leg of the agreement will be coming out of that by December next quarter.

items.statement: Related party orders from parent entities contributed approximately Rs 300 crores in H1 FY25 out of Rs 1,200 crores approved; larger contribution expected in H2.
items.quote: So, ballpark number, you can say Rs.300 crore. The Switzerland you talk about, the approval that we are taking is around Rs.1200 crores and the ballpark till 30th September is around 300+ crore roughly.

items.statement: At least one of the two remaining HVDC tenders (besides Khavda) is expected to be finalized in FY25.
items.quote: I think our view is that at least one, if not two at least one for sure, it will get finalized in this financial year.

items.statement: Leh-Ladakh HVDC bid not yet submitted; discussions ongoing on suitability.
items.quote: Leh Ladakh the bid is not submitted yet. There again discussions are going on what will be suitability, etc., all those things so not submitted answer to that.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in Q2 due to timing mismatch between collections and higher payouts for large HVDC project; borrowings increased by Rs 45 crores.
items.quote: In this particular quarter I would say the collections were good, but the payouts were also on the higher side. And why so, because you are aware that we are running a large HVDC project for which in this particular quarter the payouts were a little bit on the higher side.

items.statement: Other expenses stable at 20.9% of revenue; no one-offs identified; expected to hover around current range.
items.quote: If you see in the current quarter, the other expenses, as I told you from the percentage terms, it has come down rather, which is the 20.9%, right. So, I don't see that there are any other one-offs in this particular other expenses.

items.statement: Service portfolio contributed 12% of total orders in Q2 FY25, driven by industries, renewables, and transportation including restoration and SLAs.
items.quote: For quarter 2, the service portfolio witnessed substantial growth, with contribution of 12% to the total order received, stemming primarily from industries, renewable and transportation, including restoration and service of service-level agreements.

items.statement: Continued investment in manufacturing capacities and workforce up-skilling to capture energy transition opportunities.
items.quote: And last but not the least is continuing to invest in capacities for future growth- capacities for our manufacturing, and workforce.

items.statement: High-speed rail conversations still ongoing and not concluded.
items.quote: It's still ongoing. It's not concluded.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps YoY to 46.9% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA percentage, grew 240 points up on an annual basis, just short of 47%, about 46.9%, but I think, very heartening.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to reach 47.5% by end of FY25, with less than 48% doable
items.quote: Definitely, 47.5% is doable in our mind.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue contribution target of 20% by FY27 maintained, with non-MF growing at mid- to high-20s%
items.quote: we're certainly holding on to do the 20% guidance. Just think of it this way that traditionally, the MF market has grown, our own revenue base would have grown early to mid-teens.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 59.4% YoY vs industry 53.5%, gaining ~100 bps market share to ~66%
items.quote: Equity assets, and this is active equity, which kind of defines the P&L because it's almost upwards of 60% of overall MF revenue contribution, grew almost 60%. So equity assets grew almost 59.4%, much ahead of the rest of the industry of 53.5

items.statement: New SIP registrations hit 1.2 crore in Q2 FY25, with monthly run-rate reaching 45 lakh and targeting 50 lakh
items.quote: INR1.2 crores new SIPs were registered during the quarter. In 1 month, it was INR45 lakh, we are bracing ourselves for shortly for that number to get to INR50 lakhs in some months.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue share was 12.9% of total revenue in Q2 FY25, flat YoY as MF grew faster
items.quote: Share of non -MF revenue, which has hovered around 13%, was 12.9% of overall re venue. I think a good Call(3:45) why it did not expand because MF expanded just ahead of everything else

items.statement: CAMSPay revenue split ~55-60% MF (mostly SIP) and 40-45% non-MF, stable over past year
items.quote: Think of CAMSPay as about a little over 50% of the business accruing from mutual funds. So between 55% to 60%. And the balanced business is non-MF business.

items.statement: CAMS KRA non-MF revenue share rose to ~20% from near zero, MF KRA growing 30-35%
items.quote: what used to be close to 0 has now reached around 20 percentage. So 80% will be MF-based customer and 20% will be non -asset management companies.

items.statement: Opened second GIFT City office, a 50-seater facility, signalling commitment to alternatives business
items.quote: we opened our second office in GIFT city. And again, you would realize we are putting our money where our mouth is. So we opened this office. We had a small office. We now have almost a 50-seater.

items.statement: Alternatives business added 57 new mandates in Q2 FY25, highest quarterly wins, driving 21% YoY revenue growth
items.quote: alternatives came back. We reported som e falloffs last quarter if you're running a business, which is almost a decade and a quarter old, you will have some falloffs. I think this time, 21% year-on-year revenue growth has the highest number of quarterly wins, 57 new

items.statement: Yields stable; AUM-to-fee growth conversion at 84% vs typical 75% thumb rule; management maintains 75% long-term assumption
items.quote: We generally say that the growth of AUM to growth of AUM fee is around 75%. At this time, you had the AUM to fee proportion to be around 84%. So yields have been largely stable.

items.statement: Unified Lending Interface (ULI) could impact Account Aggregator business; management watching closely
items.quote: If the regulatory platform starts doing exactly what commercial areas are doing, then obviously the impact will be there. There's no question about it. But I suggest we just watch it and see how it emerges over a period of time.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 25/share declared (INR 14.5 regular + INR 10.5 special)
items.quote: the CAMS Board has approved an interim dividend of INR25. This INR25 is essentially 2 components. INR14.5 is what traditionally we would have paid for a 65% payout policy. But just given the fact that we've had a strong run overall from an earnings perspective, we did believe, and the Board did believe that it was time to kind of signal to the markets that we want to reward them out.

items.statement: MFCentral JV with KFin approved; currently booking ~INR 1.7 crore quarterly revenue (50-50 split); JV to enhance financial transactions and loan-against-MF
items.quote: In the current quarter, the revenue will be around INR1.7 crores of -- it's 50-50 revenue split between the 2 RPAs. So the revenue is just in the books. Going forward, once the JV is incorporated, this will be handled by the JV company as a 50-50 joint venture.

items.statement: ESOP grant in Q2 FY25 to add ~INR 4 crore incremental cost in FY25 and more in FY26
items.quote: yesterday, there was a grant of e quity of options, the ESOPs that went to employees. So going forward, post, there could be some increase that you will see on the ESOP cost. Incremental cost for the year could be around a little more than INR4 crores

items.statement: Management confident of delivering better than 15% volume growth in H2 FY25 to compensate for H1 and beat industry growth by 17%
items.quote: So as our guidance for the whole year change or we still maintain that and are confident of achieving growth more than 15% in second half to compensate the whole year.

items.statement: Management expects revenue growth better than current 10% for full year FY25
items.quote: We are very confident of better growth than the current 10%.

items.statement: Management targets 260-270 stores by end of FY25, adding ~50 stores in H2
items.quote: Generally, we are able to open between 25 and 30 stores. So assuming for the next 2 quarters, you can safely assume another 50 stores. So we begin in the third quarter, I think 260, 270 stores is where we should end up.

items.statement: Management plans to continue aggressive store expansion at 25-30 stores per quarter for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think the next 2, 3 years, we will be at least at big space, if not accelerate this. We are seeing very good outcome of this channel. And all those things that we wanted to learn, I think the learning, we did enough learning. And so we will continue to be aggressive on opening the stores. And at the time being, we believe that we will continue to we'll expand the stores at about 25, 30 stores ev

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to hover between 11-14% over medium term (3-5 years), definitely hitting 14%
items.quote: So with these 2 both totaling up, so the average number will hover between that 11% to 14%. We believe definitely in the medium term between 3 to 5 years, we'll definitely hit that 14%.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to reach 40% in next 4-6 quarters from current ~38%
items.quote: I don't want to guide you to 42%, 44%, today in the short -- in the next 4 to 6 quarters, you can definitely expect us to deliver 40% if not better than that, but 40% is what you should expect us to deliver.

items.statement: Operating leverage to start reflecting from Q3 FY25, full reflection in 4-6 quarters
items.quote: I think you will start seeing immediately from this quarter, but this is not that it will be the complete stack that we want to do. If you really want to see that, I think you'll have to have patients for the next 4 to 6 quarters. But you will start seeing that operational leverage panning out immediately from this quarter, Q3.

items.statement: Current manufacturing setup can support double current year's revenue with only maintenance capex needed

items.statement: Indian cotton at 1,300 basis points over NY Future (~84-85 US cents/lb), equal to US cotton price but inferior quality; 11% import duty blocks cost arbitrage.
