items.quote: The liraglutide DMF, since you asked that specific question, the DMF was accepted by the FDA and the ANDA, which was filed for liraglutide is under review. We have made significant progress, and especially in the peptides, the key aspect that the FDA looks at is the API and the API efficiency letter or the DMF efficiency letter is clearly a big win for us, where they have accepted the API impuriti

items.statement: Aspart biosimilar opportunity remains for CY25 despite contracting cycle timing due to no other biosimilar competition; Malaysia facility clearance pending
items.quote: But the important piece to remember is that there isn't any other Biosimilar for Aspart at this point in time. So, while it would be true typically for most products where you have options and the payers and PBMs could look for alternatives and they could tie up. Here, it is a very unique situation that would still keep the opportunity available.

items.statement: Stelara biosimilar launch upon approval in EU, Canada, UK per settlement; US launch date already communicated; auto-injector development as needed
items.quote: We've been able to secure a launch upon approval timelines on these countries. So as soon as we secure approval, Jamsheed, we will be looking to bring these products to market. So, I think we've been able to negotiate a very good position, and we have already said what our launch date in the United States is going to be.

items.statement: Bengaluru and Malaysia facilities face US FDA CRLs; VAI classification received for India rHI drug substance site; working collaboratively with FDA to resolve
items.quote: We have responded to all the observations. As you know, we were given an OAI status earlier this year and the inspection was conducted, so we have responded to that and the CAPAs are with them because they came back for an inspection. We will look to get a positive outcome out of that inspection like we have just got a VAI status, which is a positive outcome for the India facility, which makes the

items.statement: Debt reduction priority; multiple levers being explored; action expected before end of fiscal; BBL IPO remains option but timing depends on market and business momentum
items.quote: We have taken measures to restructure the debt, but we would also indicate that we are going to look to reduce it. And we have many levers to explore on that. We are. And I think you can expect to see us act before the end of the fiscal, but we will determine which instrument, which opportunity we use as we progress through the year.

items.statement: Pegfilgrastim market share ticking up as competitor faces supply issues; Biocon well positioned to capture additional share at right price points
items.quote: Yes. Look, we are well positioned. Certainly, as other manufacturers have issues, we are here to supply. And certainly, as they continue to report that they are having these issues. We are getting more and more customers reaching out to us. So Biocon is well positioned and ready to fulfil those orders.

items.statement: Net debt: Group ~USD 1.4 billion; Biocon Biologics USD 1.2 billion as of September
items.quote: The net debt for the group is ~USD 1.4 billion and in Biologics as of September is USD 1.2 billion.

items.statement: Syndicated loan cost currently ~6.75% (SOFR + 175 bps)
items.quote: That is that is about SOFR plus 175 basis points. So, depending upon the average 3 months SOFR, it could vary. But currently, it is around 6.75%.

items.statement: Humira biosimilar high concentration filing part of development plan
items.quote: Yes. So that is something that is certainly a part of our development plan, and we will update as things progress.

items.statement: Semaglutide opportunity USD 40-50 billion; liraglutide USD 3 billion but underserviced; vertically integrated peptide capabilities
items.quote: Of course, there is a huge shift of patients to Semaglutide, which is almost now between USD 40 billion and USD 50 billion opportunity. As far as Lira is concerned, what you see today is not what we believe is the true representative of the demand because it is not fully serviced given the focus has moved to Semaglutide.

items.statement: FY25 capacity addition target revised to 1.8 GW from earlier 2.6 GW
items.quote: We are expecting 1.8-gigawatt this year.

items.statement: FY26 capacity addition target of 6,357 MW and FY27 target of 3,000 MW
items.quote: '24-'25, we are planning to have 1,800 -megawatt almost in '24 -'25; plus '25 -'26, it will be 6,357-megawatt. And '26 -'27, another 3,000 -megawatt will be added

items.statement: FY25 capex revised down to INR 9,000 crore from INR 12,000 crore; FY26 and FY27 capex at INR 12,000-13,000 crore each
items.value: INR 9,000 crore, INR 12,000 crore, INR 12,000-13,000 crore
items.quote: this year, capex against the INR12,000 crore s, we are revising it to INR9,000 crore s for the financial year '24-'25. And next year, we are having a capex of INR12,000 crores. We have -- today itself we have got the budget approved. And similar capex, INR12,000 crore s, INR13,000 crores is expected during '26-'27.

items.statement: 18.6 GW tenders floated and 8.1 GW awarded under REIA mandate
items.quote: Overall, SJVN has floated tender of 18.6-gigawatt and awarded capacity of 8.1-gigawatt till date.

items.statement: Operating portfolio: 2,467 MW (12 projects + 2 transmission lines); Under construction: 1,558 MW hydro, 1,320 MW thermal, 1,958 MW solar
items.quote: So giving a brief of our project as on day 12 of -- 12 projects of 2,467 -megawatt and 2 transmission lines are under operation, 4 hydro projects of 1,558 megawatt, 1 thermal project of 1,320-megawatt and 11 solar projects of 1,958-megawatt are under construction.

items.statement: Quarterly interest cost ~INR 200 crore expected to continue at similar levels
items.quote: Yes, yes, almost it will be a similar number.

items.statement: REIA hybrid tender lowest tariff discovered at INR 3.19/unit vs earlier INR 3.50/unit
items.quote: in case of tender of hybrid today, we have discovered a lowest price of INR319. So if I'll be approaching any of the DISCOMs, they will pick up first INR319 price in place of INR350.

items.statement: Lower Arun 669 MW hydro in Nepal approved at INR 5,792 cr investment; levelized tariff INR 4.99/unit
items.quote: Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs, chaired by Honourable Prime Minister of India, has approved the investment of INR5,792.36 crores for 669-megawatt Lower Arun hydroelectric Project in Nepal. The levelized tariff of the project will be INR4.99 per unit on 28/24.

items.statement: Regulated equity for operational projects (Nathpa Jhakri, Rampur, solar, wind) at INR 7,339 crore
items.quote: Regulated equity is INR7,339 crore s for operational project Nathpa Jhakri, Rampur solar, wind.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 saw fewer tent-pole releases and underperformance of key films, leading to muted advertisement revenue.
items.quote: The combination of fewer tent-pole releases and the underperformance of several key films in the quarter, along with a lack of successful Hindi films in September, resulted in a muted Advertisement revenue for the quarter, contributing a decline of 17% YoY and improvement of 12% on QoQ basis.

items.statement: Management is optimistic about building momentum in upcoming quarters due to a strong release pipeline including Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, Singham Again, Kanguva, Pushpa 2, and Baby John.
items.quote: Looking ahead, although the quarter began on a subdued note with the release of "Vettaiyan", "Jigra" and "Vicky Vidya ka woh wala video", the upcoming release pipeline looks good with releases such as "Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3 ", "Singham Again", "Kanguva", "Pushpa 2", , and "Baby John". We are optimistic about building momentum in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA for Q2 FY25 was Rs. 102 million, down from Rs. 177 million YoY but up from Rs. 66 million QoQ.
items.quote: EBITDA was lower at Rs. 102 million, compared to Rs. 177 million YoY, though it improved from Rs. 66 million in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA was Rs. 168 million compared to Rs. 340 million in H1 FY24, mainly due to lower advertisement revenue.
items.quote: EBITDA for H1FY25 was at RS. 168 Mn, compared to Rs. 340 million in H1FY24, mainly due to lower advertisement revenue.

items.statement: Ad sales team maintained higher price points; decrease in ad revenue was not as steep as drop in volume, strengthening pricing position post-COVID.
items.quote: Although we don't disclose specific pricing details, you can observe that the decrease in ad revenue is not as steep as the drop in volume. This indicates that our ad sales team has been able to sell at higher price points than in previous quarters.

items.statement: Advertisers base decisions on recent cinema performance; weaker Q1 content led to lower ad allocations in Q2, with a lag of at least a quarter for advertisers to re-evaluate the medium.
items.quote: In our business, advertisers often base the ir decisions on recent cinema performance, so weaker content in Q1 generally leads to lower ad allocations in Q2

items.statement: Advertisement screen network grew to 3,735 screens (13% YoY), including 2,122 multiplex and 1,613 single screens, with 432 screens added over the past year.
items.quote: On the screen network front, the advertisement screen network grew to 3,735 scr eens, marking a 13% year -over-year. This includes 2,122 multiplex screens and 1,613 single screens, with the addition of 432 advertisement screens over the past year

items.statement: Network composition shifted significantly toward multiplexes: from 1,565 multiplexes in 2020 to 2,122 currently, improving network quality and supporting better pricing.
items.quote: In 2020, we had 3,792 screens, with 1,565 of those being multiplexes. Today, while our total screen count is slightly lower at 3,735, our multiplex count has increased to 2,122.

items.statement: Ad revenue share with exhibitors increased due to acquisitions of ~400 screens in South with higher minimum guarantees; share dropped from 85% in Q1 to 69% in Q2 and will decline further as revenue per screen rises.
items.quote: These acquisitions came with larger commitments under minimum guarantees, which were higher than our typical sharing rates. To put this into perspective, we added nearly 400 screens to our existing network of 3,600, resulting in a ~12% increase in the overall network.

items.statement: Equipment sales (trading business) reached Rs. 22.5 crore in Q2 FY25 with Rs. 5.7 crore margin; Rs. 17 crore revenue and Rs. 4.7 crore margin from Middle East.
items.quote: On the number front, for this quarter, equipment sales reached ₹22.5 crore, with a margin of ₹5.7 crore. Of this, approximately ₹17 crore in revenue and ₹4.7 crore in direct margin came from the Middle East, significantly contributing to our overall performance.

items.statement: No buyback planned despite strong liquidity; technically not possible due to accumulated losses from earlier periods.
items.quote: However, there are no discussions around a buyback, and technically, it isn’t possible due to accumulated losses. So, even though th ere’s no buyback consideration, our focus is on getting the business back on track

items.statement: Caravan Cinema business fluctuates, peaking around events like elections; expected uptick in coming quarters as winter approaches. Nova Cinemas launched one property in UP, second opening during Diwali.
items.quote: As winter approaches, we expect to see an uptick in this business, particularly in the coming quarters. Now, when it comes to increasing footfall in theatres, we’re focusing on initiatives like Caravan and Nova Cinemas to enga ge audiences in underserved areas and encourage theatre attendance

items.statement: Incremental ad revenue has high flow-through: doubling minutes and pricing could quadruple sales with ~55-60% of incremental revenue converting to PBT (free cash) without mandatory capex.
items.quote: Importantly, this increase would not come with a proportional increase in expenses like sharing. Therefore, around 55-60% of my incremental revenue would directly contribute to profit before tax (PBT). Moreover, there is no mandatory capex required, as we are essentially optimizing our existing network.

items.statement: Management expects ad revenue share percentage to normalize to 40-45% range as revenue per screen approaches Rs. 8-9 lakh; currently at 69% in Q2 down from 85% in Q1.
items.quote: For instance, if revenue per screen is around ₹4.5 lakh, the share could be approximately 60-65%. As we approach higher revenues per screen, closer to ₹8-9 lakh, the share would drop to around 40-45%.

items.statement: Digital cinema advertising is <1% of overall ad spend; sustained content quality needed to regain advertiser mindshare and normalize consumption to 5-7 movies per year.
items.quote: To put it into perspective, digital cinema currently makes up less than 1% of the overall advertising expenditure, So, what that means is 99% of adver tising budgets are already allocated elsewhere

items.statement: Consolidated cash at end of Q2 FY25 was Rs. 998 million; net cash Rs. 409 million after outstanding debt.
items.quote: The consolidated cash at the end of quarter was at Rs. 998 million and the net cash was Rs.409 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of around INR725 crores with EBITDA margin around 21%
items.quote: We expect to achieve revenues of around -- overall revenues for the year for around INR725 crores with a margin around 21% by end of FY '25.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 20% reaching roughly INR860 crores with EBITDA margins closer to mid-20s around 24% +/- 100 bps
items.quote: So for FY '26, we are looking at a growth of 20% with improved EBITDA margins moving forward from there.

items.statement: Current order book at INR940 crores as of end Q2; targeting INR1,400-1,500 crores by end FY25 including Kaiga 5&6 orders
items.quote: So the overall order book as of end of Q2, I think, is around INR940 crores. And the orders that we have won for this quarter is around INR247 crores in all. So that's what it is. And by end of the year, as I mentioned earlier, that we're looking at INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Bloom Energy increased forecast from 3,000 to 4,000 units for calendar year 2025; expects 20% revenue growth in clean energy vertical in FY26
items.quote: We are optimistic about growth in clean energy in FY'26 as Bloom gave an indication for execution of 4,000 units in calendar year 2025 as against an initial indication of 3,000 units. We expect a 20% growth in revenues from this vertical alone in FY'26.

items.statement: Sequential margin improvement expected in H2 FY25 due to operating leverage and batch production ramp-up; targeting mid-20s EBITDA margin by FY26-FY27
items.quote: For FY '26, we are looking at, as I said, closer to mid -20s. That's around 24% plus, minus 100 basis points. That's what we are looking at.

items.statement: New exclusive aerospace facility in Hyderabad to be commissioned by end of December for MNC customers
items.quote: We are establishing a new exclusive aerospace facility by end of December this year. We are doing -- we are taking all the required steps to achieve what we are trying to tell us that's the goal for the company.

items.statement: Roller screws qualified as 100% import substitute; expects INR50-70 crores revenue over next 1-2 years after certification paperwork completes in a month
items.quote: It is pretty much -- over the next one, two years, we are looking at about INR50 crores to INR60 crores or INR70 crores of business coming in from Roller Screws as well.

items.statement: Nuclear sector expects over INR500 crores orders in H2 FY25 from Kaiga 5&6 and reactor refurbishment; FY26 growth of 40-45% backed by robust order book
items.quote: As I said, we're ex pecting more than INR500 crores worth of orders coming in from nuclear in the second half of this year

items.statement: MNC Aerospace expects INR45 crores execution in H2 FY25; projects 45% revenue increase over next 3-4 years with long-term agreements signed with IAI and GKN Aerospace
items.quote: We expect to execute around INR45 crores of orders from MNC aerospace with H2. We estimate a robust growth in this vertical over the next three to four years with 45% revenue increase.

items.statement: Oil & gas vertical: first article order received from Weatherford; expects USD 25-30 million annual orders; volume production from H2 FY26, full revenue in FY27
items.quote: Probably the second half of the year, the overall order book - orders for these products can be between $25 million to $30 million per year. So we can expect the - we'd have established a specific line for it and we are looking at probably in the second half of next year, probably we should be able to start the real batch and volume production for that.

items.statement: Other expenses at 12.5% of sales in Q2; expected to stabilize at normal levels by end FY25 as plasma coating qualification completes and outsourcing costs reduce drastically
items.quote: Yes, exactly because our outsourcing costs are going to come down drastically, because of the cost. Once we are qualified, our costs are going to come down.

items.statement: Bloom Energy orders released quarter-to-quarter with calendar year forecast; 4,000 unit forecast may increase further by end of current quarter
items.quote: See, they normally -- presently, they're releasing orders based on quarter -to-quarter basis, but they give forecast for the calendar year, in fact. So right now, from 3,000, they have increased it to 4,000 units for next calendar year, which can even go up further.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 FY25 expected to deliver similar to slightly higher revenue than Q2's INR190.2 crores to achieve full year INR725 crores target
items.quote: No, we'll do similar -- I'm not trying to not to give numbers, but we'll do more or less similar numbers in Q3 and slightly more in Q4. That's what we're going to do.

items.statement: Space order book at INR158 crores (INR50 crores MNC aerospace, INR108 crores ISRO); ISRO projected 20% YoY growth over 2-3 years
items.quote: We have closing order book of INR158 crores in space of which INR50 crores is from MNC aerospace and INR108 crores is from ISRO.

items.statement: Clean energy executed INR192 crores in H1 FY25; dispatched 1,808 hotbox units and 36 electrolyzers; Bloom closing order book at INR493 crores
items.quote: In clean energy, we have executed around INR192 crores of orders in the first half of the year. We have dispatched 1,808 units of hotbox units and 36 units of electrolyzers. The closing order book for Bloom Energy stands at INR493 crores.

items.statement: Project more than doubling volume in Andhra Pradesh from FY24 level of 1.7 million cases on annualized basis
items.quote: We project more than doubling our volume in AP state from FY24 level of 1.7 million cases on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Expect 300 basis point improvement in EBITDA margins over three years from capex projects
items.quote: In current year FY25 we'll be incurring about what we expect a 300 basis point improvement in the EBITDA margins over the same period and would be ROCE accretive.

items.statement: Expect H2 ENA prices to be 2-3% higher than H1
items.quote: We are expecting the H2 ENA prices to be about 2%-2.5%. I mean, this is just a broad estimate at this point of time, but we expect it to be higher between 2%-3% in H2 versus H1.

items.statement: Board approved INR525 crores capex over three years for ENA plant acquisition, malt distillery, PET bottling, and supporting infrastructure
items.quote: So overall we will be investing about INR525 crores of capex over a period of three years which will be funded through a combination of internal accruals and debt.

items.statement: Year 1 capex INR185 crores, Year 2 INR220 crores, Year 3 INR120 crores
items.quote: So, of the INR527 crores, year one is INR185 crores. Year two will need about INR220 crores, and year three will need about the balance INR120 crores.

items.statement: ICONiQ White annual run rate 4-5 million cases, expected to double from last year's 2.3 million cases
items.quote: Currently the annual run rate is between 4 to 5 million cases which means that the brand is Allied Blenders and expected to double from its last year volume of 2.3 million cases

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 42.9% in Q2 FY25 from 38.7% in Q1 FY25 and 39.2% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: The gross margin improved to 42.9% in quarter 2 of FY '25 as Allied Blenders and compared to 38.7% in Q1 of FY '25 and 39.2% in Q2 FY '24

items.statement: EBITDA margin at roughly 12% in Q2, targeting 15% industry parity over 2-3 years from capex projects
items.quote: if you see our Q2 EBITDA is roughly 12%. And if you look at the economic value that the capex project will add over the next two or three years, so they hopefully live about two and a half years from now. So the incremental EBITDA that this project will deliver is roughly 300 basis points.

items.statement: Expect price increases in coming financial year to be no different than current year at mixed level
items.quote: So for now as we see things, I think even for the coming financial year, we expect price increases to be no different than what we have seen in the current financial year.

items.statement: Anticipate positive shift in consumer sentiment in festive season driving market growth
items.quote: First a little bit about the industry as we move into the festive season, we anticipate a positive shift in consumer sentiment which is expected to drive market growth.

items.statement: P&A volume salience increased to 39.7% in Q2 FY25 from 36.9% in Q1 FY25 and 36.5% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: The growth was led by premiumization of the portfolio with continued increase in P&A volume salience to 39.7% in Q2 FY '25 as compared to 36.9% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Telangana receivables at INR350 crores, expect significant reduction by Q4 FY25 as payments now coming daily
items.quote: So at the end of Q2, the overview are by and large in the same range, about INR350 odd crores. So there has been some change, but not significant. And again, if we were to go by the guidance that we received from Telangana, we do expect a significant reduction.

items.statement: Peak debt for capex projects expected at INR200 crores, overall debt to come down as Telangana overdues get paid
items.quote: So, like I said earlier the INR525 crores of debt is spread across three years. INR185 crores in year 1, INR220 crores in year 2 and about 100 balanced debt in year 3. This will be funded out of internal accrual and on debt and we believe from our planning perspective, I think our peak debt for this project will be about INR200 crores.

items.statement: Launched Zoya gin in Goa and Rajasthan, planning two new flavors and key markets in Q3 FY25, expanding to UAE
items.quote: Post the successful launch in Haryana and Maharashtra, ABDL has expanded Zoya's presence in Goa and Rajasthan. Additionally, key markets and two new flavours are planned for launch in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Formed ABD Maestro subsidiary with Ranveer Singh holding 20% equity for luxury portfolio
items.quote: Essentially, this entity will focus on the luxury portfolio and in terms of the infrastructure that we are building, the people skills that we are building, the focus is on our luxury portfolio. So that's about the entity. As we have made - as we provided declarations I think this is Ranveer will hold 20% equity in this venture. ABD will hold 80%, it will be a subsidiary of ABD.

items.statement: Signed distribution agreement for Russian Standard Vodka portfolio (Original, Gold, Platinum) in India
items.quote: ABD and Rouse Corporation one of the largest vodka producers in the world announced the launch of world's number one Russian premium vodka in India.

items.statement: Revised full-year revenue growth guidance to approximately 16%
items.quote: Earlier, we had given the guidance of 18% for the full year, but now we are revising the top line guidance to 16% approximately for the next quarter as well as for the whole year.

items.statement: Revised EBITDA margin guidance to 100 bps improvement over last year
items.quote: Earlier, we have given the guidance of 100 bps reduction. But now we have revised the EBITDA margin guidance, 100 bps improvement over last year.

items.statement: Expect at least 100 bps gross margin growth for the full year
items.quote: And in the coming quarter and the whole full year basis, we are expecting at least 100 basis points growth in gross margin.

items.statement: Pricing impact was around 4% in Q2, expect year-end gap around 3%
items.quote: We see pricing impact in quarter 2 is around 4%, in quarter 1 was more than 6%. And on year-end basis, we are expecting the gap should be around 3%, not much, beyond 3%.

items.statement: Generic prices stabilized but may reduce 2-3% further in next 2 quarters
items.quote: But now I think they are stabilized, and I don't foresee. But there can be a possibility in few molecules where the inventory levels are high, 2%, 3% further reduction in the prices is possible in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Rabi acreages appear very positive and bright with good reservoir levels
items.quote: With good reservoir position and groundwater situation being very favourable we are looking at very positive Rabi acreages coming up, including paddy in South India, very high acreages of over Bengal gram, red gram, and black gram in almost entire South and Maharashtra.

items.statement: New products LaNevo, Purge, MYCORe Super performing beyond expectations
items.quote: LaNevo, Purge, MYCORe Super have done beyond our expectations in many markets.

items.statement: Dahej plant revenue guidance of INR250 crores over 3 years
items.quote: So over 3 years, we'll be doing to INR250 crores.

items.statement: Dahej breakeven estimated at INR150-200 crores annual revenue
items.quote: Yes. So for breakeven, our estimate is close to a revenue of INR150 crores to INR200 crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Partnership products revenue share expected at 33-36% for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think it would be in the range between 33% to 36%.

items.statement: Exclusive partnership products gross margin 1000-1500 bps above average
items.quote: Range, you can say whatever our average gross margin, the range is more than 1,000 basis points to 1,500 basis points.

items.statement: Sales returns increased over 40% to more than INR100 crores in Q2 due to continuous rain
items.quote: Yes, the sales return has increased significantly as compared to previous year, the sales return has increased by more than 40%. It's more than INR100 crores in quarter 2.

items.statement: Inventory buildup due to sales returns and missed sprays, expected to normalize by year-end
items.quote: Inventory, you see because of continuous rain in the month of September, there were many sprays or missing pesticides because of which we have left a little more inventory, one, and another is the high return of weedicide which was sold in quarter 1 and taken back in the quarter 2. But I'm expecting the inventory would be in line with our expectation by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Volume growth around 10% in Q2, would have been 20%+ adjusted for returns
items.quote: Yes, volume growth is around 10% in quarter 2.

items.statement: ITI index at 16.09% for H1 vs 16.39% last year
items.quote: ITI index is 16.3% -- 16.09% in this half year basis as compared to last year's 16.39%.

items.statement: Export revenue target revised to Rs. 600-650 crores for FY25 from earlier Rs. 650-700 crores
items.quote: Rs. 650 crores look a little tough, it is not unachievable. Given the kind of stretch which is happening in Europe and U.S. in terms of demand slump down, Rs. 650 crores looks a little bit tough. But Rs. 600 crores to Rs. 650 crores anywhere in between is what we are trying to target.

items.statement: Alloy wheel export growth target of 50% for FY25
items.quote: And we feel that for this financial year 50% growth on alloy wheel export will be a minimum thing which is going to be targeted by us.

items.statement: Tractor segment domestic growth 9-11% for FY25 with market share rising to 41-42%
items.quote: And that growth could be anywhere between 9% to 10% to 11% for the Financial Year '24-'25. And the trend is very, very aggressive and on this side that first we need to stabilize at 41%, 42% in terms of the industry landscape.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckle commercialization starts Q3 FY25; mass production from October; target Rs. 15 crores revenue in FY25
items.quote: Mass production has started from the month of October. And I think it is still at a nascent stage. And Q4 will be when it is going to be at close to 70% of the first phase capacity.

items.statement: FY25 capex revised lower to under Rs. 200 crores from guided Rs. 225 crores; funded by internal accruals
items.quote: I guess, based on what we have spent in H1, the amount that we will be spending on CAPEX will be lower than what we have guided for. I guess it will be under Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel improved to Rs. 256 in H1 FY25 from Rs. 251 in H1 FY24; margin 11.33% vs 11.19%
items.quote: If you look at H1 current year, we are already at Rs. 256 and this number is versus Rs. 251, which was H1 last year. So, this number has already started to inch upwards.

items.statement: Price correction agreed with OEMs; margin impact visible from Q4 FY25; annual impact Rs. 10-25 crores
items.quote: So, that price correction has been agreed with the OEM and I think that you will see that correction coming into action in terms of the Q4 end in terms of pricing and margin increase.

items.statement: Target 15-50 bps margin improvement in FY26 from repricing and efficiency; not 100-200 bps
items.quote: I don't think 100, 200 basis point is the right expectation. I think we are at close to 11.5-odd something that we are trying to run around right now. But at a scale that we are trying to work out in next financial year, we expect 15, 20, 25, 50 basis point improvement in this, that is what the intent is.

items.statement: Debt reduced by Rs. 121 crores in H1 to Rs. 926 crores; target Rs. 825 crores by FY25 end; Rs. 300 crores repayment over next two years
items.quote: For the current quarter, overall debt stands at Rs. 926 crores versus Rs. 1,047 crores in Q4 FY '24, thus a reduction of around Rs. 121 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target revised to Rs. 4,300-4,400 crores for FY25 from earlier Rs. 4,800 crores
items.quote: Rs. 4,300 crores, Rs. 4,400 crores is what we are eying.

items.statement: Export uncertainty from US election outcome, freight cost spikes, and dumping from Vietnam/Thailand impacting margins by Rs. 2-3 crores
items.quote: One is the current situation of freight, which has suddenly again gone up and because of the Chinese and the Singaporean disruptions, which has created a little bit of uncertainty. And second thing is, given the situation, which is there in U.S., I feel a lot of uncertainty is there with this Trump and Harris coming into picture.

items.statement: Key FY25 capex items: aluminum expansion, knuckle equipment, solar panel balance payments
items.quote: A key area remains, one, aluminum expansion that we are doing; s econd, the knuckle, flow from equipment and the balance payment towards solar panel installations. So, those are the key CAPEX items that we have for current year

items.statement: Domestic alloy wheel penetration risen to 41-42% from 36-37%; target 3.6-4 million domestic alloy wheels plus 0.5 million exports
items.quote: We feel that the alloy wheel industry, given that the industry grows at 5% to 6% in terms of the passenger vehicle production, we feel that the industry has fairly a capability of growing at 10% to 11%, 12%.

items.statement: Revenue target of ₹1,500 crores for FY25; may reach ₹1,600 crores
items.quote: Own projection is ₹1,500 crores. It may be ₹1,600 crores also. So, let's see. We are working hard on that.

items.statement: Previous guidance for FY26 was around ₹1,800 crores; management feels confident to achieve projections
items.quote: The way the business is growing and moving, the way we are getting orders, the way the company is getting international goodwill also, international presence also, we feel we should be able to achieve all what we said or what we project.

items.statement: Three new SORTEX units at Karnal costing ₹1.5-2 crores each; all operational by January end
items.quote: the machinery, I think one unit will not cost more than ₹2 crores, would be less than ₹2 crores. So, we're not talking much money

items.statement: New unit at Mundra/Gandhidham with ₹1.5 crores CapEx; potential ₹100-150 crores annual revenue
items.quote: It will be around ₹1.50 crores CapEx. Complete machinery, SORTEX, electric, all is likely to be, because the budget is ₹1.50 crores approx.

items.statement: More orders than current packing capacity; rushing CapEx to meet demand
items.quote: As of now, I can speak that we have more orders than what we are packing monthly. So, there is a lot of future. There is a lot of scope to grow.

items.statement: No demand slowdown; demand exceeds supply prompting capacity expansion
items.quote: No, no. With us, we have more demand than our own supply even. That's why we are rushing for the CapEx increase.

items.statement: Ocean freight dropped from $5,000 to $2,000; CIF sales at old high freight rates boosting margins
items.quote: With the Red Sea crisis last year, the ocean freights had gone up. And now from $5,000, they have already come down to $2,000.

items.statement: Iran ban on Indian rice lifts 22 Nov; no impact as company doesn't trade with Iran
items.quote: 22nd November, this ban is going to get lifted. There is absolutely no impact. We don't work with Iran.

items.statement: Malaysia sales are transshipment hub; rice goes to Indonesia, Japan, Australia
items.quote: Regarding Malaysia, I would say the Port of Malaysia is used. That is why you're getting confused that rice is going to Malaysia. It is going all over the places from Malaysia.

items.statement: Three new Karnal units: two for 5kg packing, one for 50kg; Mundra unit for larger packs
items.quote: Two plants are dedicated for 5-kilogram packing and one plant is dedicated for 50-kilogram package.

items.statement: Bank limits ₹350 crores (HDFC ₹300 cr, PNB ₹50 cr); seasonal borrowing starts November at ~4% interest
items.quote: ₹300 crores by HDFC Bank and ₹50 crores with PNB.

items.statement: Directors' remuneration percentage to reduce over time as profits grow; dividend ~10% of profit
items.quote: As regard dividend is concerned, we have given around 10% of the profitability in the last one year and recently dispersed dividend.

items.statement: Crop size 15-20% higher this year; prices very reasonable compared to last year
items.quote: In this particular year, the crop size is around 15% to 20% higher, and some parts are not evaluated by APEDA.

items.statement: Debottlenecking capex of Rs 10 crore in ATC AZO business to be completed by March or April 2025, adding 720 tons per year pigment capacity and Rs 30-35 crore annual revenue.
items.quote: We have embarked upon a small debottlenecking exercise with the CapEx of 10 crores, which should be completed by March or April of 25. This 10 crore CapEx should increase above pigment capacity by 720 tons per year. This should add a revenue of 30 to 35 crores per year on the top line.

items.statement: Target to reach Rs 25 crore quarterly revenue run-rate in AZO business by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: I think we should be able to reach there in the first quarter of the next financial.

items.statement: Aim to achieve Rs 200 crore API revenue in FY26; H1 FY25 revenue was Rs 52 crore.
items.quote: We have the capacity, we have the opportunity now we have to work over there. But yes for 25-26 that is a real possibility.

items.statement: Blue business EBITDA margins are well into double digits and inching up towards the 13-15% target range, but timeline depends on demand recovery.
items.quote: are well into the double digits on the blue business and we hope to build upon this and so we are kind of close to where, you know the 13-15 you indicated and we should, of course we would like to get to that 13 to 15 and that should be possible

items.statement: Blue pigment demand environment remains very bad; volume growth expected at Hindu rate of 3-5% over couple of years with 15-20% free capacity available.
items.quote: Over a period of couple of years, you could probably see in you know the Hindu growth rate of three to 5% kind of thing over there, but nothing more exciting in that area.

items.statement: AZO business utilization at 65-66% overall; red and yellow lines improving QoQ, expecting proportional utilization increase in coming quarters.
items.quote: Our overall capacity utilization for the AZO business stands at about 66 percent, 65%.

items.statement: Pregabalin demand estimated to grow 5-8% CAGR over next five years; pricing under pressure this quarter but demand is growing.
items.quote: Pregabalin demand is estimated to grow about 7% over the next five years. Prices continue to be under pressure so that we will see now with China plus one also how it plays out now that Trump is in office will also put an interesting aspect to it, but demand for pregabalin will prob ably do decently well 5 to 8% over the next five years compounded

items.statement: API strategy: focus first on high-volume, cost-efficient molecules to fill Chattral capacity, then pursue high-value niche molecules; two new molecules developed at Odhav R&D but no major revenue impact in FY26.
items.quote: we would be using both the strategies and we would need to use both the strategies the higher volume, lowe r margin, lower value you know products to fill up capacity and the high value lower volume, higher margin products to you know, get a name in the market

items.statement: No inorganic growth planned in pigment business currently; board not entertaining such thoughts, but open to inorganic growth in Pharma/API segment in future.
items.quote: We are not at this point of time considering any inorganic growth in the pigment business. This does not mean we may not revisit that in the future, but as of today, the board is not entertaining any thoughts of inorganic growth for the pigment business as such.

items.statement: Working capital turns improved to 3.36x in Q2 from 2.84x in March 2024; cash conversion cycle improved to 86 days from 109 days.
items.quote: our working capi tal turn at the quarter stood at 3.36 turns. This compared favorably to 2.84 turns for March 24. Of a cash conversion showed at 86 days, which also compares favorably as compared to 109 days on a group basis for March 24

items.statement: Second half FY25 expected to show reasonable improvement from new plants (Dahej AZO and Chattral API/intermediate) vs first half, but not game-changing on half-year basis.
items.quote: We would clearly want to see the reasonable improvement from two of the four plants, which is both the new plants. 1 the pigment plant at Dahej, the AZO plant and the intermediate and API facility in Chattral. So, from these two we should see certainly improve the second-half as compared to the first half.

items.statement: Capex cycle of last three years ending; deleveraging process starting; capex done expected to deliver top-line growth in FY26 and FY27 with bottom-line improvement from 2025.
items.quote: The future for Asahi Group looks solid. The team is very excited as we come to the end of our CapEx cycle of the last three years and start the deleveraging process. The CapEx we have done are starting to deliver top line growth and will continue to do this for the year 25-26 and year 26-27, we hope to start improving on our bottom lines as well as we enter 2025.

items.statement: TTC (global partner) uptake decent but below target; improvement seen this quarter vs very poor last quarter; Europe recovery expected in 2025 with Trump presidency potentially ending Ukraine-Russia war.

items.quote: Yes so currently if you notice we are growing at 20% in the first half and generally Q3 is quite sluggish due to the festive demand which is there and the holidays which are there so due to that we will we have put up a 15 to 18 % growth rate which we will hopefully achieve looking at the current scenario.

items.quote: So we already have planned capex for the next 18 months which we had spoken about in the last earnings call also tha t it is in the range of INR 70 to 80 crores out of which INR 25 crores is going towards the recent acquisition that we have done in Malaysia for acquisition of mines and there is another capex which will be ongoing capex for 20 Microns in terms of the addi tion of capacities for our

items.statement: Raw material costs increased over 1.5% YoY, the major factor driving expense increase; freight costs for imported materials and transportation costs also rose.
items.quote: So basically as I mentioned to you in my opening remarks that the raw material cost has increased which is a major factor which has increased by more than 1.5 % YoY so that is the major contributing factor to the overall expense compared to any of the other expenses that we have in place.

items.statement: Optimistic about H2 FY25 with constant progress in demand expected, especially in domestic market; Q3 currently sluggish but pickup expected post-Diwali.
items.quote: Looking ahead. we are optimistic about the second half of the financial year as well which is expected to maintain the consumption across key industries and we anticipate a constant progress in demand in the coming quarters especially in the domestic market.

items.quote: So definitely this is one of the factors along with certain transportation costs which have also increased due to the increase in the sales that we have seen in the past half a year. items.statement: EPC gross margin stable at 14.5-15%; target EPC EBITDA 11-12% and PBT ~10% over time; blended margin ~9% this year, rising as real estate share grows
items.quote: EPC has been quite stable with the growth in scale of EPC, we hope to achieve EBITDA in the range of 11% and 12% . Hope to get a PBT closer to , our target is to reach, step -by-step reach close to 10 % in terms of PBT

items.statement: Plan to launch 2-3 real estate projects in FY25: OM Sainath (Santacruz) in Dec 2024, Powai in early 2025, others in FY26; Pune launches (Kharadi 0.5 msf, Baner-Pashan 1 msf) in FY26

items.statement: QIP on hold due to market conditions; will use private equity or short-term debt for real estate project funding; GMP sale net proceeds Rs 100-110 Crore (Rs 60-70 Cr to real estate, 20-25% to EPC collateral)
items.quote: As of now, we put QIP in the back seat as because, if you look at that market and all these things, we are not very hopeful to go with the QIP as because dilution of the existing stakeholder will be quite substantial with th is price.

items.statement: GMP sale proceeds to create EPC collateral for augmenting bank guarantee limits; need ~Rs 100 Crore BG limit over next 6 months for Rs 1,000 Crore order booking target
items.quote: And to achieve a Rs. 1,000 Crores order booking, you need 5% BG, and conservatively speaking another at least 5%, 7% of advance that we would like to draw down to start those projects. So, about 10% so Rs. 100 Crores of BG limit would have to be fronted over the next six months

items.statement: Cost of borrowing likely to stay 11-12% as short-term collateral-free loans for real estate/EPC interim funding carry ~12% rate; no drastic reduction planned
items.quote: Cost of borrowing, although we would like to attempt to bring it down. But at this point of time, as I said, for the kind of loans that we look for which are short term loans in both real estate and EPC, collateral free, they would come in that range of 12% only.

items.statement: Q3 EPC billing trajectory climbing; Moshi, Police Housing Pune, Capgemini, Suphal Bihar projects ramping up; Q3 top line much better than Q2
items.quote: No, Q3 is going as per plan, couple of projects M oshi and P olice Housing in Pune and now Capgemini, all three have taken off. And so, the billing trajectory on these projects now is climbing.

items.statement: Real estate EBITDA/PBT ~double EPC levels (16-17% PBT); blended margin depends on revenue mix (currently 90% EPC)
items.quote: On the real estate our gross, our PBT would come about double of our EPC PBT would be in the range of 16% – 17%.

items.statement: Expect double-digit sequential profit growth for rest of FY25
items.quote: Overall, we had 30% growth in sequential PBT this quarter, and we are confident of maintaining strong double-digit growth in sequential profits for rest of the quarter.

items.statement: Plan INR20 crore capex over 18 months for Hire Tech platform starting Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are planning for a total spending of roughly about INR20-odd crores of capex starting Q1 of this year, and this would be spend over a period of 18 months.

items.statement: Specialized staffing EBITDA up 18% YoY and 26% QoQ due to cost savings and one-time absorption benefits
items.quote: EBITDA is up by 18% year-on-year and 26% sequentially, largely due to cost-saving efforts and some onetime sourcing and absorption benefits.

items.statement: Other HR Services target 6-8% EBITDA margin for FY25, 8-10% sustainable in coming years
items.quote: So at annual level, we should be able to make 6% to 8% EBITDA margin in other HR Services this year, and that can improve to 8% to 10% sustainable margins in the coming years.

items.statement: Q3 general staffing growth muted due to BFSI caution from RBI KYC norms; consumer and telecom to grow
items.quote: Q3 can be muted on the backlog of caution in the BFSI sector and the drawdown which typically happe ns due to temporary sensitive hiring, which takes place towards the end of Q2

items.statement: Specialized staffing expects moderate Q3 growth from GCCs and non-tech; IT services closures taking longer
items.quote: We don't see a dramatic surge in the demand right away. I think that's going to come in gradually. A lot of hiring that has happened, and I know that a lot of new fresher hiring that has also been opening up. But the closures, like I mentioned are taking time.

items.statement: Added 37 new logos in Q2 (80 in H1), 70% on variable model; 15 new specialized staffing clients including 9 large strategic accounts
items.quote: We had about 37 new logos that makes it in H1 about 80-odd logos, driven largely by consumer financial services and manufacturing sectors. Of these, as I highlighted before, 70% have signed on to variable model.

items.quote: GCC contribution, about 18 months back, was at 40% on revenue. And about the year back, it's at 50%. So we are consistently adding numbers and clients on GCC front, and that's also helping us to improve margins overall.

items.statement: BFSI headwinds from RBI KYC strictures expected to suppress Q3 outlook; no new guidelines assumed
items.quote: We think it should be just a Q3 impact because of the specific guideline issued and hence an action to be taken by the NBFCs on that front, subject to no new guidelines coming from RBI to the institutions.

items.statement: Free cash INR340 crore as of 30 Sep 2024; working capital borrowing up at EdTech in line with growth
items.quote: Free cash stands at INR340 crores as of 30th September 2024. These are the high level comments on quarterly results.

items.statement: Hire Tech platform to go live in FY26, aims to cut hiring costs and boost recruiter productivity across all employment clusters
items.quote: We've also been adding new logos and delivering more on hiring. Parallelly, we are investing in a high-tech platform, which we believe will go live in FY '26. The platform aims to bring down our hiring costs significantly in a phased manner.

items.statement: 80JJAA tax benefit continues with no sunset; standalone effective tax rate 0% for 3-5 years, consolidated 8-10% from next year

items.quote: We had more than 3,000 new additions across all the apprenticeship schemes, be it NAPS, NATS or the work-integrated learning program. And we saw INR27 increase in our PAPMs, with learning additions increasing by 23%.

items.statement: On track to meet FY26 revenue target of 3200 crores through organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: We are pretty much on track to meet our numbers as a combination of organic and inorganic, we are very much on track to meet our numbers.

items.quote: I have always maintained that we are looking at around 600 crores of CAPEX over 3 years. I am requesting my CFO to correct my statement and next year will be about 150 to 180 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 13-13.5%, exports recovery could add 50 basis points
items.quote: I have always maintained in many quarters that our 13 to 13.5% EBITDA is what we intend to maintain and what looks reasonable for our set of products. Margins will be a little better when exports resume. Exports, this was probably the weakest quarter in many quarters, so when exports resume or comes back, margins will go up about 50 basis points.

items.quote: Demand is very muted in the industry. My industry peers also tell me that their performance is also very muted. In terms of exports, because of the Elections in the US, and the policies of the Republican government that have come in, expor

items.statement: Exports at 6.5% of revenue vs 9% last year, US election impact on export demand
items.quote: Same quarter last year was about 9% and this year is about 6.5%.

items.statement: May raise up to 300 crores debt for acquisitions, currently debt-free with cash reserves
items.quote: We are a debt-free company. We have cash reserves. But depending on the size of the acquisition, we are not only looking at this. We are looking at other inorganic play also, safe inorganic play in allied areas and as I have maintained in my earlier calls, up to about 300 crores of debt, we are looking at probably raising based on the kind of acquisition.

items.quote: In H1 FY '25, banks have floated RFPs of more than 21,000 plus ATMs and CRMs.

items.quote: So, Ankur, our endeavour is to maintain that margin.

items.statement: Expect larger ATM and CRM deployment volumes in H2 FY25 compared to H1
items.quote: So, we normally see an H2 which is higher than H1. So, we expect still larger volumes coming on to H2.

items.quote: Our ongoing pilot of contactless fueling solution on the Ongo app has expanded to over 60 fuel outlets in Mumbai, and we have onboarded about 2,000 fleet vehicles.

items.quote: So, we expect to roll out city-wise, maybe by 500 outlets by the end of the year.

items.quote: The EBITDA has improved from INR 383 million to 429 million, which shows a margin gross from 17.1% to 20.1% margin.

items.quote: The net debt position of the company stood at INR6,839 million along with the reverse factoring and INR6,092 million without reverse factoring.

items.quote: We expect the repayments to improve from Q4 onwards as green shoots of improvement are starting to show up in Q3

items.quote: So, this year, like I have said in last time we spoke, Saketji, we are looking at a 20% minimum growth in the small farm machine space.

items.statement: Management expects at least 20% plus growth in tillers for full year FY25
items.quote: So, tillers, I would expect at least 20% plus growth by the end of the year.

items.quote: We are going to take it to about 25% to 30% of our business.

items.quote: So, to get to that 3,000 number, it looks like we will have to move to FY '27, but definitely that milestone is not something we will give up on, and we will definitely chase it down.

items.statement: Management expects Rs 2,000 crore revenue visibility in FY26
items.quote: But then we currently have like in the last quarter, I shared with you that we have a visibility of around 2,000. That looks very much there.

items.statement: Power weeder manufacturing started in India using existing power tiller facility with capacity expansion plans
items.quote: The good news I can share with you, which I had announced earlier also, we will be manufacturing power weeders in India. With the scale up of volumes that has happened, we are rolling out the first power weeders this month onwards.

items.statement: Government orders caused receivables to increase to 70 days, expected to normalize to 45-50 days by end of Q3
items.quote: So, receivables have gone up purely because of the government orders we have received and the supply which is in process. So, I would say that by the end of Q3, it would normalize and come back to the normal levels of around 45 to 50 days of receivables.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin maintained at 13.33% in Q2, target range 11-13% on operational level
items.quote: See, the margins have been maintained as I said that 13.33% on an operational level, and I had said, we will always be on the higher side of 11% to 13%. We will be closer to 13%.

items.statement: October volumes encouraging: 1,783 tillers vs 1,200 in Oct'23; 680 tractors vs 289 in Oct'23

This year, I would say, H1 was kind of flattish, except for the Q1 drop that we had about 30-40 crores. But if you see Q2, we have caught up. And, in fact, we have got slight growth and in Q3 and Q4, we should be able to grow at the rates we always wanted to grow at about 20% to 30%

items.statement: VST Zetor JV launched in May 2024, targeting 1,000 units in FY25; 56 dealers in North, targeting 75-80 by year end
items.quote: Very happy to state that the scale up is happening, and it is going as per plan. This year I had indicated we should be doing around 1,000 numbers.

items.statement: Power weeder volumes growing rapidly: H1 3,490 units vs 2,206 last year; targeting 8,000+ units in FY25 and 3x in next 2 years
items.quote: We should be upwards of 8,000 numbers this year within just 2 years. And we expect in the next 2 years, we should be 3x that volume, minimum.

items.quote: So, the one concern that I have is on the bottom line. I hope that doesn't reverse itself and the commodity prices shoot up because of an extended war or the Gulf War or whatever reason. I hope that d

items.statement: Interest cost run rate targeted at Rs.75-80 crore per quarter
items.quote: I would say the interest cost should be in the range of Rs.75-80 crores is something that we have been working on, saying that it should not go beyond Rs.75-80 crores in terms of a run rate of the interest cost.

items.statement: Capacity expansions and CAPEX cycle completed; manufacturing facilities strategically located
items.quote: Our strategically located manufacturing facilities, completed capacity expansions and CAPEX cycle, and our continuous focus on cost structure optimization, product development and innovation, emphasis on data center portfolio and tier one customer approvals.

items.quote: Largely, we typically enjoy better realizations in the North America market. And so, since those volumes have come down, as you would have seen last few quarters, our average realization at company level would have come down compared to maybe last year or two years ago.

items.quote: As per latest CRU projections, the medium term demands the optical fiber volumes is to go up steadily to 652 million fiber kilometers by 2028. This projects a healthy 4.3% annual growth in the annual demand and a strong 7% annual demand growth for ex-China during 2023 to 2028.

items.quote: Our optical connectivity product line continues to demonstrate strong growth momentum, as we noted, our highest ever quarterly revenue for optical connectivity products an attach rate of 22% during last quarter.

items.quote: We have taken a target that 25% of our optical business revenue should come from this segment in the medium term, that's the whole thought process.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty in Europe: no supply disruption; Italy facility scaling improves profitability
items.quote: So Nikhil, from the supply chain perspective absolutely there is no impact because whatever customer orders are being placed, we have been able to serve all of them without any kind of disruption

items.quote: The date for the final petition is pending with NCLT Mumbai bench, the final NCLT order is expected in an indicative timeline of next 3-4 months that is Q3, Q4 of FY25 and resulting companies can be expect to get listed on stock exchanges.

items.quote: We continue to work with our customers for growing our business in the US, Europe and India across technology and service verticals and expect the future growth to be driven by robust order book of more than Rs.336 crores, healthy order pipeline and executions strength backed by right team of leadership and consultants.

items.quote: Normal value is about 15% to 20% in a year.

items.quote: Our new office spaces in Chandigarh and Pune will go live in Q3 and the new space in Mumbai will go live in early Q4.

items.statement: Combined technology and analytics under single leadership to improve agility and value proposition
items.quote: We have combined technology and analytics under single leadership. This will help us position our services better improve agility and enhance the value proposition for our clients.

items.quote: if we are moving into more change and analytics kind of work, then the employee cost in those areas is higher. So, it's kind of hard to say definitively that the employee cost has peaked.

items.statement: Senior leadership hiring under CEO largely done; further hiring case-by-case for sales and delivery
items.quote: The senior leadership under Kapil , that hiring is done. But under the senior leaders, we will decide on a case-to-case basis on whether we need to strengthen in certain areas, add more sales muscle in other areas and so on, that continues to happen on a case-to-case basis.

items.statement: Buyback vs dividend priority to be examined after tax changes; no immediate decision
items.quote: I think we will definitely have to examine it, as you say, there is no difference in buyback and dividend anymore other than the reduction in dilution. So, we have to examine, but I guess there is a lot of time for us to do it.

items.statement: Margin dilution for new Cayman hospital now expected to last 4-5 quarters instead of 6-8 quarters
items.quote: we'd like to change our estimates from the 6-8 quarters and change it to about 4-5 quarters is when we expect some margin dilution.

items.statement: International patient business expected to go to zero over next 10 years
items.quote: the international business is one number that I expect to go to zero over the next 10 years.

items.statement: Committed projects include 700 beds in Kolkata and Bangalore greenfield and 150 beds brownfield in Raipur over next 3-3.5 years
items.quote: We already 5 have committed projects which include greenfield in Kolkata and Bangalore totaling to around 700 beds and the brownfield in Raipur with around 150 beds. This will come up in the next 3-3.5 years’ time

items.statement: Total bed addition target of around 1500 beds in next four years across Bangalore, Kolkata, Raipur and potential new greenfield projects
items.quote: all in all, it would be adding around close to 1500 beds in the next four years from now provided there are no material delays on the projects.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex spend of Rs 530 crores, with Rs 320 crores in India including Rs 160 crores for Bangalore land
items.quote: We have spent about ₹530 crores in H1 of which ₹320 crores is in India and balance is in Cayman. Out of this ₹320 crores, ₹160 crores was for the land we bought in Bangalore

items.quote: The intent is to add 1000 beds in Kolkata but it will go live in two phases. So, the first phase which we are building, is what we have factored right now.

items.statement: New hospital cluster revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 130 crores with 11% EBITDA margin in Q2
items.quote: the new hospital cluster has done pretty well in this quarter. It's given a very strong revenue growth around 13% year -on-year, with the revenue crossing around ₹130 crores for this quarter, with an EBITDA of around 11%.

items.statement: Typical annual price increase is low single digits 4-5%, with ARPP growth beyond that driven by efficiency, complex procedures and payor mix
items.quote: Our typical price increase is low single digits, 4-5% every year. So, anything beyond that is all efficiency driven.

items.statement: Cayman outpatient and inpatient volumes declined in Q2 due to team focus on new hospital commissioning and hurricanes causing 7-10 days disruption
items.quote: We had a couple of hurricanes that led to about 7-10 days of unproductive work. Just a g eneral slow quarter but we're happy and comfortable that in the month of October things are back to a very positive trajectory

items.statement: Bangladesh patient flows remain severely restricted with only critical patients allowed, no timeline for normalization
items.quote: The situation in Bangladesh, it continues to suffer. The visa restrictions are still in its minimal. Only the critical patients allowed entry into the country.

items.statement: Domestic ARPP higher than international; shift to domestic patients and growth in complex procedures like TAVI and robotic cardiac surgery driving ARPP growth
items.quote: Historically, the domestic ARPP has always been higher when compared to international ARPP. So, some of that has played in terms of the average ARPP that has come through.

items.statement: No further significant capex planned in Cayman; surplus cash netted against debt, exploring repatriation or other investment opportunities
items.quote: with the new Camana Bay hospital we're done with any significant capital outlay in that market. So, that is correct. The liquidity, I would just, you know, although there is a cash balance, it is also significantly netted off against our outstanding debt

items.statement: Insurance pilot in Mysore encouraged expansion to Bangalore; Rs 1.2 million GWP since launch, focusing on building distribution channels
items.quote: We were sufficiently encouraged by the results that we actually pr eponed our entry into Bangalore and launched in Bangalore as well towards the end of the quarter

items.statement: Consolidated effective tax rate outlook maintained at current 14-17% range as India performance offsets Cayman zero-tax benefit
items.quote: we would like to maintain the outlook on the tax rate as it is going currently.

items.statement: No specific revenue growth guidance given; focusing on healthy EBITDA, improving realizations per patient and reducing ALOS
items.quote: We don't normally give out guidance on the growth numbers. We're just trying to maintain a healthy pace of growth, keeping in mind that we're not adding any new beds

items.statement: Cayman new facility expected to reach pre-commissioning margins in 4-5 quarters instead of 6-8 quarters
items.quote: We initially anticipated about 6-8 quarters to return to pre-commissioning margins. We now think that will be closer to 4-5 quarters as I had shared earlier as well.

items.statement: All new capex for hospitals adjacent to existing facilities with future-proof design including robotic ORs and ICU-convertible rooms
items.quote: Yes. So, all the Capex that we are putting forward are almost adjacent or within a short driving distance of the hospital that we have.

items.statement: Corporate overheads run at 4% of revenue including significant technology investment in ATHMA and MEDHA
items.quote: 4pc of revenue is what we normally clock in as corporate overheads but that also includes a significant investment in technology because we are investing significantly in ATMA and MEDA and including that, we do about 4pc of revenue.

items.statement: Bangladesh revenue contribution declined from 9% to 6.5% and expected to trend to zero over a decade
items.quote: Bangladesh was typically around 8-9pc of revenue. We have come down to 6.5pc of revenue.

items.statement: Cayman Q2 revenue declined 7% YoY due to hurricane but October already back to previous growth trajectory
items.quote: in the month that’s have gone by, that’s October, the first month of quarter 3, we are alr eady back to our previous growth trajectory and a little better as well

items.statement: Focus expanding beyond cardiac and oncology to GI sciences, orthopedics, nephro-urology, acute care, and day care beds
items.quote: Apart from the cardiac sciences and the oncology, I think a lot of focus is going into GI sciences, orthopedics. Nephro Urology has been a very strong point in most of our centres.

items.statement: Integrated care and insurance business EBITDA burn expected around ₹55 crores for full year, similar burn rate for next 2 quarters
items.quote: You can expect a bit more, but the total number should not exceed ₹55 crores.

items.statement: No QIP planned currently due to sufficient leverage and internal cash flows, and belief market undervalues company
items.quote: Not at this point for 2 reasons – one is, we have sufficient leverage available within the India balance sheet to be able to fund a lot of the expansion that we have planned through borrowing.

items.statement: India hospital margin disclosed in investor deck; Cayman margin derivable from group margin minus India margin and NHIC/NHIL cash burn
items.quote: So our India margin is, our India hospital margin is there in our investor deck. We have also given the cash burn that we incur in NHIC and NHIL. So the group margin minus the cash burn and the margin that India has made is the Cayman margins.

items.statement: Insurance payor mix currently 29% in India vs industry average 40-45%; expected to increase over 5-10 years
items.quote: 45pc of our patients pay in cash and about 29pc of our patients, I am talking about India, are insured patients.

items.statement: New hospitals will be fully paperless, reception deskless with kiosk navigation, single/double rooms convertible to ICUs, robotic OT ready
items.quote: the new hospitals will not have as much waiti ng rooms, as many registration desks and reception. It will be a fully paperless reception deskless system where with your phone and with kiosk, you are able to navigate yourself through the hospital

items.statement: Cayman Q2 margins dropped 500-600 bps sequentially due to new facility costs (65% incurred in September) and lower existing hospital revenue
items.quote: Yes, I mean an exact break-up won't be possible but you can sort of…..for example there are USD 29 Mn for Q2, the previous quarter was at USD 32 Mn and the one before was at USD 30.5 Mn or so.

items.statement: NHIC cohort model burns cash for ~18 months per cohort before break-even; similar burn rate expected near-term as new cohorts added
items.quote: The logic with which NHIC works is cohort by cohort which means that we start a particular code which is a group of clinics and that cohort breaks even in about 18 months.

items.statement: ATHMA SaaS and MEDHA AI revenue minimal for next 2-3 years; focus on adoption and product improvement not monetization
items.quote: For now, we're just looking to really increase adoption and improve the product.

items.statement: India flagship occupancies 64-65% vs 70% at other units; Bangladesh disruption and Kolkata issues impacted flagships
items.quote: When it comes to flagship s, the occupancies have been at 64 -65pc and had not this issue of Bangladesh and the issue which had 23 happened in Kolkata in this last quarter that happened, the flagship would have also registered occupancies to the level in which the other hospitals have registered, which is nearly 70pc

items.statement: Insurance patients less price-sensitive, opt for private rooms and robotic surgery; out-of-pocket patients more price-sensitive
items.quote: people who paying out of pocket are much more price sensitive whereas people who end up paying insurance while the insurance company will negotiate very hard with the companies on the Rack Rate and discounts on the Rack Rate.

items.statement: Net interest margin rose from 5.2% to 7.1% for H1 FY25 due to increasing lending-as-a-service partnerships.
items.quote: we have seen an increase in our net interest margin, which rose from 5.2% to 7.1% for the half year, given increasing business with these lending as a service partner

items.statement: Lending-as-a-service contributes 47% of total AUM; long-term target is 70% gold loans, 25% business loans, 4-5% three-wheeler EV.
items.quote: LAAS today is about 47% of total AUM. I think it will stay between 40 to 47-48 percent is the number where it is.

items.statement: CapEx plus OpEx to operationalize a gold loan branch is Rs 10-11.5 lakh; FY25 branch additions minimal, FY26 modest at ~7-8 branches.
items.quote: Usually, the CapEx plus OpEx to get a branch operational, especially catering towards the gold loan businesses anywhere between 10 to 11 and a half lakhs.

items.quote: I think it's also because we've focused and we've been working hard on our order book across our businesses, right? So I think that with a specific focus in certain sectors is giving us better growth.

items.statement: Collections and overdues becoming challenging across industry due to money crunch
items.quote: We believe that in this industry and many of the other peer industries, overdue and collections have become a bit of a challenging because of some money crunch that we observed in the market.

items.statement: Inventory built up to INR 741 crores ahead of festive season, expected to normalize in 30-45 days
items.quote: The inventory buildup is predominantly ahead of the festive season. We beefed up the inventory, and that has resulted in a spike in inventory, as of 30th September, we were at INR741 crores. It will get normalized over a period of 1 month to 45 days period.

items.statement: Distribution expansion targeting 5,700-6,000 towns in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are on the anvil of getting close to 5,700 to 6,000 towns between -- in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increased in decorative B2C after new entrant, discounts marginally up
items.quote: So the answer on competitive intensity is, of course, it's increased. I mean, frankly, it has increased over the last 6 months after the new entrant has come in.

items.statement: Management hopes to cross 10% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: I think this year also we hope to cross 10%.

items.statement: Finished good prices dropped 5-6% while raw material prices dropped 3-4%, squeezing margins by about 2 percentage points half-year to half-year
items.quote: So, the finished good prices have dropped a little more than the raw material prices over the period half year to half year. And therefore, the margins have got squeezed by about 2% at points. So, say the finished good prices have dropped by an average of 5%-6% but the raw material prices have dropped 3%-4%.

items.statement: Focus will be on volume over margins in H2, but management tries to expand margins; difficult to predict where margins will land
items.quote: Well, it's difficult to say at this point in time whether we will be able to. We are always optimistic that we will try to improve the margin, but we don't want to sacrifice volume because of it. So, our focus will be more volume than margins, but of course at the same time, we try to expand the margins. But it's difficult to say where we will in the end land up. items.quote: No, this is a part of that 225 crores project. The other part we are still on the R&D stage. This is one of the two lines of products which we were looking at that time. items.statement: FY25 CAPEX around 80-100 crores; FY26 CAPEX around 100-120 crores
items.quote: This year it will be around 80 to 100 crores, and next year may be a slightly larger, about 100 to 120 crores may be.

items.statement: Pharma inventory issues easing; agrochemicals remain under pressure from Chinese cost competition and inventory overhang
items.quote: I would like to say at a macro level, the issues which we had a couple of years back in terms of the so much of inventory in the pipeline and things like this, within pharma sector we see that this seems to be easing a little bit because the other part of the life science, which is the agro-chemical segment still continue to remain under pressure both from the inventory point of view and also from

items.statement: Life sciences accounts for 65-70% of turnover; domestic-export split ~80-20; pharma share growing over agrochemicals long-term
items.quote: They haven't changed at all from our regular life sciences accounting for 65%-70% of our turnover and the rest all, as you can see from our website or wherever, it doesn't change dramatically. Even the domestic export sectors are more or less the same 80-20.

items.statement: Coal cost stable at Rs 9,000-10,000 per metric ton (+/-10% over two years); ammonia prices may see slight bump due to Middle East crisis but planned month-to-month; ethanol imports cheaper than domestic, covered for 5-6 months
items.quote: Yes, the coal is Rs. 9, Rs. 10 Kg. Yes, we of course look at metric ton. So, Rs. 9,000 to Rs. 10,000 a metric ton.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market ~30,000 tons; company market share ~50-55%; utilization ~60% across two plants
items.quote: So, I think the market share remains in that region. As earlier stated by, I think, Nirav, that the market is in the region of 30,000, and you can see that the imports are coming in from the Chinese. So, we are in that region.

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization 65-70% on average; ethylamine plant has headroom for 3-4 years; new CAPEX will not detract from existing lines
items.quote: The existing capacities on average would be 65% to 70% utilization, but it varies from product to product. Some we have very tight where we will be de-bottlenecking and there is some CAPEX involved with that. items.quote: So, after oral hearing now they will come for investigation of our plant and as well as costing records, and then MoC will issue their findings. After that, MoF generally takes 3 to 4 months. Next 4 to 5 months we should expect something.

items.statement: Chinese overcapacity and weak global agrochemical demand driving pricing pressure across value chain; normalization timeline uncertain
items.quote: Yes, I think it is more of a capacity expansion issue. There are overcapacities. They have put on more capacities in the last few years, and the demand has really not picked up too so that all those capacities are utilized, and we see such an immense pressure across the value chain.

items.statement: DEK plant utilization not yet improved as expected but management more optimistic; worst period likely over
items.quote: The utilization rate has not improved as much as we expected to, but going forward, we think it will improve even further. And hopefully, the worst period is over, and we are lot more optimistic on the product now than we were before.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant campaign-based operation runs at 100% when running; no meaningful efficiency gain from higher utilization at contribution margin level
items.quote: No, you have to understand how our plants operate. Our plants are campaign based. So, when they run, they run at 100% capacity, and then we shut down and start. So, there is no question of improvement in efficiencies as such. So, utilization occupancy keeps going up.

items.statement: Working capital cycle stabilized; no significant change expected in working capital requirements
items.quote: I think the working capital cycle, number of days of debtors, number of days of creditors and all have, I think, more or less stabilized, maybe an improvement marginally as volumes go, but nothing significant. I don't think there will be any change in working capital.

items.statement: No CAPEX guidance for FY27; too far out

items.quote: So, by Q4, you can actually expect a growth as compared to what we did in Q4 of last year. Q3 might again not be that great is what our indications are.

items.quote: They are very bullish that this summer there will be a bumper sale in this sector.

items.quote: are already getting a lot of enquiries. So we have started our banana process ing and sampling has already been submitted. So let us see. items.quote: So as far as volume growth is concerned, we are still confident of growing it by 15% volume. But in terms of value because of around whatever reduction of pricing that we had to take on our books. So net-net, the now as a value growth will be hardly low single digit.

items.statement: Standalone publication EBITDA margin expected 30-31% in FY25; stationery 12-13%

items.quote: Yes, Maharashtra -- as I mentioned earlier, we have a gut feel that they'll be able to change only 1 grade, which is grade 1 that in that additional 5% should come from arrest.

items.quote: But coming to specific to Navneet, the revenue from CBSE schools would grow by around 25%, 26% over last year, which was around -- again, in terms of rupees, it was around Rs.25 crores.

items.quote: So overall, on Rs.85 crores that we had, we should grow around 15% to 17%.

items.quote: So altogether, with land, it will be Rs.40 crores to Rs.42 crores of investment, additional investment in the current year.

items.quote: There we plan to further increase the capacity, both manufacturing and storage, and for that, we may end up spending between Rs.50 crores to Rs.60 crores.

items.quote: But generally, I would say that earlier that -- on a yearly basis , last year that we would have lost around Rs.30-odd crores purely on digital business. This year, that loss may come down to around Rs.15 crores.

items.quote: Yes. I mean that for convenience purpose if we could reduce this and that, otherwise 10% plus.

items.quote: We have got closely around INR30,000 crores of jobs under pipeline in various stages. Some of the tenders, some tenders is issued, some we have submitted the bid.
