items.quote: But as I said that end of the year, total job I think INR10,000 crores will be secured in this year. That we are confident about that.

items.statement: Received INR1,600 crores plus GST order in October, over and above the INR5,000 crores H2 target
items.quote: INR1,600 is not part of that. That is beyond INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR67 crores in Q2 FY25, expected to be under control in FY26 as major investments done in last 2 years
items.quote: so far, our capex is around INR67 crores this quarter. Going forward, next year, we had said that the capex will be under control because whatever we have invested, just we have done the last 2 years, we don't see that much investment coming.

items.statement: Middle East market showing very good promises with infrastructure and township building activity
items.quote: Yes. I think the Middle East market has shown very good promises. A lot of things are happening there. You maybe knowing that infrastructure and the township building, etc.

items.statement: Focus on marine segment, with capability for airports, buildings, industrial structures; exploring data center, green energy, renewable energy, high-speed track laying
items.quote: Well, as a principle, we'd like to stick to the segments what are working and do more jobs going abroad, increase the footprint, etc. But we also can keep at it from the new segments like data center, green energy, renewable energy.

items.statement: Bangladesh transmission line project affected by political situation; work expected to restart from December after mobilization
items.quote: So hopefully, from December onwards we'll be able to start the work. And as a local competition, so far, we are okay. I mean, we don't see much of problem.

items.quote: Marine as I told you that, see, one of the marine job in Bangladesh, which was supposed to be done. We could not do much because of the political issue. So revenue has affected and accordingly margin also.

items.statement: Adani Group ownership expected to positively impact international expansion and domestic growth
items.quote: Definitely, it will impact positively. That's what I can say now.

items.quote: In fact, the fourth quarter onwards we are just hoping that we will get at least a 10% growth.

items.statement: Smart meter business expected to grow 70-75% YoY to Rs 70-75 crore in FY25 with continued growth for next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at about 70% to 75% growth in that area. And that is keeping in mind the business that we've done in these two quarters, this current quarter, as well as the next quarter, the Q3 and Q4 we expect to see a further growth of 10% to 15% from these previous two quarter.

items.quote: if the combination of both, the product will be in 50- 50% it will improve, improve further on, further here on. So today, if we are at 47-48% it should go up up to 50%.

items.quote: in shunt register, which is still an evolving application, based on which we try to get it reduced and keep it below 20% as an average.

items.quote: we have projects and plans in place for 25 calendar year, 25 and 26 where we'll be aggressively adding further capabilities in terms of testing equipment, you know, smaller prototype processes which replicate our production lines, and also, of course, manpower.

items.quote: they have been asking us to be prepared to supply 20% to 25% in some cases, higher than this year.

items.quote: Our gross margin has declined a little bit, which was in the last year, 21.68%, it goes down to 20.79% marginality of 89 bps.

items.quote: In H1FY25, our Shunt segment in India grew by 45.27%.

items.statement: US bimetal market still declining but expected to improve from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Most of this is coming from the decline of the US market, so that is still under decline at this point. We expect that to increase in the fourth quarter.

items.quote: in the last year we have done almost eight and a half percent. And this year, till compared to the six months, is around 13 and half percent.

items.statement: Metalor JV not proceeding in original structure due to high investment relative to returns; evaluating alternate arrangement
items.quote: the investments required were much higher than the kind of business or kind of, you know, the bottom line that it could eventually add so financially, it was not making as much sense, at least in the structure that was originally envisioned.

items.statement: Established wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy to engage European market directly, replacing retiring agent
items.quote: establishing a wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy this year is a significant step forward. This subsidiary will now allow us to engage directly with the market, bypassing intermediaries, and delivering products more efficiently and responsively.

items.statement: R&D spend currently ~1% of sales; targeting increase over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: currently we are at approximately 1% but we have projects and plans in place for 25 calendar year, 25 and 26 where we'll be aggressively adding further capabilities

items.quote: So no capex plan. We are already good on capacity for the next 3, 4 years. It's only after that, we will figure out whether we need more capacity expansion.

items.quote: Relating to the issue, as you know that they will take a good amount of time. And our request towards the business interruption loss has been put forth which we have placed with them, it is under process. Definitely, it will take some more time.

items.quote: The price at the growing market is between INR22.75 to INR23.50, depending on -- that's the average price, ballpark price is close to INR23, INR23.50.

items.quote: While we expect FY25 to be flat, we remain confident that our business will regain momentum from FY26 based on significant order pipeline and strong customer demand.

items.quote: The wage hike we have done, has a cumulative effect of about a 1.1%, somewhere in that zone, and that that takes us typically about two quarters to recover that.

items.statement: 0238 sugarcane variety reduced from 75% to 50% of crop; further reduction expected next year
items.quote: Last year, we were around 75%, and we have come to around 50% this year, and we expect a substantial reduction going forward next year.

items.statement: No further capex contemplated beyond ₹20 crore IMIL approval; CBG viability questioned due to press mud prices above ₹50/quintal
items.quote: So the only capex that has been approved by the Board in its board meeting yesterday was ₹20 -odd crore for the IMIL business. Be sides that, we are not contemplating any further capex at this particular point in

items.statement: Expect to maintain run rate of more than INR800 crores per quarter in remaining two quarters of FY25
items.quote: And on the revenue side, I think we should be able to maintain this run rate of more than INR800 crores going forward as well. So...

items.statement: Will announce expansion plans before FY25 ends; evaluating spinning and fabric capacity additions with focus on better margin products
items.quote: Definitely before this financial year ends, definitely we will come with something going forward as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margins running at 14-15% range for last 3 quarters; expect improvement in H2 but depends on cotton prices and demand
items.quote: If you see our last 3 quarters, we are running at near to the similar kind of EBITDA about -- in the range of about 14% to 15% is the EBITDA range, which we have been there.

items.statement: Domestic demand expected to improve in H2 due to winter and marriage season; export demand subdued but maintaining momentum via new markets
items.quote: And we expect that normally in second ha lf always we have better domestic demands due to the seasonal requirements of winter as well as the marriage season which happens

items.statement: Cotton-yarn spread currently INR90/kg; Indian cotton at 14-15% premium to NY futures; landed cost now at parity with imported cotton
items.quote: Yes, cotton to yarn spread is, as of today, is in the range of about, basic cotton to yarn is in the range of about INR90 a kg.

items.statement: Blended yarn reached 17-18% of total production; fabric exports 17-18% direct, rest via domestic exporters; knitted fabric utilization limited by margin threshold
items.quote: Blended has now reached nearly, out of our total production at this point of time, blended yarn has reached about 17%, 18% of our total capacity.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions suppressing global demand; Bangladesh transition smooth but ongoing issues; US tariff risk on China could benefit India
items.quote: But we have been able to maintain our momentum by exploring certain new markets as well as penetrating more with our existing customers.

items.statement: Gross debt INR1,180 crores; expect to repay INR90-100 crores in next two quarters; debt-equity improved to 0.97 from 1.17
items.quote: We have repayments of nearly INR90 crores to INR100 crores going in, in next six months. So, that should be there.

items.statement: Solar capacity at 18.8 MW (8-9% of power needs); grid cost INR7/unit vs solar INR3.50/unit; spent INR12-13 crores in H1 on solar
items.quote: I think last year we did, we had spent -- in the first half itself, again we have spent INR12, INR13 crores.

items.statement: Cotton procurement based on order book; imported cotton 25% of usage in last 6 months; may increase under advance license for exports
items.quote: So in last 6 months our utilization of imported cottons exceeded more than 25%. So this may still continue going forward looking to the prices which is there.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth guidance lowered to double-digit from 15%; EBITDA per kg expected around Rs. 38 for FY25
items.quote: Probably we are still aiming at double digit growth for the full year and probably the EBITDA average which is now currently at 36.73, probably it will land around 38.

items.statement: Paint segment volume growth expected 7-8% for FY25 vs earlier 10% target
items.quote: Paint this year will be we expected around 10% but I think we will end up somewhere at 7% to 8%.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth target 12-15% driven by ABG ramp-up and pharma scale-up
items.quote: Next year onwards we should be in the position to reach somewhere around 12% to 15% volume growth.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected Rs. 85-90 crore including Panipat, Cheyyar, pharma balancing and printing equipment
items.quote: Already Rs. 70 crores has been committed and we have some more printing and other equipment being ordered, which will arrive before March. So, the overall cost of investments could be in the region of Rs. 85 crores to Rs. 90 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated Rs. 50-60 crore, lower than FY25 as no greenfield projects
items.quote: Next year CAPEX may be limited to 50 crores to 60 crores as of today but we can only comment as we go towards the end of this year.

items.statement: ABG H1 volumes 1,500-1,600 tons; H2 expected 2,000+ tons; targeting 70% utilization of 5,000 ton initial capacity
items.quote: H1, maybe the volumes are around 1500 tons to 1600 tons. Probably in the second half, it may go to 2000 plus. So, we are online. About 70% of the capacity will be utilized.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg currently Rs. 36.73; target Rs. 40 by Q1 FY26 as capacity utilization improves
items.quote: I think we should be able to see that in the first quarter of next year itself. That is the Q1 of next year. It may inch towards 40. And overall, next year, we are aiming definitely for 40 as a minimum number to achieve.

items.statement: Paint realization down to Rs. 180-190/kg from Rs. 215/kg two years ago due to lower raw material prices and mandatory recycled plastic usage
items.quote: At that time, the raw material price went up to 120 -125. Currently the raw material price is around 105. More or less in this year, the price was stagnant there. And also, in the paint segment, like any other segment, RCP, that is recycled plastic usage has become mandatory.

items.statement: Pharma sales accelerating: Rs. 1 crore in Q2, Rs. 75 lakh in October alone; targeting Rs. 1-2 crore/month from January
items.quote: In the month of October , we did close to 75 lakhs sales in pharma alone and going forward the numbers will increase because now Marksans, MSN Labs, Graviti, Pulse. and also, Nutra Life and many other companies have cleared their audit and started taking our commercial line trials and small lot supplies.

items.statement: Pharma revenue target Rs. 30-50 crore for FY26; long-term opportunity Rs. 5,000 crore market
items.quote: At least we will see Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 50 crores. It could be 30 or 50. It all depends upon how products that are being launched we will be taking off.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Paint 47%, Lubes 20%, Food & Qpack 32.4%, Pharma 0.5%; IML share up to 72.57% from 66.7%
items.quote: In terms of revenue, 47% is from pain t, 20% lubes, food and Qpack together is around 32.4%, 0.5% is pharma.

items.statement: Mahad plant delayed due to local pollution approvals; supplying ABG from Satara for 2-3 quarters
items.quote: There are some issues related to local pollution and local approvals. They got delayed and that is why because the plant got delayed, ABG agreed supplies from Satara for next few quarters.

items.statement: Printing capacity constraints limiting IML development; consolidation to Sultanpur delayed to January 2025
items.quote: We have moved 70% of the machines but another 30% we are not in a position to move because of the i ncreasing demand for IML. And this will be able to do only in January once additional machines are received

items.statement: Asset turnover ratio currently below 2x due to high unutilized capex; target to exceed 2.5x as plants ramp up
items.quote: Our asset turnover ratio always used to be around 2-2.5, but currently it is low because of very high investments that have been made which are yet to become completely utilized. So, going forward, we should be able to cross to 2.5 asset turnover ratio.

items.statement: Panipat plant Qpack supplies started Oct-Nov; full IML food packaging from January; ice cream/dairy by March-April
items.quote: Just in the month of October and a little bit in November, we are making some supplies of Qpack from North. But the real quantities would start only by end of December. As I said, the printing consents will be coming out by end of this year, that is December and then we will be in a full-fledged way to provide the IML containers f rom January in the North also.

items.statement: FY2025 revenue target Rs.900 Crores; confident of exceeding it
items.quote: This time we have been cautious and we have set a target of Rs.900 Crores and we hope to cross Rs.900 Crores, but by how much, let us wait and see.

items.statement: Average 50% CAGR over next three years based on FY2025 figure
items.quote: With respect to the F Y2026 projection, we have said that we will have an average CAGR of 50% over the next three years and we are confident, given the huge order pipeline that we have, that we will be able to achieve the 50% average CAGR over the next three years, based on the 2025 figure

items.statement: Order pipeline Rs.3500 Crores; expect Rs.1200 Crores inflow by end of FY2025
items.quote: Even though the order pipeline is almost Rs.3500 Crores, we expect about Rs.1,200 Crores to come in by the end of this financial year, which we will be able to execute in the next year.

items.statement: FY2026 order inflow expected to be very big; order book upwards of Rs.2000 Crores to support 50% CAGR
items.quote: The order book should be upwards of Rs.2000 Crores if you want to achieve that. Again, we think that the order book in FY2026 is going to be really big for orders that we are expecting.

items.statement: US manufacturing setup estimated cost less than $10 million (~Rs.80 Crores) in FY2026
items.quote: We have estimated it should be less than $10 million, maybe about Rs.80 Crores or so. That will be the total expenditure that may happen for our setup and cost over the next it may be for the FY2026.

items.statement: Acquisition and capex budget Rs.400 Crores and less than Rs.100 Crores respectively
items.quote: Our budget has been about Rs.400 Crores for acquisition and capex would be less than Rs.100 Crores that is what the plan is.

items.statement: H1 FY2025 EBITDA margin 36.8% and PAT margin 28%; expect to maintain FY2025 guidance of 35% EBITDA and 25% PAT
items.quote: Despite the lower margin we were able to maintain our operational margin of 37% in H1, though the Q2, it is on a lower side but in H1 this operational EBITDA is around 36.80% which is above our guidance given for 35% and PAT is also 28%.

items.statement: Gross margin 50% in H1 FY2025 lower due to evolving new products, R&D allocation, geography and product mix
items.quote: You are correct that in H12025 our gross margin is 50% which is quite lower however it is partly offset from the benefit of scale of operations and despite the lower margin we were able to maintain our operational margin of 37% in H1.

items.statement: Order book split expected 40-60 between simulators and anti-drone systems
items.quote: We will not be able to exactly predict that at this point in time, but again, we expect a 40 -60 split to be there . Last year it was there and maybe probably that will continue in this year also.

items.statement: Anti-drone systems and remote control weapon stations seeing dramatic demand increase; surveillance systems also strong
items.quote: In terms of short -term pain everybody is feeling the pain of the drone attacks. The drones are becoming very, very severe problem. Drones with the AI -enabled remote control weapon stations and surveillance system is the complete solution that they are looking forward.

items.statement: US market entry expected to yield large orders from FY2027; could be 10-50% of revenue
items.quote: In FY2027, it could be as little as, about 10% to 15%, but it could go as high as 50 %. By the way, we have not factored this into our growth plans and this would be completely additional revenue that we will be getting.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in Indian defense orders; government committed to strengthening defense
items.quote: No, we do not see any slowdown in the defense orders. We expect the orders to come through, but definitely there may be some delay in action, but definitely not any complete elimination of the orders or anything like that.

items.statement: QIP of Rs.1000 Crores subscribed 5x; proceeds for acquisitions (Indian and overseas targets Rs.100-300 Crores typical size)
items.quote: Again, coming back to the fact that we have raised through a QIP Rs.1000 Crores it was subscribed more than five times, part of the proceeds we intend to deploy for acquisitions and we have in view both Indian and overseas targets. A typical size we are looking at is between Rs.100 to 300 Crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to improve to 160-170 days by end of FY2025 from ~200 days in H1
items.quote: Going forward, we can say that by end of this financial year, it will be again down to 160 to 170 days. This significant realization will happen in the current quarter.

items.statement: Barbarik remote control weapon station tested by Army; orders expected next year
items.quote: With respect to Barbarik the army has seen it, they have tested it and they have found it to be very useful. We expect requirements to come up in the next few months and we will be waiting for that.

items.statement: Management does not provide guidance for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We are not giving guidances.

items.statement: H2 FY25 domestic business expected to grow high single-digit, better than market in specialty
items.quote: We should do a high single -digit growth at least in H2.

items.statement: U.S. business H2 FY25 will be much stronger than H1 due to back-ended launches and market share ramp-up
items.quote: H2 will be much stronger for us compared to H1.

items.statement: ROW generics expected to grow 15-20% in H2 FY25 with strong order book
items.quote: I expect th at the H2 will remain at these similar levels 15% to 20% growth, at least, for the ROW business

items.statement: U.S. price erosion continues at high single digits to low double digits, no change in intensity
items.value: high single digits to low double digits
items.quote: it could be anywhere between high single digits to low double digits. That's what we're seeing in terms of the market.

items.statement: Gross margin comfortable at 72% ± range, depends on product mix and launches
items.quote: I think 72% ± is a good range to be in.

items.statement: R&D spend for FY25 revised lower to INR 500-520 crores from earlier INR 550 crores
items.quote: It will be a little bit on the lower side, w e would be closer to the INR500 crores, INR520 crores kind of

items.statement: Three major capex projects: domestic formulation facility near Indore (completion end FY25), peptide block at API facility, and two line extensions at F3 (one operational end FY25/early next year)
items.quote: We have 3 major projects around as of now in hand, one is a new formulation facility for domestic market, which is coming up near Indore. That should be completed by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting semaglutide and tirzepatide for GLP-1 portfolio; semaglutide launch will be late, not in first wave; in-house peptide manufacturing capability being built
items.quote: Yes. we will launch -- we will target semaglutide and tirzepatide both. There's still time of tirzepatide and the launch is still some time off. Sema, we will not be in the first wave, we will be a little late.

items.statement: API business degrew 15% due to price erosion and loss of key accounts; recovery expected by end of FY25 or FY26
items.quote: API business degrew by 15%. This is a trend that we've seen in the last couple of quarters. We've seen some price erosion in the API business and have lost some key accounts.

items.statement: API business loss due to competitors offering lower prices, Chinese aggression, and customers switching vendors for better pricing
items.quote: s just a matter of price erosion and competitors offering lower prices, and we moved some, I think. There are a few key accounts that we lost is built up which occurred, but we're seeing price erosion

items.statement: ROW business has strong order book supporting 15-20% growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: This has a strong order book, and I expect th at the H2 will remain at these similar levels 15% to 20% growth, at least, for the ROW business

items.statement: Filed 1 ANDA, received 9 approvals, launched 8 products in U.S. in Q2 FY25; plan ~10 launches in H2 FY25
items.quote: We filed 1 ANDA. We also received 9 approvals and launched 8 products in the U.S. during the quarter. And as I mentioned, we will launch about 10 products in H2 as well.

items.statement: ANDAs filing lag expected this year due to project push to complex and cost reduction; back to 15+ ANDAs from FY26
items.quote: From next year onwards, we will get back to the higher 15 -odd ANDAs that we've been filing.

items.statement: Working capital and debt elevated in Q2 due to inventory build for launches and dividend outflow; expected to normalize by end FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Probably that will be a close call. But going forward, if we talk of FY '26, I think we should be back to normal level

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of 1.7 GW peak as of 30 September 2024
items.quote: we have an unexecuted order book of 1.7 gigawatts peak

items.statement: Order book value roughly Rs 2,500-2,700 crore
items.quote: This would roughly now translate to around Rs. 2,700-odd crores, between Rs. 2,500 crores to Rs. 2.700-odd crores.

items.statement: Pipeline of 17.8 GW being chased
items.quote: our pipeline which you asked is now 17.8 gigawatts

items.statement: Expect to execute 1.2-1.3 GW from current order book in H2 FY25
items.quote: we are hopeful of around 1.2 gigawatts to 1.3 gigawatts

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at double-digit near 15% for current order book valid next 9-12 months
items.quote: our EBITDA margins at a sustainable level should be double-digit, almost near to 15% levels

items.statement: Government targeting 40-50 GW renewable procurement per annum; tenders coming up significantly
items.quote: government has committed that they will increase the business of renewable energy in terms of procurement of power up to almost 40 gigawatts to 50 gigawatts per annum

items.statement: No significant slowdown observed in sector investments from government or other parties
items.quote: We haven't observed any significant slowdown in this sector in terms of investments from the government or from other parties as well.

items.statement: Order book split 15-20% PSU, rest utility/rooftop/other; bulk is balance-of-system orders
items.quote: our current order book is between 15% to 20% in PSU side, and the rest is towards either utility scale or rooftop or other projects

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 587 MW; expect 2-3x growth next year onwards
items.quote: O&M is at 587 megawatts. Also, what happens is that when we undertake EPC clients, they give us, majority of them, not all of them, give us between three to five years of O&M. So, mostly once the projects gets completed next year we will see an uptick in O&M as well. And the company also keeps actively bidding for O&M customers outside. So, we are hopeful that this should also see a 2x to 3x growt

items.statement: No significant supply chain bottlenecks foreseen; domestic supply geared to meet requirements
items.quote: we are until now not foreseeing any significant bottlenecks towards that end as of now

items.statement: Business model requires only working capital; negative working capital cycle with 21-30 day collection vs 40-45 day payables
items.quote: Technically, our working capital cycle is, actually we have a negative working capital. It means we do not need capital to do this business.

items.statement: Advance payments 5-15% (thumb rule 10%); performance bank guarantees 10-15% (thumb rule 10%)
items.quote: advanced ranges hover between 5% to 15%, but thumb rule is 10%. And performance bank guarantees we have observed has been around 10% to 15%, thumb rule again 10%.

items.statement: Green hydrogen demand not yet scaled up in terms of orders; expecting it to scale up
items.quote: But from a demand perspective, we are expecting it to scale up. But as of now a significant demand on that front has not been scaled up in terms of orders.

items.statement: Hit rate on pipeline historically 25-30%; entire 17.8 GW pipeline up for bidding in H2
items.quote: Our hit rate in the past has been around 25%-odd, but depending upon which is numerator, and which is denominator, 25%, 30% has been our hit rate. The entire one is for the second half anyway

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY25 revised to early double-digits (11-12%) from earlier 20% revenue growth target
items.quote: Yes, early double-digits. Like I think 11%, 12% would be a good estimate.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA expected at Rs. 220-230 crores
items.quote: I think it should definitely be much higher than last year, there should be about Rs. 220 crores to Rs. 230 crores in Q4.

items.statement: FY25 capex revised to Rs. 720 crores (H1: Rs. 337 crores, H2: Rs. 377 crores)
items.quote: Yes, you are right, it's at about Rs. 720 crores, yes.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at Rs. 450-500 crores (Silchar Rs. 300 crores, Jorhat Rs. 100 crores, operational Rs. 100 crores)
items.quote: So, in total it is about Rs. 480 crores to Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Silchar grinding unit commissioning delayed to December 2026 from September-October 2026
items.quote: Now we are expecting it to commission by December '26. So, there is a two, three months delay.

items.statement: Jorhat grinding unit expected commissioning by FY27
items.quote: In Jorhat plant we are expecting by FY '27 and.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 per tonne EBITDA Rs. 995 vs Rs. 1,164 YoY; H1 FY25 Rs. 1,007 vs Rs. 1,176 YoY
items.quote: On per tonne EBITDA front it is Rs. 995 during this quarter, as against Rs. 1,164 per tonne same quarter last year.

items.statement: Northeast EBITDA per tonne Rs. 1,300; Outside Northeast EBITDA per tonne minus Rs. 200 in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA per tonne for Northeast was about Rs. 1,300 per tonne, and the EBITDA per tonne for outside Northeast was about minus Rs. 200.

items.statement: Northeast cement prices increased Rs. 10/bag QoQ; Outside Northeast (Bihar/Bengal) prices crashed and remain flat QoQ
items.quote: In the Northeast, the prices have increased by about Rs. 10 compared to the quarter too. So, in the Northeast the prices are a bit more stable than outside the Northeast.

items.statement: Current Northeast cement price ~Rs. 460/bag; expect Rs. 15-20/bag increase by December
items.quote: The current price in Northeast is about Rs. 460 per bag. And in November I do not see an increase in the pricing. But I think going ahead, hopefully, I think we should be, I think by December I think normally the prices do increase. So, we do see like a Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 scope of increasing prices.

items.statement: Fuel cost at Rs. 1.5 per GCV in Q2, expected to remain same in Q3/Q4 with possible reduction
items.quote: Yes, I think it probably will remain the same only. So, I think in Q1 also it was Rs. 1.5, right now also it's about Rs. 1.5. And I think it should remain Rs. 1.5 in the coming quarters as well. I think there could be some reduction but no increase.

items.statement: Northeast demand subdued in H1 due to low government spending; expect pickup from Dec-Jan with scheme rollouts
items.quote: So, basically the main problem at least in the North East was that the government expenditure in Northeast in the first half was a bit low, right, and because of that the demand was a bit subdued.

items.statement: New clinker plant (Line-3) stabilization delayed due to electrical panel faults; expect resolution by Nov 22, ramp-up to 7,000-7,500 TPD by end-Nov
items.quote: So, now on the 17th those panels will be received, and on the 22nd we will erect those panels. And I think after that we should have smooth functioning. So, this is broadly what it is.

items.statement: GST incentive booking low in Q2 (Rs. 37 crores) due to clinker plant issues; expect Rs. 50-60 crores/quarter in Q3/Q4
items.quote: But in whatever is left of Q3 and in Q4, we do expect a good generation of GST. The exact numbers I will quantify, and I will let you know. I will probably ask my CFO to get back to you. But I think about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores quarterly is what we expect in the coming quarters.

items.statement: AAC block plant in Guwahati to commission by early December 2024; eligible for central and state subsidies
items.quote: AAC block in Guwahati should be commissioned by December, in the first two weeks of December. And with that, we are also launching construction chemicals, right, so we will be getting into motor, waterproofing chemical and all these items.

items.statement: No disbursement targets given for current or next year; clarity expected in January (revised estimate) and February (budget)
items.quote: I will not be giving numbers but going forward I can assure you that our disbursement as well as the project sanction will pick up steadily.

items.statement: NTPC wagon leasing deal signed for Rs 700 crore (first tranche of 20 rakes, 15-year lease)
items.quote: That is 700 crores. This is just the beginning because this is the first time they have done a leasing model with us.

items.statement: Expanding beyond railways to forward/backward linkages in logistics and infra; targeting NTPC, petroleum companies for rolling stock leasing
items.quote: We are entering into arrangement to fund NTPC for purchase of their wagons which they use in the railway system for their coal logistics.

items.statement: Railway lending at 35-40 bps margin; non-railway lending expected at higher spreads (peers at 250-300 bps) to boost PAT
items.quote: Once we go outside this purview, we don't have that restriction. So obviously we will be doing the lending at a very attractive rate and try to be competitive than the

items.statement: Will maintain zero-NPA track record; building robust appraisal team with government and industry talent for prudent underwriting
items.quote: We are a zero-NPA company and would like to maintain that kind of good thing that we have with us that we remain there.

items.statement: Board and shareholders approved Rs 8 lakh crore total borrowing limit; current debt-to-equity at 7.83x, net worth over Rs 50,000 crore
items.quote: Our board and shareholders have already approved 8 lakh crores of total borrowing limit.

items.statement: No equity raise needed; capital adequacy over 700%, net worth growing annually, comfortable for growth
items.quote: there is absolutely no constraint for further growth and plus I will be adding to my net worth . Further, as you know since more than 99% exposure to M oR, m y capital adequacy is more than 700

items.statement: Lease rentals based on WACC plus risk pass-through (interest rate and currency variations); cost-plus model
items.quote: it's a cost-plus model. So, cost plus some of the risks are also p assed on. But you're right if cost is 7, then at 7.4 I will be calculating my lease rentals

items.statement: Railway disbursement paused for 6 quarters to cool debt-to-equity from ~9x to ~7.5x; discussions ongoing with MoR and MoF for renewed lending
items.quote: With very high and steep growth in its assets under management for 5 consecutive FYss, there was no disbursement in the last FY and current FY till now.

items.statement: Tax status: zero tax payment expected for next couple of years due to accumulated depreciation on lease assets including NTPC deal
items.quote: because of the accumulated depreciation and further depreciation on whatever financial leases we do subsequently will get dep reciation on that also. So, we don't see any tax payments coming for the next couple of years

items.statement: Provisioning for non-railway exposure at 0.4% (same as RVNL loan); minimal impact on profitability
items.quote: We are currently doing 0.4% for whatever funding we have done, for RVNL Loan, the same provisioning will do for this exposure also.

items.statement: Project lease structure: 15-year primary lease, 5-year moratorium, secondary lease reduced from 15 to 10 years (total 30 years)
items.quote: The primary lease period would be 15 years and in case of a project asset, secondary lease period will get reduced from 15 to 10.

items.statement: Management hopes muted demand streak ends in Q3 and industry reverts to normal growth rate
items.quote: Finally, we hope that this long streak of muted underlying demand situation comes to an end in Q3, and that the industry does a sharp reversal towards its normal growth rate.

items.statement: Water-based plant at Jodhpur expected to commission in Q2 FY26; solvent-based plant by Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; putty brownfield expansion by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The water-based new plant is expected to be commissioned sometime in Q2 of the next fiscal, while the solv ent-based plant, we are trying to get it up and running by the Q4 of this fiscal, at most, it may spill over to Q1 of the next fiscal

items.statement: Total capex outlay: water-based plant INR250-275 crores, solvent-based plant ~INR50 crores, putty brownfield expansion below INR15 crores
items.quote: The total capex outlay for the water-based plant that we are setting up is going to be somewhere around INR250 crores to INR275 crores. For the solvent-based plant, I believe, is about INR55 crores or something like that. Sorry, it's closer to INR50 crores. And for the brownfield expansion of the putty plant, it will be around below INR15 crores or so.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 44.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 45.7% in Q2 FY24; EBITDA margin 14.8% vs 15.2% YoY; PAT margin 8.2% vs 9.6% YoY
items.quote: As usual, we have maintained the pole position in terms of gross margin, which stood at 44.1%. The gross margins were sligh tly muted compared to the corresponding period of the previous year when we had recorded 45.7% in Q2 of last year

items.statement: Price cuts of ~4.5-5% in Q3/Q4 FY24; price hikes of ~1.5% in Q2 FY25; net pricing deficit of 3-3.5% YoY
items.quote: the price cuts that were taken in Q3 and Q4 of last year aggregated to somewhere around 4.5%, almost 5%, depending upon your product mix. And the price hikes that have happened in the quarter just gone by is at best 1.5%. So there is still a clear 3% to 3.5% deficit in pricing.

items.statement: Q2 opened with strong double-digit growth in July but August-September were a drag; low-demand scenario persisted in Q2
items.quote: Though this quarter, Q2, opened with strong double-digit growth for us in July, the months of August and September were a bit of a drag, which resulted in the streak of a low-demand scenario to continue in Q2 as well.

items.statement: Premium emulsion grew significantly faster than economy; waterproofing drove higher value vs volume growth in Primer/Distemper/Misc segment (13.7% value vs 7.1% volume)
items.quote: The Emulsion segment, which is the largest segment, also saw good growth, and premium segment of the emulsions grew at a significantly higher pace than the economy segment.

items.statement: Differentiated products collectively account for 30% of top line; putty >10% of top line; 65% of offerings don't require tinting machine
items.quote: Most of our differentiated products, which account collectively for 30% of our top line, they don't require tinting. Putty accounts for well over 10% of our top line

items.statement: Hamirpur plant revenue Rs. 50-60 crores in FY26, Rs. 70-80 crores from two blocks at full run-rate
items.quote: From our Hamirpur facility, next year we feel that we should be able to get around Rs.50 crores, Rs.60 crores.

items.statement: Formulation revenue growth target at least 20% per year
items.quote: Formulation growth also would be similar, at least 20% per year.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement sustainable at current levels if prices stable

items.statement: Expect to maintain 40% EBITDA margin for full financial year despite new center drag

items.quote: The B2C revenue stood healthy at 93%, and our radiology business stood at 35%.

items.quote: Because of that, there were multiple strikes. And even because of this Bangladesh issue, for some time, that market has suffered. So that's the only reason why almost for 20, 25 days, the business got hit in this market.

items.statement: EV revenue share at 4.1% for the period, up from ~4% previously
items.quote: Our EV shares of the revenue for the period is 4.1%.

items.quote: With some customers, it is at a quarterly lag, and with some customers, it is at a half yearly lag. So there could be impact on the P&L but that's more of a timing gap. Over a period of time, it really doesn't kind of impact our P&L in either way.

items.statement: Second greenfield plant delayed by 6 months by customer, SOP starting Q1 FY26

items.statement: 12 stores opened in H1 FY25 with total capital outlay of Rs 35 crores

Anyways the consumer offers now in India are much higher than the rest of the world. It can be lowered.

items.quote: Our ASP for H1 FY25 stood at Rs. 2,15,952 as compared to Rs 1.87 lakhs in H1 FY24. Share of luxury and high luxury watches for H1 FY25 stood at an all-time high.

items.quote: In our pre-owned segment, the certified pre-owned business, which is Second Movement, it has experienced a 25% year -on-year growth , reaching billings of Rs. 43 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Opportunity exists to open 20 stores per year for next 5 years; constrained by manpower and brand tie-ups
items.quote: But is there an opportunity in the next 5 years to open 20 stores a year, yes.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to be maintained at 30% irrespective of GST hike; management confident in ability to protect margins

items.quote: As I mentioned our SSG has been 15.5% in the last 6 months. Our goal is to increase our overall revenue, and our overall business will be 10times in 10 years. I think it will be a healthy mix of same store growth and new store addition.

items.quote: We have bid for a certain quantity of syrup based ethanol. We have also bid for B -Heavy ethanol and we have some quantities of C heavy ethanol with the private OMCs, the private oil marketing companies.

items.quote: Full year? Around INR 180 crores-INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Annual CAPEX and product development budget of Rs 300-400 crore.
