items.quote: In fact, every time we design a park, we always leave space for a resort. So, I think definitely it's part of our plan for most of our projects.

items.statement: Expansion to continue via long-term government leases where possible; not averse to buying land if lease rental and land cost are similar
items.quote: Wherever possible we would like to keep the CAPEX low and do the lease.

items.statement: Company has evaluated and passed on acquisition opportunities in last couple of years as they did not make financial sense
items.quote: Yes, we have already passed on. We have actually said no to most of it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided range 12% to 14% for Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA has also been in the guided range of 12% to 14%, coming at 12.6% for the quarter after investments, as Ravi was highlighting.

items.statement: Gross margin increased by nearly 100 basis points in Q2 FY25
items.quote: At the same time, we have also been able to deliver good increase in the gross margin by nearly 100 basis points.

items.statement: Core lubricant volume grew 8.8% YoY in Q2 FY25, 2-3x industry growth of 3-4%
items.quote: We have seen that in this quarter, there was some lingering effect of the elections and certain liquidity challenges, but given our strategies, we have posted strong volume numbers.

items.statement: Personal mobility mix increased ~2% to ~22% in Q2 FY25 driven by motorcycle growth
items.quote: In terms of personal mobility, we are higher by around 2%. In terms of industrial and others, we are lower by 2% So more or less in that range.

items.quote: Also considering that our capex requirement for lubricant business also is around INR20 crore, INR25 crore-INR30 crore annually.

items.quote: For Q2 FY '25, it was around INR14 crore, and for the H1 FY'25, it is around INR24 crore-INR25 crore, which in the last full year turnover was around INR24 crore-INR25 crore for Tirex.

items.quote: However, this was a seasonally impacte d quarter as Ravi highlighted already. During monsoon season, obviously, the movement of trucks and CVs, which is the large consumption segment is relatively lower

items.quote: We have been currently paying out roughly 55%, 60% as dividend payouts. That we have increased over the last two, three years from 35%, 40% to now 55%, 60%.

items.quote: Yes, I think we are now at around 6% -7% in terms of our export as a percentage. While earlier it used to be 3%-4% and then we stabilized around 5%. Now it has gone to 6%-7%.

items.quote: We have already guided that our usual advertisement is in the range of 3% to 4%, as Ravi highlighted. In a normalized way, we would be towards the lower end of this band.

items.statement: B2B industrial lubricants growing double-digit; market share <5% but expanding with manufacturing growth
items.quote: This business has been growing double -digit volume for us. Obviously, we have certain strengths which we have in each of the

items.quote: we have had to store higher inventory because as I was mentioning in one of the earlier questi ons, some of the refineries where we have a term contract, were going for a maintenance shutdown during October, November we had to prebuy some of the

items.quote: We continue to focus on our premium range of products. And again, we are happy to share that this has contributed to the overall kitty by notching up double the growth rate.

items.quote: I think it's going to be still single-digit volume even if it goes to its maturity.

items.statement: Tirex targets INR500-700 crore revenue in 5 years; EBITDA neutral to marginally positive in FY25
items.quote: We will be obviously aiming to double the top line every year at least for the next three, four years. That's where we believe, and we have announced in the past also that we want to take this company at least to INR500 crore to INR 700 crore top line in the next five years.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 800-1,000 crores
items.quote: No, we'll be incurring the capex will be around INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance revised to 5-6% range going forward
items.quote: I think our EBITDA margins would be in the range of 5% to 6% now going forward.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 5-7% YoY for FY25 subject to price volatility
items.quote: I think last time also, we gave a guidance of around 5 to 7 percentage. We stick to that guidance, subject to the price volatility and the demand increase, which is going to happen based on that.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex was INR 330 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, the company invested close to INR 130 crores into the gas infrastructure, aggregating to INR 330 crores up to the half year of this financial year.

items.statement: Morbi market size estimated at 7.5-8 mmscmd, current consumption ~6.5 mmscmd including propane
items.quote: The market size would be around 7.5 to 8 mmscmd. And right now I think because of various issues in Middle East and all, I think, the consumption would be close to 6.5 mmscmd, including propane consumption.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA per SCM at INR 6.86 vs INR 6.14 in Q2 FY24
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA per SCMD, it stands at close to INR 6.86 against INR 6.14 in the previous quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Industrial prices increased by ~INR 2/SCM in Q2 due to LNG price rise from $9.5 to $13/MMBtu
items.quote: During the quarter, we had to increase the industrial prices by approximately INR 2 per SCM. The increase was mainly on account of significant increase in LNG prices. The spot LNG prices were around $ 9.50 per MMBtu in April 2024 and the current prices is approximately $ 13 per MMBtu.

items.statement: Evaluating CNG price increase to offset higher gas procurement costs from APM cut
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating options to increase the CNG prices in near future to basically offset the increased cost of gas procurement.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 Morbi volume expected at 3.5-4 mmscmd, up from 2.86 mmscmd in Q2
items.quote: I think in quarter 3, we are looking at a growth of around 3.5 to 4 mmscmd.

items.statement: CNG sales grew 12% YoY in Gujarat and 25% YoY outside Gujarat in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, CNG sales in Gujarat increased by 12% year-over-year, while outside Gujarat sales surged by 25% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: CNG and domestic share in portfolio increased from <20% to >40% over last few years
items.quote: See, I think if you look at the last few years, the growth of CNG and the domestic has increased in our portfolio from close to less than 20%, it is more than now 40 percentage.

items.statement: APM gas allocation cut from 74% to 50% in Q2, being replaced by new well gas and spot LNG
items.quote: So for the quarter ended September '24, we were getting I mean, the shortfall was approximately 26% which was being fulfilled through spot. So -- and after that there has been a further reduction in APM gas. The reduction is now approximately 50%.

items.statement: BG and other long-term LNG contracts expiring mid-2025, replacement discussions ongoing
items.quote: So that LNG contract will expire somewhere in the middle of 2025. And we are right now in discussions for a new LNG contract to replace those volumes.

items.statement: FDODO scheme: 400 LOIs issued, 125 accepted with bank guarantees, construction starting Dec 2024
items.quote: We have issued nearly 400 LOIs, out of which 125 have been accepted by the applicants. And apart from that, they have already submitted the bank guarantee of INR10 lakhs for those LOIs from those 125 locations. The way things are going, I think we will start on the action and will start sometime in the first week or maximum second week of December for the construction of the stations.

items.statement: Delhi High Court stay order obtained against PNGRB common carrier regulations for 20 GAs
items.quote: What we have done as GGL management is we have immediately moved Delhi High Court again and obtained a protection order, a favorable order from Delhi High Court. So this prevents PNGRB from taking any coercive action against GGL.

items.statement: LNG trucking: LCNG at 4 stations, surveying routes to major ports and expressways for LNG dispensing
items.quote: We are already supplying LCNG at 4 of our stations where we are converting LNG into CNG and supplying to the customer. So we are in the process of setting up a dispenser at these 4 stations. So we can start LNG dispensing also at these stations.

items.statement: Matchmaking billing expected to return to growth levels in Q3; both billing and revenue growth expected to move to better levels in Q4
items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for Q3, the matchmaking billing expect to come back to the growth levels in Q3. However, there will be revenue decline due to the muted billing growth in Q2. In Q4, we expect both billing and revenue growth to move to a better levels.

items.statement: Marriage services expected to be at similar level as Q2
items.quote: Marriage services, we expect to be at a similar level of Q2.

items.statement: Profit after tax expected to be lower than Q3 of last year due to investments in new areas
items.quote: On the outlook for Q3 margins, we expect the profit after tax to be lower than the levels of Q3 of last year due to the investments in the new areas.

items.statement: Expect volume growth and some marginal increase in ARPU from Q4 onwards
items.quote: We may expect some increase in ARPU possibly from Q4 onwards and volume may also increase. But we are not giving a number at this point in time.

items.statement: Matchmaking EBITDA margin at 22.6% in Q2, same as Q1 and up from 21.3% a year ago
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the matchmaking business in Q2 is at 22.6% same as in Q1 and increased as compared to 21.3% a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 15.2% in Q2 vs 16.7% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margins in Q2 are at 15.2% compared to 16.7% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago.

items.statement: Profiles have started bouncing back; increase in fresh payments seen in October and November; renewal payments expected to bounce back from Q4
items.quote: The good thing is that the profiles have bounced back and even in the month of October, there is an increase in fresh payment, even in the month of November as we speak there is an increase in the first-time payment. But the renewal may take one more quarter because since we are two quarters of decline, it may take one more quarter to bounce back.

items.statement: Investing in northern markets with Anil Kapoor as brand ambassador for Community Matrimony and Great Indian Matchmaking Fest campaign
items.quote: We have also taken Anil Kapoor as a brand ambassador exclusively for the northern and western markets. So, we intend to invest in northern market in particular.

items.statement: Fraud and fake profiles remain a challenge though numbers are minuscule; no foolproof mechanism exists yet
items.quote: However, the numbers are minuscule, it's a concern, it's one of the challenges the industry is grappling with. So, not only in online matrimony, the online industry is facing various forms of fraud. So, there are challenges in our categories about these kinds of frauds and all the things. We need to figure it out.

items.statement: Created about 30,600 plus success stories in Q2
items.quote: We create about 30,600 plus success stories.

items.statement: Marketing expenses for matchmaking optimized to 45.2 crores in Q2 from 47.1 crores in Q1 and 46.1 crores a year ago
items.quote: Marketing expenses for matchmaking in Q2 is at 45.2 crores as compared to 47.1 crores in Q1 and 46.1 crores a year ago. So, you would have observed we have optimized the marketing expenses a bit in this quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance at 379 crores, declined slightly from Q1 due to dividend payout
items.quote: Our cash balance is at 379 crores, declined slightly as compared to Q1 due to the dividend payout.

items.quote: ROCE annualized is at about 13%.

items.quote: Today, we have a presence in eight airports across India for EliteMatrimony and we are definitely looking Matrimony.com November 07, 2024 at EliteMatrimony as you rightly said, the premium segment is an opportunity though it's small at this point of time. items.quote: Basically, the board evaluates the various ways to reward the shareholders, and so these are the second buyback and we discussed with the board and we thought it's better to set at certain second premium and it was a board decision on the buy back.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit healthy revenue growth in FY26 versus FY25 driven by export order execution and growth in other streams.

items.quote: So, in the range of about 20-21% and this would be the range the range of EBITDA and about 15 to 16% of PAT margin moving forward even on a FY basis.

items.quote: Our order book of export as it stands now is about `1300 odd crore and we expect that this will start fetching revenue by early next FY.

items.quote: At PBDIT levels also, we see basically almost 480 bps points, which is coming in from a larger quantum of Q2. The good part is that in terms of the PBDIT margins, we are still in that range of about 18.5%.

items.statement: Took 1.2% price increase in Q2 FY25; full realization expected in Q3
items.quote: Overall, we have taken a price increase of 1.2% in this quarter. But I think the full realization of this price increase will come in Q3.

items.statement: Raw material inflation of 1.5% in Q2 FY25 vs 4% deflation in Q2 FY24
items.quote: If you see Q2FY24, we had deflation of about almost 4%. If you look at the current quarter, we had an inflation of about 1.5%.

items.statement: Urban demand stressed; rural recovering; Q3 challenging due to high base; improvement expected from late November
items.quote: Right now, you know we are sitting on a higher base of Q3 overall, given the fact that last year there was a late Diwali and October was a full month. So October has been also a little bit challenging and therefore we are not seeing too much immediate recovery in Q3, but there is a good wedding season in the offing and we will have to see how the demand really goes up from the third week of Novemb

items.statement: Good monsoon and rising government infrastructure spending should aid demand in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: The good part is that we have had good monsoons, and we are also seeing government spending go up with respect to the overall infrastructure market. Therefore, coupled with this, these two factors should really start aiding the overall demand, both in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Product mix weaker in Q2 FY25; economy segment seeing intense competition
items.quote: Also, the product mix this year has been weaker and we have seen material inflation in the current year.

items.statement: New products contribute 12% of revenue; Advance range targets 15-30% of qualified dealer sales
items.quote: And we see that today 12% of the revenue contribution still comes from new products and this is something which we are continuing taking forward in a very strong way.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion capex complete; backward integration projects (VAM-VAE at Dahej, white cement at Fujairah) on track
items.quote: Most of the capex which we had committed for brownfield expansion projects is now complete. Now we are looking at all our backward integration projects, which seem to be online. Whether it was the VAM-VAE which we are doing at Dahej in Gujarat or the white cement in Fujairah, Dubai. I think these projects are also well on track.

items.statement: Industrial business grew ~6% in Q2 FY25; PPG JV grew 6% in Q2, 8% in H1; Protective paints JV grew 6% in Q2, 3% in H1
items.quote: If you see from the point of view of PPGAP, which is the auto OEM and the refinishes business which we have, we got almost about 6% overall growth at the quarter level and about 8% at the H1 level.

items.statement: Impairment of ~₹200 cr on White Teak and Weatherseal goodwill and derivatives due to slower growth and bottom-line erosion
items.quote: Therefore, I think we have taken an impairment, which is totalling up to almost about ₹ 200 crores. And this is also covering the fair valuation loss on the derivative contracts for future stake purchases in White Teak and Weatherseal which are in the offing.

items.statement: ₹56 cr forex loss in Ethiopia due to currency devaluation
items.quote: Another exceptional item is the forex loss in Ethiopia, where we are seeing almost about ₹ 56 crores impact which has come in given the significant currency devaluation which has happened.

items.statement: Interim dividend of ₹4.25 declared, lower than last year due to reduced H1 profits
items.quote: We have looked at really calibrating the overall dividend for the year. We have got a dividend of about ₹4.25. This is a little bit lower than what we gave as an interim dividend 24 | P a g e last year, but this is in line with the reduced profits in the first half of the year

items.statement: Guidance is flattish for FY25 with 3-4% top-line growth and margins similar to last year
items.quote: So, the guidance was flattish guidance. So we said at the top line level, maybe 3% - 4% we are in kind of, we are okay on that, margins obviously there will be some margin made up in Q3 and Q4 but, obviously margins are under a bit of pressure.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA was ₹270-272 cr vs ₹205 cr in H2 FY24; aim to recoup lost ground in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, if you break the previous financial year into H1 and H2, out of the ₹ 477 crores of EBITDA we did ₹ 270 crores or ₹ 272 crores in H1 and we did ₹ 205 crores in H2.

items.statement: Agrochemical investments dried up; muted for a few more quarters. Pharma picking up in India with large projects. Chemical cycle turn expected in a couple of quarters
items.quote: We have seen a shortfall and where we do see a little bit more stress in the glass lined business, especially when it comes to the chemical. And when I say chemical, mainly the agrochemical sector where the investments have really dried up and it does mean that there is probably a few more quarters of, I would say muted investment.

items.statement: Mixing ~10% of H1 FY25 revenue; Heavy Engineering, Edlon, Mixing growing double-digit; non-glass-lined making up glass-lined shortfall
items.quote: 10% is the number that we have currently in terms of mixing. And mixing is an area where we want to grow. So there is a big push for us to kind of get into new industry segments.

items.statement: Glass-lined pricing stabilized after 10-15% discount increase; attempting to raise prices slowly via differentiation
items.quote: I would say the discount levels have increased by about 10%-15% little bit more in some cases, it would probably been a little bit more than that but now we are at about a 10%-15%.

items.statement: Relighted capex for Edlon to increase capacity for semiconductor demand; first equipment made in Poland for European sourcing
items.quote: We have actually kind of relighted a little bit of capex for them to increase capacity, because the market is moving and the semiconductor space in the US is doing quite well.

items.statement: Agrochemical downturn may last a couple more quarters; chemical/agrochemical visibility low; competitive pricing pressure persists
items.quote: I don't see the green shoots yet, I do see some talk happening in terms of new investment coming in like I said in the pharmaceutical industry, we do see positivity, but chemical and agrochemical in particular seem to be a little bit more time before we see a complete turnaround.

items.statement: Hired head of mixing globally; mixing group defined 3-year strategy; plan to share details in next investor call
items.quote: Last week, we had the entire mixing group from across geographies, the Canadians, the Indians and the French sitting in the room, 26 of them defining their strategy and building their plan for the next three years.

items.statement: Poland facility operational; first two equipment for Mavag passed FAT; lower cost than Western Europe, skilled workforce available
items.quote: We made the first set of two equipment for Mavag our swiss subsidiary, and the FAT was actually done a couple of days ago, and the results were quite encouraging.

items.statement: Targets $200 million revenue by calendar year 2027, approximately two financial years from now
items.quote: We are hoping that the economy is going to be opening up. Interest rates will open up and like Srini said taxation will be reduced. That means that there will be quicker acceleration in the initial phases, like Srini was talking about. So, our thing is we have set ourselves certain targets for next year and in line with whatever we are progressing now, we will be on a similar path to get to the 20

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to improve significantly over the next few years through customer consolidation and bench realignment
items.quote: We anticipate that the EBITDA numbers are going to be much better than where we are today for the next following years.

items.statement: Four to five deals delayed by US election uncertainty expected to close in Q3 FY25 and start before December holiday season
items.quote: There were about four or five opportunities that we were going to sign last quarter, but due to the uncertainty of the elections and so on, customers have pushed them to the right. So, we expect to close all of them in this quarter and hopefully start some of them before the holiday season in December.

items.statement: Expects initial US economic growth under Trump presidency to drive IT spending acceleration starting calendar year 2025
items.quote: Initial buoyancy will start the calendar year I want to say 2025. I want to make sure that I'm differentiating between the financial year and the calendar year when the Trump presidency takes off.

items.statement: Europe remains a headwind with flat growth due to Ukraine war impact and shrinking economy
items.quote: Europe is still struggling, right, while we're still struggling, we don't know when it's going to come out of it. The baggage of Ukraine, how long it will continue in Europe, we don't know. We've been, for lack of a better word, on a flat line when it comes to Europe.

items.statement: Strategy to reduce number of customers while increasing per-customer revenue to lower overheads
items.quote: We are also targeting this is something that for the financial year, we are looking at and we have given a target to all our CEOs operations, sales related leadership that we want to reduce the number of customers while increasing per customer revenue.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.1%, H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin of 12.1% and the net profit of 19.6 crores. The PAT margin for this quarter is 7.2% and the EPS for this quarter is of Rs. 2.6.

items.statement: Promoter stake reduced from 51.68% to 40.82% due to share sales and ESOP dilution
items.quote: We did some selling of our shares last quarter. That's the partial reflection of that and partial reflection is related to some of our reporting requirements we have done. Other than that there's nothing else.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth expected to be flattish due to H1 volume loss
items.quote: It would be flattish because it will take time to cover up the 6-month sales and volume loss.

items.statement: Sparx category revenue growth targeted at 8-10% for FY25-26
items.quote: And we are hoping that we can grow around 8% to 10% in Sparx category.

items.statement: Overall revenue growth expected to be positive but no specific target given
items.quote: Difficult to say as of now, but definitely it should be positive.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 capex expected at INR 100 crores plus, split across halves
items.quote: FY25, already we have spent around INR 50 crores. So, it will b e again in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores in next half. So, total will be INR 100 crores plus in this full year

items.statement: Advertisement spend reduced to 3% of revenue for FY25 from usual 4%
items.quote: Generally, we used to spend around 4%. So this year, we have just thought about 3%, 1% lower than last year.

items.statement: Ad spend expected to return to 4% in FY26
items.quote: Next year, definitely. Not this year. Next year, definitel y, we will review, and we may go back to the original percentage spend

items.statement: No price increase taken in Q2 FY25; ASP rise due to January hike and premium mix
items.quote: No, no, we have not taken price increase.

items.statement: Demand subdued in Q2 and October; expecting improvement in November-December wedding season
items.quote: Currently, like in October or whatever, you can see the start, we have not seen a great start. So we are hoping that because of this November-December having a huge number of weddings, so demand should improve.

items.statement: Closed footwear mix unchanged from last year; focusing on distributor and e-commerce expansion
items.quote: So it's same like what it was th e last year and last quarter. T here's not much of a change happening there

items.statement: Creating separate e-commerce portfolio to manage channel conflict and discounting
items.quote: So we are now creating separate portfolio for e-commerce. That is the thing, that in total, I mean, kind of conflicting and not complementary but sometimes totally opposite.

items.statement: Unorganized competition intensified due to lower raw material prices, GST change, BIS exemption for small players, and Chinese imports
items.quote: Yes, it's actually both. Plus 2 years back, there was a change of GST from 5% to 12%. Since then, like a lot of new players or unorganized competitors have come up.

items.statement: BIS compliance exemption for small players creating unethical competition
items.quote: Yes, that could be a reason because all small manufacturers, th ey are exempt from Quality Control standards. So whatever quality they want to produce, they can downgrade and they can cause unethical competition also

items.statement: Retail network expanded from 55,000 to 70,000 retailers over 2 years; same run rate to continue
items.quote: if you see 2 years back, we were at 55,000. Now we are at 70,000 retailers. So, it's a continuous activity, continuous process.

items.statement: Inventory increased by INR 47 crores due to subdued demand and factory utilization
items.quote: Due to subdued demand, and we have to run the factories and bec ause there is pressure on the demand, that's why inventory has increased

items.statement: Credit growth guidance maintained at 12%-14% on conservative basis despite current 18% run-rate
items.quote: Our guidance is 12%-14%, right. And if you look at within the credit growth, our RAM growth is always around more than 18%; almost 18%.

items.statement: Slippage guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY25 despite elevated Q2 slippages from MTNL account
items.quote: overall we have given a guidance of 1.25pc, 1-1.25pc. I believe, in the remaining half, we will be able to maintain because out of June 24 quarter, slippages of around 400 crores, 144 crores has already been recovered and upgraded.

items.statement: IT and digital transformation budget of ₹1,000 crore approved for FY25 with ₹360 crore already spent
items.quote: we have already got board approval for 1000 plus crore for this year, which include digitization of our products, bringing new technologies also, even replacing our old hardware also

items.statement: NARCL resolution pipeline of 4 accounts worth ₹610 crore under Swiss challenge process
items.quote: there are already 4 accounts are there where bids are submitted by NARCL and now it is the Swiss challenge, and everything has to happen and 4 accounts where bids are submitted are is 610 crores.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.10% from 2.84-2.86% range through portfolio rebalancing toward retail/MSME and selective corporate lending
items.quote: Overall NIM which used to hover around 2.84 to 2.86 has now touched 3.10. and what we have done to achieve this level is we have rebalanced our credit portfolio.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced from 4.91% peak in Dec'23 to 4.86% by reducing bulk deposit reliance and using TREPS market
items.quote: Our cost of deposit peaked in December ’23 it was 4.91 now it is 4.86. Our cost of deposit has started coming down because we h ave reduced our reliance on the bulk

items.statement: Vehicle loan growth accelerating sequentially: 39% in Q2 FY25 vs 33% in Q1 vs 30%/27%/23% in prior quarters
items.quote: our vehicle loan growth is more than 39% in this quarter, previous quarter it was 33%, prior to that it was 30%, 27 and 23.

items.statement: Corporate book reshuffled from AAA to AA/A rated exposures for better yield and cross-sell; AAA exposure reduced ~₹2,000 crore, AA exposure increased ~₹4,000 crore
items.quote: we would love to go for A and double A to maximize not only on yield front but also on the cross -selling of the products. So as soon as we get the opportunity, we will continue to grow in these 2 segments.

items.statement: MTNL exposure of ₹245 crore slipped to NPA; 50% provision made in Q2, additional provisioning planned for Q3
items.quote: We had one account MTNL. Let me tell you honestly and around 245 crores was the exposure. Because of that, for this quarter, our slippages are little elevated but overall we have given a guidance of 1.25pc, 1-1.25pc.

items.statement: ECL implementation impact estimated at ₹2,000-3,000 crore over 5 years; ₹1,000 crore forward-looking provisions already held
items.quote: Roughly I take, let us say for our bank size, maybe 2000 or 3000 crores is the hit. Let us say 3000. So, 1000 crores, we have already provided for, I think that is taken care, 1/3rd is already taken care.

items.statement: Capital raise of up to ₹2,000 crore approved; launch timing by end of Q3 FY25 or early Q4 FY25 depending on market conditions
items.quote: Capital raising, we have already taken approval, and we have already today we had the kickoff meeting also with our BRLM and statutory auditors and legal counsels and now we are planning for the launch.

items.statement: 130 new branches planned for FY25; 27 operational as of Nov 4, 100 locations approved, all targeted by March 2025
items.quote: We have planned to open around 130 branches in this financial year. About 100 locations have been approved by our HOPC Committee - HO Premises Committee, of which 27 branches have been made operational as on 4th November

items.statement: Project Parivartan targets 25 digital products by March 2025; Tab Banking deployed at 1,700 branches for quality CASA acquisition
items.quote: We have planned to launch around 25 products by March. We have already launched at the time of launching of this project and others are in pipeline.

items.statement: Daily active mobile users grew from 500-600 to 7,000-8,000; daily logins from <1 lakh to >3 lakh in one year
items.quote: On an average , active mobile customer addition in June quarter was 500 -600. Now, it is in the range of 7000-8000 on a daily basis. That is what. Our daily login used to be less than a lakhs about a year back, now it is more than 3 lakhs every day on an average.

items.statement: Recovery from written-off accounts expected at ~₹667 crore in H2 FY25, similar to H1 FY25 run-rate
items.quote: See, if you look at recovery in return of account during this half year was 667 crore, half year and similar amount we are expecting in this remaining half year also

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 17.9%, up 140 bps QoQ and 270 bps YoY (excl. one-time fee)
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA was 17.9% compared to 16.5% last quarter and 15.2%, excluding that onetime fee in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA net of RSU cost at 16.1% vs 14.7% last quarter
items.quote: EBITDA, net of RSU spend, is 16.1% as against 14.7% last quarter.

items.statement: No quantitative guidance provided; management expects volume growth momentum to continue in Q4 but revenue conversion dampened by furloughs and fewer working days
items.quote: Q4 always has a seasonal impact because of furloughs, because of holidays and also a lower number of working days. So one, we believe that the growth momentum should continue. So, growth momentum in terms of volumes will definitely happen. That volume, translating into revenue, will be dampened by the lower number of working days and furloughs.

items.statement: Seeing increased sales activity, pipeline growth, higher average deal sizes, and improved spending intent across sectors for 2025
items.quote: We've seen traction begin across all sectors now. As the year is coming to a close and also US elections behind us, there are definite signs that customers are plan ning to spend more in the coming year

items.statement: Telco and tech sectors showing early signs of spending revival after cost-cutting phase
items.quote: Tech was the biggest impact or highest impacted, and where we are seeing some of the tech spend come back, telcos following behind. So, the signs of while the discussions have started, some of the deal activity signs will probably start off and start showing up.

items.statement: No billing rate increases; margin improvement driven by utilization and operating efficiency, not pricing
items.quote: No, the market environment wasn't going to support the rate increase. In fact, in the last couple of earnings calls, there were questions around whether we have given discounts to our customers. Given the nature of our services in the product implementation and product engineering space, we haven't offered discounts to our cus tomers. But on the contrary, we have not increased or we've not been ab

items.statement: Average deal size increasing quarter-on-quarter; pipeline composed of larger deals
items.quote: Anmol, we are definitely seeing our average deal size go up , quarter-on-quarter. We are also tracking it at pipeline level. And we are seeing that in our pipe, also, we are getting more number of larger deal sizes.

items.statement: Product sustenance deals emerging; targeting multi-year portfolio management engagements
items.quote: Absolutely, Sandeep. Though not v ery big numbers, but we have seen a couple of deals in the last quarter in the product sustenance space. We are currently in active conversations with at least another few customers who are talking, basically, product sustenance, the whole product portfolio management type of approach that we had talked about at some point with you as well

items.statement: Adding delivery capacity in data, cloud, AI, security; hired global delivery head; opened Mexico nearshore center
items.quote: There certainly are and we are willing to add bandwidth and employees in data, cloud, AI. And also a bunch of our specialized areas around security and similar services.

items.statement: No single client-specific concern entering CY2025; top clients stable with expected spend recovery
items.quote: So is there a singular client -centric issue that we are worried about? The answer is no. Our top clients are largely sustained and, in fact, some of whom we've seen either stagnate or not grow year-on-year. We do believe that growth with the spending will come back even in those clients.

items.statement: Sales headcount ~60 core sellers + 55-60 ISRs; flat YoY with slight ISR reduction
items.quote: Our hardcore sales team excluding the ISR would be close to around 60 resources, Nitesh Ji, excluding the ISRs? Nitesh Bansal: Yes. Mihir: Sorry, how much? Nand Sardana: 60 is the hardcore sales guys who are at o n-site location and additional 55 to 60 ISR support them in the sales lead generation, and they support from NOIDA during the night

items.statement: Sustainable margin trajectory expected despite planned sales and delivery investments
items.quote: Yes, we are very conscious of it, and we do believe that we will maintain a sustainable margin trajectory.

items.statement: Win ratios pressured industry-wide due to delayed customer decisions
items.quote: Number one, from a win ratio perspective, our win ratio for anyone, actually, across the industry, you would see, it would have gone down because there are a lot more deals which are undecided, where cu stomers have delayed decisions

items.statement: Service mix shifting to higher-value digital product engineering, data, AI, cloud; Southeast Asia revenue share up to 14.2%
items.quote: Southeast Asia has done much better and gone from 12.9% to 14.2% , which is also largely reflective of how the economies in these regions have performed, where North America and Europe had been slow, but Southeast Asia had been doing well.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin reached 10.2% in Q2 FY25, up 305 bps QoQ and 242 bps YoY, and management expects it to remain at double-digit levels
items.quote: operational EBITDA, which has now crossed double digit and is at 10.2%, up by around 305 basis points quarter -on-quarter and 242 basis points with corresponding quarter

items.statement: Management confirms double-digit EBITDA margin achieved in Q2 FY25 is sustainable going forward
items.quote: We have already hit double -digit EBITDA margin in this quarter. And we feel that this should remain and

items.statement: No plans to expand vanillin capacity beyond current 6,000 tonnes; focus is on optimizing existing capacity first
items.quote: At present, we will first utilize what the capacity we had of 6,000. We will optimize that and then later on -- at this moment of time, we don't have any plans to enhance the vanillin capacity.

items.statement: Vanillin capacity utilization at 40% currently, targeting 55% run-rate by end of FY25, 75% by FY26, and 100% in following years
items.quote: currently, we are at about 40%, which, by end of FY '25, we should be hitting closer to -- on a run rate basis, closer to 55% or so. The idea is, by FY '26, we should be at least 75% capacity utilization, and following years, to take it up to 100%.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty final orders expected by May-June 2025 (US) and April-May 2025 (Europe); interim orders by November-December 2024; no long-term contracts being signed until duties crystallize
items.quote: First round is end of November in the U.S., and by April -- by May of next year, US will finalize completely. Right now, they will have interim, and then the final order is by May.

items.statement: Heliotropin production shifted from China to India due to anti-dumping risks; China manufacturing business fully shut down
items.quote: we had a relook at the heliotropin project out of China because of all these antidumping actions being taken by US and Europe. So at the appropriate time, we will be setting up the capacity in India for heliotropin

items.statement: Europe blending revenue INR18 crores this quarter (~INR100 crores annual run-rate); targeting loan restructuring with banks to stretch repayments over longer period
items.quote: At present in this year also without -- this quarter also without diphenol business, we had an INR18 crores of turnover in Europe. And on a yearly basis, we have been doing a blending turnover of near to INR100 crores in Europe.

name: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

items.statement: Won 8 of 13 TBCB projects in Q2 (78% by annual tariff, 75% by NCT cost, 62% by number) including Khavda-Nagpur HVDC and RE evacuation lines
items.quote: We have become L-1 bidder in TBCB projects in Q2. Total, 8 numbers projects we have won out of 13 projects which includes 78% in terms of annual tariff, 75% in terms of NCT cost and about 62% in terms of numbers.

items.statement: Won 4 of 6 projects in October-November including Shongtong Karchham Wangtoo, Bikaner Rajasthan Part A & B, and Kudankulam transmission system
items.quote: And till date, we have again won in October and November. Out of 6 projects, we have won 4 projects. That includes Shongtong Karchham Wangtoo in Himachal Pradesh, then in Bikaner, Rajasthan. Then another Part A, Part B in Rajasthan. Then Kudankulam transmission system.

items.statement: Capex up to September 2024 was Rs 10,002 crore; capitalization was Rs 4,000 crore
items.quote: Our CapEx, up to September, 2024, was ₹10,002 crores and on capitalization ₹4000 crore worth projects have been commissioned up to September, 2024.

items.statement: FY25 capex target of Rs 18,000 crore likely to increase to more than Rs 20,000 crore (Rs 4,000 crore RTM, over Rs 12,000 crore TBCB, Rs 1,000 crore others)
items.quote: The CapEx planning for FY24-25 is about ₹18,000 crore, but it is likely to increase to more than ₹20,000 crore. So, it will have about ₹4,000 crore of RTM projects, and TBCB projects of more than ₹12,000 crore, others about ₹1,000 crore.

items.statement: Total projects in hand worth Rs 1,43,295 crore (RTM Rs 8,896 crore, TBCB Rs 93,000 crore, others Rs 3,300 crore, new RTM Rs 38,008 crore)
items.quote: If we consider all the projects which we have in hand, then as on today, we have ₹1,43,295 crore worth projects in hand, which includes RTM projects of ₹8,896 crore, TBCB projects of about ₹93,000 crore, and others like metering and other area about ₹3,300 crore. And new RTM projects like offshore wind and Leh-Kaithal HVDC link, that includes ₹38,008 crore.

items.statement: Expect over Rs 3 lakh crore (Rs 3 trillion) projects in execution by 2032 based on NEP pipeline and 50% win rate
items.quote: So put together, it will be more than ₹3,35,000 crore projects in execution by 2032. So, our outlook will be at least Rs. 3 trillion worth projects or CapEx by 2032.

items.statement: Profit growth muted (1-2%) due to Rs 300 crore half-year impact from CERC 2024-29 O&M charge reduction and declining RTM depreciation/interest
items.quote: As far as profit is there, if you remember that as per the CERC tariff regulation for 24-29, as per the new CERC Regulation, our O&M charges have been reduced by almost 600 crore. So for half year, the effect is almost 300 crore.

items.statement: NEP projects peak demand rising to 296 GW by March 2027 and 388 GW by March 2032; RE capacity to 537 GW by 2027 and 613 GW by 2032
items.quote: As per NEP (National Electricity Plan), recently announced by Ministry of Power, peak demand which is 249.85 gigawatt as on 30 th September, 2024, it is going to increase to 296 gigawatt by March, 2027 and about 388 gigawatt by March, 2032

items.statement: 90% of future Rs 3+ lakh crore execution expected from inter-state projects; 10% from intra-state via JVs and TBCB
items.quote: Like 90pc, 85-90pc will be inter-state. Like we have some joint venture companies with like Rajasthan and some TBCB projects which will come in intra-state sector. They will be done for intra-state but we are expecting that our share from inter-state will be about 90pc.

items.statement: Khavda-Nagpur HVDC project entity cost Rs 24,000 crore (65-70% terminals, 35% lines); Leh-Kaithal HVDC tendered, award expected by Feb-March 2025
items.quote: The Khavda project entity cost is ₹24,000 crore, which will include terminal at Khavda and Nagpur. And almost 65 to 70% will be the cost of the terminals, and about 35% cost will be for the transmission line.

items.statement: Capitalization target Rs 18,000 crore for FY25; Rs 25,000-30,000 crore for FY26; Rs 35,000-40,000 crore annually from FY27
items.quote: This year, we are targeting about ₹18000 crore capex as well as for capitalization. But the next year, it will increase from ₹18000 crore, maybe somewhere between ₹25 to 30 thousand crore and next year, it will go about maybe ₹40,000 crore.

items.statement: Telecom income Rs 267 crore in Q2 with 13 new customers and 100% backbone availability
items.quote: The income from Telecom is ₹267 crore in Q2. New customers; we have added about 13 numbers. Our backbone availability has been 100%.

items.statement: Consultancy income Rs 134 crore in Q2; 16 international and 77 domestic ongoing assignments
items.quote: In consultancy, in international, we have 16 ongoing assignments and in Q2, 3 orders have been received. In domestic front, 77 are ongoing assignments and 2 numbers orders received in Q2. Our income in Q2 from consultancy is ₹134 crore.

items.statement: Commercial billing Rs 19,000 crore with 100.31% realization in H1
items.quote: In commercial performance, we have billed about ₹19,000 crore and realization has been more than 100%; 100.31%.

items.statement: Next two quarters expected to maintain current margins; beyond that difficult to predict due to market conditions
items.quote: what he has mentioned in the interview that next 2 quarters looks like that we are going to maintain these kind of margins. Beyond that, it is very difficult to predict anything

items.statement: Total planned capex of Rs. 2,000 crores over next 6-7 years including furnace, mining, ethanol and renewable power
items.quote: Almost, we have to spend almost Rs. 2,000 crores in next 6-7 years. So, apart from the dividend, I don't see any further disbursement.

items.statement: Sukinda underground mining expansion to 1.2 million tons capacity requiring Rs. 1,000 crores over 5-6 years
items.quote: Yes, the timeline is next 5-6 years to start the improved production and investment will be about Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Ethanol project at Therubali with 120 KLD capacity, Rs. 140 crores capex, operational by December 2025
items.quote: We are expecting it to be operational by end of December 25, so last quarter of FY26, we should be seeing that.
