items.statement: Consolidation: BSPL 100% acquired in Q1; Balaji and BHC ~100% consolidated by end Q2; sales from them to be near zero by end Q3
items.quote: By the end of the 2nd Quarter, we have concluded the job work model. Therefore, in Quarter 3, we are looking at almost all volumes and revenue from Balaji and Bansal High Carbon to come into Bansal Wire.

items.statement: Dadri facility at ~20% utilization end Q2; targeting 100% capacity (3.5 lakh tons) operational by end FY25; Q2 volumes: 80k tons (30k high carbon, 27k mild steel, 21-22k stainless)
items.quote: By the end of this quarter, we were already close to 20% capacity utilization in Dadri and I would say again, for the first month itself in this quarter, we have done a lot better.

items.statement: Working capital: vendor financing and bill discounting limits tied up; utilization from Q3 as Balaji/BHC revenue ramps
items.quote: we have already tied up some limits for discounting and other various tools. We are only waiting for the revenue, which will come in the third quarter of this year to increase from Balaji 7 and Bansal High Carbon, and then we will start utilizing those limits as well

items.statement: Raw material sourced domestically (~0% imports); agriculture applications: fencing, barbed wire, grape farming wires; B2C model in Gujarat
items.quote: Almost zero, sir. All our raw material is sourced locally. So, we don't import.

items.statement: Expects H2 demand trends largely similar to H1 with potential upside if API prices improve and industry volumes pick up
items.quote: Looking ahead we expect demand trends in the second half to be largely similar to the first half. There could be some upside potential if we see some improvement in API prices and uptake in industry volumes, but that remains to be seen.

items.statement: Expects API prices to average or normalize in Q3 or Q4 FY25 as KSM intermediates show solidification
items.quote: An update on to it is while we saw the API prices softening in Q3, most of the intermediates of the KSM have started showing some solidification. So, either in Q3 or Q4, I expect the API prices will at least average or normalize.

items.statement: Expects FY26 to move positively if industry volumes and new launches pick up
items.quote: So, if the industry volumes and the new launches pick up, I feel that FY26 should be moving on those lines essentially.

items.statement: Spent Rs. 150 crore on capex in H1 FY25
items.quote: In H1 we spent around Rs. 150 crore in CAPEX.

items.statement: Started commercial production at new injectable facility in Haridwar; ampoule and SVP FFS operational, vial and lyophilized vials in Q3, LVP FFS in Q4
items.quote: In Q2 we started commercial production at our new injectable facility in Haridwar. The facility has operational ampoule and SVP FFS line and we plan to start and vial and lyophilized vials in Q3. Further in Q4, LVP FFS will also be operational.

items.statement: Completed land acquisition for Jammu plants; civil works to begin shortly; commercial production expected in FY26-27
items.quote: We have completed the land acquisition for our Jammu plants and civil works is expected to begin shortly. Commercial production from these facilities will begin in '26-27.

items.statement: API business not expected to turn EBITDA positive in Q4 FY25; will revisit plans in April; needs 6 months to turn around
items.quote: I don't think that in the Q4 this will turn around, or it would not be EBITDA positive. I think we will have to give it 6 months from here and we will revisit our business plans starting April.

items.statement: API prices of key molecules (Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan) continue to fall; cost-plus CDMO model leads to revenue deflation when input costs fall
items.quote: Prices of several key API's including Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan etc., continues to fall. As you are aware, our CDMO business is a cost-plus model, so when input costs fall, we experience revenue deflation as well.

items.statement: CDMO volume declined roughly 11% in Q2 FY25; attributes to industry cycle and API price destocking; H1 volumes flattish vs industry
items.quote: Yes, we did not experience the volume growth. We had a volume decline of roughly 11% this quarter.

items.statement: MSME compliance deadline 8th January; government stance uncertain; 10,000 MSMEs affected; commercial impact unclear
items.quote: See in the Indian scenario although the date is till 8 th January, but the government has not confirmed yet how it will behave, so our wish is each and every company of our country should follow the system which is under Indian law and grow. Right now, there is no view from government side that it will take any action on governments date or not

items.statement: Received patent for room-stable Hydroxyurea oral suspension for Sickle Cell disease; exclusive rights for Triple Hair Inc. topical alopecia solution in India
items.quote: We are happy to announce that during the quarter we received a patent for our formulation room-stable Hydroxyurea oral suspension. This is a break-through formulation aimed at managing Sickle Cell disease which has a high disease burden especially in geographies like India and Africa. Akums has been granted an exclusive right for further development manufacture and market the products innovated by

items.statement: Net sugar production expected at 28.3 million tonnes for upcoming season after 3.7 million tonnes diversion
items.quote: After accounting for diversion of 3.7 million tonnes, the net sugar production is expected to be 28.3 million tonnes as compared to 32 million tonnes last year.

items.statement: Ethanol production expected around 25 crore litres including maize plus 3 crore litres ENA for ethanol year Nov 2024-Oct 2025
items.quote: For the ethanol year, which has begun from 1st of November and will run up to 31st October, we are expecting on the basis of current cane availability estimate around 25-odd crore liter, including the maize, we would be in a position to do.

items.statement: PLA project commissioning targeted for October 2026
items.quote: Udit Gupta: Right. And this plant is on track for commissioning in October 2026. Vivek Saraogi: Yes, October 2026.

items.statement: UP Government announced 50% capex subsidy over seven years, 5% interest subvention, and SGST net reimbursement for PLA project
items.quote: The UP Government has announced a policy for bioplastics for this project, which is a 50% capex subsidy over seven years, a 5% interest subvention, and then SGST net reimbursement.

items.statement: Industry requests MSP increase, ethanol price revision, and 2 million tonnes export allowance to support sugar prices
items.quote: There are three demands of the industry that need to be met, which are very rational. 2 are coming out of a declared policy some years back, which unfortunately has not been followed up. 1) declaration of MSP. It was done for the first two years after the policy came in Minimum Selling Price (MSP). It hasn't been followed up there after, so that is one thing which can help. 2) the ethanol prices w

items.statement: Ethanol mix expected: 9 crore litres from juice, 10-11 crore litres from B-Heavy, 1-1.5 crore litres from C-Heavy, rest from maize
items.quote: Within this 25 crore liter, maybe around 9 crore liter on account of juice and around 10-11 crore liter on B-Heavy, may be 1 -1.5 crore liter C-Heavy and the rest is maize.

items.statement: Late planting in 2-3 factories may reduce cane availability due to one month less growing period
items.quote: Due to some late planting in 2-3 factories, we might have slightly lower cane availability due to yields having a month less to grow.

items.statement: Power export realization to UP grid at Rs. 3.46 per unit, average annual realization Rs. 5.82 per unit including open access
items.quote: Power which we are exporting to grid, the Uttar Pradesh grid, we are getting realization of around Rs. 3.46 per unit. Plus, open access, so average realization should be on an annual basis Rs. 5.82 per unit.

items.statement: Board announced interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board of Directors has announced an interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share.

items.statement: UP sugar production expected stable at 10.8 million tonnes similar to last year
items.quote: Regionally, UP is expected to remain stable at a production of about 10.8 million tonnes, similar to last year's level.

items.statement: India sugar inventory at 8.5 million tonnes plus 28.3 million tonnes production expected to meet 29 million tonnes domestic consumption
items.quote: As on 30th September 2024 India's sugar inventory stands at around 8.5 million tonnes. Combined with the production of 28.3 million tonnes, that is the net post diversion production, this supply is expected to adequately meet the domestic needs of 29 million tonnes, that is the forecasted consumption for next year.

items.statement: Sugar Control Act draft has zero impact according to management; Government already had powers under Essential Commodities Act
items.quote: So, first of all, the Government always has all powers under the act regarding essential commodities. So, there was just zero impact of that in my mind on anything at all.

items.statement: Distillery capacity can handle 11.5-12 crore quintals cane; currently at 10 crore quintals, waiting for cane availability before further expansion
items.quote: Our existing distillation capacity can handle cane of around. 11.5 crore to 12 crore quintal of cane. Currently we are in the region of around 10 crore quintal of cane. So, we are waiting for the cane to be there before we take any further action.

items.statement: PLA plant rated capacity 75,000 tonnes per annum; expect full utilization and sales stabilization within 6 months of commercial production
items.quote: So, 75,000 tonnes per annum is the rated capacity now peak will be only seen once the plant is installed. Vivek Saraogi: It should be full utilization and just to clarify the competition, once it is banned, gets enforceable as Avantika said, the Government is continuously saying you want us to enforce the ban shows the alternate we will enforce the ban

items.statement: Central Government approved Bio E3 policy to promote biomanufacturing including biopolymers; details awaited
items.quote: In August of 2024 the Central Government Cabinet approved a policy called the Bio E3 policy. The policy is meant to give impetus to biomanufacturing, including biopolymers, in which our project also falls.

items.statement: Management expects auto replacement segment to grow double-digit over medium term
items.quote: Mumuksh Mandlesha: So fairly to say over a medium term, double-digit can be seen in the auto replacement segment? Avik Roy: Yes. Confident about it.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin of around 13% in immediate term and around 14% at longer horizon for lead-acid business
items.quote: Asish Mukherjee: If you look at the profitability, this quarter we are at 11.3%. We do not give any guidance on the margin in future. But just to give you a feel, that our immediate objective is to get around 13%. And at a longer horizon, we'll look at around 14%.

items.statement: Phase 1 lithium-ion cell plant investment expected around INR5,000 crores, large portion in current fiscal with possible spillover to Q1 next fiscal
items.quote: the lithium-ion business- as I said, that Phase-1 investment will be around INR5,000 crores, and a large portion of that will be in this fiscal. There may be some spillover to the first quarter of the next financial year, but that's as what looks as of now

items.statement: Exide has invested INR550 crores equity in Exide Energy till October, total equity investment to date is INR2,852 crores
items.quote: In the current fiscal year, Exide has already invested equity of INR550 crores till October. With this, the total equity investment by Exide todate is INR2,852 crores.

items.statement: Lithium-ion cell plant installation and commissioning with initial runoff targeted for mid-2025, SOP in 2025, no change to original schedule
items.quote: Mandar Deo: Yes, certainly, happy to do that. So , like we have repeatedly said in the past also, our schedule remains unchanged, where we have said that in the middle of 2025, we will have our installation and commissioning as well as initial runoff completed. And then in the due course of certification and customer approval, we should be seeing SOP i n 2025. So , no change in our originally publ

items.statement: Price hikes of about 1.5% cumulatively taken in two tranches in Q2 for aftermarket; OEM and industrial prices are pass-through indexed to LME/HZL
items.quote: Avik Roy: See, there are 2 parts. One is the aftermarket. In aftermarket, in quarter 2, we have taken price hikes in 2 tranches. And cumulatively it will be about 1.5%. So on the OEM and industrial side, these are mostly pass-through. So these prices are indexed with the customers, through LME or HZL or any kind of standards.

items.statement: Telecom demand decline due to high base from 5G rollout completion; decline expected to moderate as 5G rollout mostly complete by last year Q3
items.quote: Now coming to Telecom. I mentioned that Telecom had a high base effect because of the 5G rollout last year. Slowly, the pace is getting corrected, and more or less, 5G rollout was over by last year's Q3. So going forward, we don't see this kind of a decline year-on-year on Telecom.

items.statement: Home UPS/inverter battery demand soft in Q2 due to early monsoon; expected to rebound from Q4 (January onwards) with enhanced go-to-market network
items.quote: There was early onset of monsoon in Q2, we suffered, but we have a very strong strategy in place. Now we have additionally augmented our go-to-market and finding out new channel networks. Quarter 3 will be not so positive , because this is not the season for inverter batteries. But from Q4 onwards, from January onwards, we can again see a rebound

items.statement: Industrial infrastructure order backlog drove double-digit growth in Q2 despite weak economic indicators; leading indicators (PMI 57.5 in October) suggest order inflow will increase
items.quote: If you look at the macros of quarter 2, the lagging indicators are disappointing. Most of the economic indicators of quarter 2 w ere not good. But we still posted a double -digit growth because of our order backlog. Going forward, I just came across the October results, if I see the leading indicators of October, the manufacturing Purchase Managers Index, it's showing an increase to 57.5 or someth

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties in Europe (major export market) causing hiccups; economic downturn in Germany and France expected to recover by spring next year
items.quote: There were some hiccups because of the geopolitical situation in Europe, because Europe is quite a big market for us. But we have to live with the geopolitical uncertainties. There are so me economic downturn in countries like Germany and France. I'm sure , they predict that by end of winter , which means around springtime next year, those demands are also going to come back

items.statement: Government lifted restrictions on ethanol production from sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses on 29th August 2024
items.quote: Moreover, the central government has lifted restriction on the production of ethanol from sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses on 29th August 2024.

items.statement: Company plans to use sugarcane juice, syrup and maize for ethanol production in season 2024-25 to maximize capacity utilization
items.quote: The company plans to use sugarcane juice and syrup for ethanol production during season 2024-25 in addition to molasses as also to use maize in order to maximize capacity utilization in season and to store molasses for off-season operations.

items.statement: Sugar season 2024-25 started on 7th November 2024 at both Dhampur and Rajpura units
items.quote: I'm happy to inform you that the company has started its sugar season 2024-25 on 7th of November 2024 at both the units, Dhampur and Rajpura.

items.statement: Sugar business loss reduced to INR 4.1 crores from INR 20.6 crores in comparable quarter last year
items.quote: During the quarter, loss in sugar business has reduced to INR 4.1 crores from INR 20.6 crores in the comparable quarter last year.

items.statement: Ethanol business loss of INR 0.6 crores versus profit of INR 38.2 crores due to ban on syrup and B-heavy molasses
items.quote: Loss in ethanol business is INR0.6 crores versus profit of INR 38.2 crores, again, due to ban on use of syrup and B-heavy molasses as also lower cane crush during season, resulting in significantly lower volumes.

items.statement: Sugar sales realization improved to INR 38,163 per tonne from INR 37,570 per tonne, up about 2%
items.quote: This, combined with improved sales realization, which was INR 38,163 per tonne in this quarter as against INR 37,570 per tonne in the corresponding quarter last year, an increase of about 2% has resulted in reduced loss in the sugar business.

items.statement: Ethanol sales volume dropped 73% to 93.17 lakh liters from 341.51 lakh liters due to lower cane availability and government restrictions
items.quote: In this quarter, ethanol sales was 93.17 lakh liters as against 341.51 lakh liters in the comparable quarter last year, nearly 73% lower.

items.statement: New tetra pack machine commissioned in April 2024 increased potable spirits production to 7.16 lakh cases from 5.69 lakh cases
items.quote: Production of potable spirits during the quarter has increased to 7.16 lakh cases from 5.69 lakh cases in the comparable quarter and sales has increased to 6.95 lakh cases from 5.65 lakh cases in the corresponding quarter of last year. This increase is largely due to additional production from new tetra pack machine commissioned in April 2024.

items.statement: Company repaid long-term debt of INR 24.18 crores during the quarter and INR 44.16 crores in half year ended September 2024
items.quote: The company has repaid long-term debt of INR 24.18 crores during the quarter and INR44.16 crores in half year ended September '24.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 margins dropped ~4pp YoY and ~1.5pp QoQ due to copper volatility and inventory liquidation
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, margins did take a hit. We dropped approximately 4 percentage points compared to the comparable quarter of last year and about 1.5 percentage points compared to the immediately preceding quarter.

items.statement: If copper stays steady, FY25 revenue could reach INR 6,000 cr; H1 at INR 2,600 cr with Q3+Q4 typically 60%+ of full year
items.quote: If copper remains steady, then that number can be towards the INR 6,000 crores number. But if it keeps zigzagging, then it's a little difficult to predict. So at the moment, 6 months, we are at INR2,600 crores, I think, yes. So typically, quarter 3 and quarter 4 are about 65% -- 60% plus of the year's numbers.

items.statement: Margins should track back to normalcy in coming quarters; worst of margin correction is behind
items.quote: I believe that as far as the margin corrections are concerned, the worst is behind us, and we should be more stable from now onwards.

items.statement: Major capex of ~INR 500 cr underway: e-beam facility ready awaiting BIS certification, auto cable expansion at Roorkee commissioning by Dec, fiber draw capacity 4→6 mn km equipment arriving May-Jun
items.quote: All told, approximately INR 500 crores was to be spent on all these programs. Last fiscal, we spent about INR 160 crores, I think. Bulk of the balance will be spent in the current fiscal with a small overflow into the next year.

items.statement: FY26 capex could be INR 100-200 cr depending on wire demand outlook
items.quote: Sir, is it fair to say that FY '26, the capex could be, say, INR100 crores to INR200 crores? Mahesh Viswanathan: Yes, it's possible.

items.statement: BSNL BharatNet bids opened; partners won 3 packages as L1; orders expected late Q3, supplies from Feb-Mar; 10% cable content in packages
items.quote: I expect that the ordering from BSNL to the bid winners will happen sometime towards the latter part of this quarter and supplies will commence probably around February or March.

items.statement: Wire volume growth muted at ~2% in Q2 due to copper volatility distorting speculative vs consumption demand; structural housing/capex cycles steady
items.quote: Yes, that volume growth overall is about 2%.

items.statement: FMEG business on track for ~INR 300 cr revenue in FY25 (up ~40% YoY); breakeven at INR 250-260 cr; H1 at INR 128 cr vs INR 100 cr last year
items.quote: We are on track to be very close to the INR 300 crores mark this year, which would be almost a 40% jump from last year. Also, like I said, I've said this in the past also, at INR 250 crores, INR260 crores, we should be breaking even.

items.statement: Communication cables margin 2-2.5% due to low utilization and fiber price drop; should climb back to historical 7-8% as government procurement resumes
items.quote: We used to average around 7%, 8% in the past. For that to happen, it will take a little bit of time, but it should start climbing.

items.statement: Power cable business is tender-driven L1 with collection risks; peers have DSO 60-70 days vs Finolex 14-15 days; practices not comfortable
items.quote: So risks that are there are tow ards collection, timing of collection. So you will find that many of my peers have that impact visible on their DSO. I have a DSO of, I think, 14 days or 15 days. Typically, you will find most of them having DSOs of 60, 70 days

items.statement: Fiber prices dropped from $4/km to $2.6-2.7/km landed; expect normalization in 6-8 months as global consumption picks up
items.quote: what used to be $4 per kilometer 2 years ago is now $2.6, $2.7 per kilometer landed in India. So there is a substantial reduction in the realization of fiber. I think as the consumption of fiber picks up acros s the globe, we should expect to see this coming back to normal levels, probably over the next 6 to 8 months

items.statement: Wire capacity ~23-24 lakh coils/month at ~65% utilization; auto cables ~80% occupied; agri seasonal
items.quote: we have the capacity to make approximatel y 23, 24 lakh coils per month. Utilization is around slightly over 65% at this point in time. This is on the standard wire. Then, of course, there are additional capacities for auto cables and for agricultural applications. Auto is more or less 80

items.statement: Wire market share steady at 18-20% of ~INR 25,000 cr market; no material change in last 2-3 years
items.quote: At an annual basis, and again, if I take last year's number, our wire revenue was somewhere around INR 4,200 crores or INR4,300 crores out of a total wire market size of about INR 25,000 crores. So slightly over -- slightly under 20% at that level.

items.statement: NCLAT disposed matter, directed NCLT to decide ownership of disputed Orbit shares and control of entities within a time period
items.quote: There was one matter before the NCLAT, which was disposed off and directions given to the NCLT to decide on the matter that is before them within a period of time. And what is that matter between -- in front of the NCLT is basically who holds ownership of the disputed shares in Orbit, and therefore, who ga ins -- who gets control over all the entities

items.statement: Management expects demand growth to be positive in the next 2-3 months and 6 months as budgetary allocations convert to purchase orders.
items.quote: On the macro side, we believe there is every reason for demand to be better in the next 6 months versus the last 6 months, largely because most of the budgetary allocations will now get converted into purchase orders across states.

items.statement: Management expects volumes to grow broadly in line with industry demand growth over the next couple of years.
items.quote: Volumes performance, I am convinced, we should be in line with the industry demand growth. Sometimes little higher, sometimes a little lower, but we should be broadly in line with the industry demand growth.

items.statement: Ongoing expansion projects at Jaitaran, Kodla, Baloda Bazaar, and Etah are on track for commissioning between April to June next year.
items.quote: Our ongoing expansion projects in Jaitaran, in Kodla, in Baloda Bazaar, in Etah are running on track and we expect all of them to be completed between April to June next year.

items.statement: Capex guidance of roughly Rs. 4,000 crore per year for the next 4 years remains intact.
items.quote: Yes it does. We will be roughly Rs. 4,000 crore every year for next 4 years.

items.statement: Company remains committed to reaching over 80 million tons capacity by FY28.
items.quote: We remain committed to reaching our goal of over 80 million tons capacity by FY 28 and are actively identifying growth opportunities to meet the target.

items.statement: Total cost excluding depreciation and interest reduced 8% year-on-year from Rs. 4,503 to Rs. 4,122 per ton.
items.quote: We, however, kept sharp focus on efficiency in our operations, which helped us achieve about 8% reduction in the total cost excluding depreciation and interest from 4,503 per ton to 4,122 per ton on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Average CV fuel cost reduced from Rs. 2.05 to Rs. 1.71 year-on-year; current purchase price is Rs. 1.51 with consumption cost expected at Rs. 1.65-1.64 this quarter.
items.quote: Supported by durable international fuel prices, our average CV fuel cost reduced from 2.05 to 1.71 on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Fuel purchase price currently at Rs. 1.51; consumption cost expected at Rs. 1.65-1.64 this quarter with full benefit in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26.
items.quote: This quarter, we will be at about 1.65-1.64 because of the pipeline inventory which we are carrying, but today we are purchasing 1.51. So, the effect will come only in Q4 FY25 or maybe partly in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Premium product share in trade segment reached 15% in Q2, up from 9% in Q1; management aims to stabilize at 15% for next few quarters.
items.quote: Premium products were central to our strategy and with the share in that trade segment reaching the last quarter to about 15%.

items.statement: Management intends to stabilize premium product share at around 15% for the next few quarters before targeting higher levels.
items.quote: So, as we speak now, we will like to stabilize it going forward also at around the same numbers. Once we stabilize, then we will take the next jump to a higher level.

items.statement: Urban demand moderated due to soft consumer sentiment; rural demand improving on good monsoon, higher MSP, and MNREGA allocation.
items.quote: Overall, urban demand moderated due to the softening of the consumer sentiments; however, the good news is that the RBI survey indicates improved business expectation for the upcoming quarter. Rural demand is improving as reflected in increasing FMCG volume sales and a rise in the three-wheeler and tractor sales.

items.statement: Sustained price improvement depends on steady demand recovery across segments; pricing environment difficult to quantify.
items.quote: However, sustained price improvement depends also on the steady demand recovery across segments. We believe that despite the current pressure, we are navigating these conditions by shoring our brand, focusing on key optimization and continuing operational excellence.

items.statement: Depreciation for FY25 expected at ~Rs. 2,700 crore; management emphasizes cash profit over net profit.
items.quote: However, you have given me the opportunity to explain that I had always been maintaining vis-a-vis Shree that please look at cash profit numbers and not net profit numbers. And I am very happy to say that in spite of whatever we have done, the cash profit still stands at about Rs. 200 a share vis-a-vis 259-260 in last quarter, so Rs. 200 is the cash EPS, net EPS is 25 and it is nothing but because

items.statement: RMC business launched with 7 plants (5 in Mumbai, 2 in Hyderabad); targeting double-digit plants by FY25 end.
items.quote: We started in West and South in Hyderabad as well as in Mumbai where we have taken 5 plants in Bombay and 2 in Hyderabad. That makes 7 plants to date. We are also constructing plants in other regions now and what we had assured to the investors was 5 plants in year 1. We have already crossed that to 7 as I said and I hope we will be in double digit by this financial year end.

items.statement: Middle East unit is now making cash profits.
items.quote: Sir, my question is that our Middle East unit is making cash profits now? Ashok Bhandari : Yes, it is.

items.statement: India aluminum COGS guidance for Q3 FY25: up 1% to 1.5% vs Q2
items.quote: The guidance for Q3 is that it could be up by about 1% to 1.5%.

items.statement: Aluminum and copper smelter expansions ~$1 billion each; total declared projects $4-5 billion over 3-3.5 years
items.quote: So both these will be roughly 1 billion each. So on top of what we have already declared, if you put 2 billion, so we are roughly going to be between 4 billion and 5 billion of declared projects.

items.statement: Aluminum smelter commissioning Oct 2027; copper smelter 2029; alumina refinery CY2027
items.quote: I think that we are saying that the aluminum smelter should come on stream in October of '27, and the copper smelter will be in '29. Sumangal Nevatia: Understood. And sir, the refinery? Satish Pai: The refinery will be also more or less coming on stream in '27 calendar

items.statement: Bay Minette 420 Kt beverage packaging capacity fully contracted
items.quote: This is expected to be completed in the second half of calendar year '26 with 420 capacity targeted to beverage packaging, which is fully contracted.

items.statement: Copper EBITDA sustainable guidance ~INR650 cr/quarter after one-off gains
items.quote: Q3, Q4, we stick to a guidance of around 650.

items.statement: India FRP demand FY25 expected to grow 7-8% YoY led by packaging
items.quote: The Indian FRP demand in financial year 2025 is expected to grow by 7% to 8% on a year-on-year basis, led by strong demand from the Packaging segment.

items.statement: Global aluminum FRP demand ex-China to grow 4% CY24 and 6% CY25
items.quote: The global aluminum FRP demand excluding China is expected to grow by 4% in calendar year '24 and 6% in calendar year '25, with demand recovery across all major segments of beverage packaging, automotive, specialty and aerospace.

items.statement: Novelis scrap spreads under pressure; near-term EBITDA/ton impact uncertain; mitigation actions underway
items.quote: We are trying to ensure, trying to size up the situation and see where spreads go. We need to see one of those cycles. So you'll have to hold off that. And as soon as we have some clear visibility, we will come back.

items.statement: China adding ~20 Mt scrap melting capacity, tightening global scrap market
items.quote: So nearly 20 million tons of scrap melting capacity is being put up in China, and hence, a lot of scrap is being bought in there.

items.statement: India downstream aluminum EBITDA/ton down 11% YoY due to unfavorable product mix; imports surged ahead of BIS certification
items.quote: The resulting EBITDA per ton was at $179 per ton, lower by 11% year-on-year this quarter, impacted by unfavorable product mix.

items.statement: Novelis Bay Minette expected ~$1,000/t EBITDA; significantly more profitable than Sierre
items.quote: I mean directionally, we have already said earnings call that about $1,000 per ton is a very, very reasonable expectation from Bay Minette alone.

items.statement: India coal sourcing mix Q2: 50% linkage, 47% e-auction, 2% own mines
items.quote: The coal sourcing linkage was 50%, e-auction was 47%, and our own mines was about 2%.

items.statement: Board vision targets Rs 15,000 crore revenue in 4-5 years via organic and inorganic growth across three verticals
items.quote: If you see the three businesses that we have focused on over the last few years in our transformation journey, we believe all the three are now at an inflection point and set to fire. So, we expect all three to grow and contribute to our overall vision.

items.statement: GCL plus Excel EBITDA margins at 14.4% in Q2; committed to 13-15% range going forward
items.quote: If you see, even my Q2 results or if you take the trend, GCL plus Excel, our EBITDA margins are at 14.4%. Now, therefore, we are continuing to trend in a 13% to 15% range, which is what I would commit to.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA improved 130 bps QoQ to Rs 59 crore in Q2
items.quote: On a standalone basis, EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 59 crore, up by Rs. 9 crore from last quarter and improved by 130 basis points.

items.statement: BOM costs decreased 7-12% across models in H1 FY25 through supplier engagement and scale

items.statement: International markets EBITDA positive contributing INR 1.4 crores in Q2
items.quote: Our international markets continue to be EBITDA positive, contributing INR1.4 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Non-FCT revenue grew 3.1% YoY to INR 24.2 crores driven by IP events like Spell Bee and Mirchi Freshers
items.quote: Our non-FCT segment showed a 3.1% year-on-year growth, generating revenue of INR24.2 crores. Despite limited industry events, we achieved this growth through our own successful IP events such as Spell Bee and Mirchi Freshers, which received a strong response.

items.statement: Multimedia solutions degrew due to loss of one client and muted ad growth; IP events business grew 59%
items.quote: The multimedia solution, which is the advertisement led, that business has shrunk a bit. Largely, the degrowth, if you see has been led by one client, which we had last year, and it didn't come in this year. But having said that, the overall industry muted advertising growth has led to a degrowth of the multimedia solutions. Otherwise, our IP business has grown very strongly at 59%.

items.statement: Inventory utilization 74% in Q2 vs 77% last year
items.quote: We are at about 74% against last year of 77%.

items.statement: Target INR 1,000 crore paint revenue in next 4 years with ~15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: In fact, we have made a road plan for next 4 years. And we are targeting to achieve the turnover of INR1,000 crores from the present level with a margin of around 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Expect 15% TMT demand growth in FY25
items.quote: We are expecting 15% growth in the FY '25 in terms of 1 year.

items.statement: Paint business targeting 10-15% growth this year to surpass INR 350 crore
items.quote: We have achieved a turnover of INR350 crores in the state. And this year we are trying to surpass that and achieve 10%-15% growth.

items.statement: Steel PBT margin improved to 11% in Q2 FY25 from 7.3% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: We also achieved significant improvement in PBT margins, which rose to 11% from 7.3% last year.

items.statement: Paint EBITDA margin 6.7% in H1 FY25 vs 7% in H1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA de-grew to INR7 crores from INR9 crores in half H1 of '24 with EBITDA margin of 6.7%.

items.statement: TMT average selling price fell due to lower international steel prices, lower iron ore prices, and seasonal monsoon demand pressure
items.quote: First, prices in the international market are decreasing. Second, the prices of iron have also decreased. So, demand supply is also temporarily facing challenges in Q2. Like the flooding was very high, so there was a little pressure on demand at that time.

items.statement: Paint average selling price per kg/liter rose from INR 58 in FY15 to INR 79 in H1 FY25, a 37% increase over the period
items.quote: Our commitment to premiumization continued to fuel performance as reflected in the increase of our average selling price per kg or per litter from INR58 in the financial year '15 to INR79 in H1 of financial year '25, a growth of 37% over the year.

items.statement: Steel volumes grew 11% YoY in Q2 FY25 (franchisee) and 8% YoY (own manufacturing) despite regional flooding
items.quote: Our steel volume from franchise route had stood at 8.3 lakh metrics ton in Q2 FY '25 compared to 7.5 lakh metric ton in Q2 FY '24, the year-on-year growth of 11%. Our steel volume from own manufacturing stood at 31,778 metric tons sales compared to 29,398 metric tons, a year-on-year growth of 8%.

items.statement: Paint strategy focuses on premium value-added products to raise average selling price and expand in semi-urban/rural areas via dealer network
items.quote: To drive value, we are working on raising our average selling price by focusing more on premium value-added products. For volume growth, we will expand further into regions where we have been building a strong dealer network.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of 30 September 2024; annualized ROCE 28.9% and ROE 22%
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free as on 30 September 2024. ROCE and ROE on an annualized basis stood at 28.9% and 22%, respectively.

items.statement: Expect PBT around INR400 crores in FY25 and about INR500 crores in FY26
items.quote: I think I would say overall, we should expect an increase of about INR100 crores in the total PBT of the company. So, that should put us at close, I think this year our PBT is tending to be around INR400 crores. So, I think that should put us at about INR500 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Scaffolding division revenue target INR1,250 crores for FY25
items.quote: We are on track to do about INR1,250 crores in revenue this year FY25.

items.statement: Scaffolding margins expected at 20% level in FY26 once Aurangabad plant fully operational
items.quote: So, in FY '26, once the Aurangabad Plant is fully operational, we do expect the margins to be at the 20% level.

items.statement: No major capex planned for scaffolding apart from de-bottlenecking and routine capex
items.quote: No, I don't think there are any capex that are being planned apart from de-bottlenecking and routine kind of capex. There are no major capex that are planned.

items.statement: MACH ONE domestic scaffolding order book steady with extremely robust demand
items.quote: The demand is extremely robust in India. The order book is also quite steady. And we are not seeing any. We are seeing only increase in demand there.

items.statement: Freight rates doubled from $4,000 to $8,300 per container impacting margins by roughly 7% in Q2
items.quote: The freight rates almost doubled in this particular quarter from where it used to be around $4,000 a container, it went as high as $8,300. So, I think the impact of that was roughly about 7% on the margins.

items.statement: Textile division targeted at 12%-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Return on capital, I have not calculated, but I have envisaged that all put together, this business can generate about 12% EBITDA, not more, 12%-13% EBITDA, 12% to 15%, let us say, high side 15.

items.statement: Scaffolding prices increased 5%-7% to absorb freight cost increase, further increases possible with tariffs on Chinese imports back
items.quote: So, we have been able to increase prices now. Actually, we have been able to increase prices to this tune 5% to 7%. On the other hand going forward, I think we are a little on a stronger footing in the US as far as price increase is concerned, because the tariffs on Chinese imports are now fully back on.

items.statement: US scaffolding demand pickup expected from Q1 next calendar year (Q2 FY25) post election results
items.quote: People have been on wait and watch mode owing to the result of the election. Now with the election result being out, first quarter next year is when we should see some pickup in demand in the US.

items.statement: Europe scaffolding demand reduction and slowdown ongoing due to geopolitical situation around Ukraine
items.quote: The demand, we have definitely seen reduction and slowdown in Europe. That's been ongoing for the past few quarters because of the geopolitical situation around Ukraine and all that.

items.statement: Drum closure growth trajectory similar for next few quarters; China demand steady, increasing output at China plant
items.quote: So I think going forward, the next few quarters should be similar to what the last two, three quarters have been. Similar trajectory.

items.statement: Raised INR 905.44 crores via preferential issue of equity shares and warrants
items.quote: Furthermore, we have successfully completed a potential allotment of equity -shares and warrants, raising a total of INR905.44 crores.

items.statement: About INR 260 crores of raised funds to be invested in facilities
items.quote: Most of this money, about INR260 crores is going to be invested in our facilities.

items.statement: No specific top-line or EBITDA guidance provided for FY26 or FY27
items.quote: No, currently, we are not having any guidance on this as of now.

items.statement: Expect robust growth in ash handling and EV fleet for next two years due to government push and corporate ESG compliance
items.quote: For the next two years, we see a great demand in our fleet vehicles due to the shift of large corporates to sustainable companies, sustainable transportation of their employees.

items.statement: Ash handling margins to improve by deploying own vehicles; power trading margins to remain stable
items.quote: But the ash handling, we've been trying to deploy a lot of our own vehicles also going forward to improve the margins there. So there, we see a better improvement in margins going forward, sir. In power trading also, it's a regulated business. So the margins will be similar and we don't see any large growth in the percentage of margins in our power trading business, sir.

items.statement: Coal business is back-to-back with no price risk; ash handling risks include forex exposure and tender-based L1 pricing
items.quote: We do not have any risk in that coal business. Like we always keep saying that all our coal businesses are purely back to back. We do not have any price risk in that. And apart from that, we are not having any kind of commodity which we are trading into. The other business risk from the ash handling such as – ash, here risk is about foreign currency which we t ry and hedge whenever possible.

items.statement: Refrigerant gas segment seen as limited growth potential; focus remains on ash & coal handling, power trading, green mobility
items.quote: The company's total going forward will be ash and coal handling. There is a gap it's been contributing the same time over the years. And the market for this is very limited. So we don't see a large growth in this sector in the topic -- in this business in the future.

items.statement: Green Mobility targets ~2,000 vehicles by year-end; current ARR ~INR 34 crores
items.quote: We are currently at an ARR of almost about INR 28 crores -- sorry, INR 34 crores. And this looks like it will keep growing continuously. We are adding a lot of vehicles business by this year -end, we'll have close to 2,000 vehicles.

items.statement: INR 60 crores of raised capital earmarked for debt repayment; debt reduction is highest priority
items.quote: The recent capital raise is almost INR60 crores is towards repayment. And debt reduction is the highest priority.

items.statement: Power trading growth driven by ash & coal handling; considered sustainable
items.quote: The majority of the growth is from Ash And Coal Handling business and this growth is sustainable sir.

items.statement: Ash handling pricing varies by contract (distance-based, fixed, variable); not linked to commodity prices
items.quote: The prices are very different for every company. Every company has a different pricing based on the number of kilometers we have to dispose the ash. Some have fixed prices and the fixed distance. Some have variable distance to the project.

items.statement: No new revenue streams targeted; focusing on existing diversified portfolio
items.quote: No, sir. Currently, we are only focusing on the existing revenue stream, sir.

items.statement: Export opportunities under evaluation; no specific timeline
items.quote: And we are planning to start the export for that one. But which is currently under evaluation. And there is no specific timeline.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 revised to 22-24% from previous 25-26% expectation
items.quote: Performance for the H2 is largely going to remain muted because of these kinds of headwinds of imports and lower priced imports coming in. I think what will offset is in future with demand growing gradually but continuously and surely that should help in offsetting this larger volume import and we should be able to maintain our margins for at least FY24 -25 at about between 22% and 24%

items.statement: Mill expansion project financial closure completed, major equipment orders placed, on track for March 2026 completion
items.quote: Finally, we are ple ased to report that the financial closure for our mill expansion project is completed and we have placed orders for all major equipment of our paper machines, DDS system for the pulp mill, lime kiln and other related utilities. We are on track to complete this project by March 2026

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 450 to 675 tons per day (50% increase) over next 18 months
items.quote: So, we are currently operating at 450 tons per day and we are planning to increase it by 50% and go up to 675 tons per day.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 23.64%, Q2 at 21.8%
items.quote: On half yearly basis operating revenue was reported at INR 560 crores which declined by 8 % on YoY basis and EBITDA was INR 132 crores with EBITDA margin of 23.64% for the period.

items.statement: NSR dropped INR 6,000 per ton YoY in Q2, wheat straw prices declining helping cost control
items.quote: This was mainly due to a drop in the net sales realization by INR 6000 per ton.

items.statement: Wood raw material prices stable at higher levels due to MDF/board industry competition, agro material (wheat straw) prices declining
items.quote: I think wood is not really seeing a declining trend in pricing. In fact, it's either stable or showing an increasing trend. It's the agro raw material primarily wheat straw which is showing a declining trend and helping and aiding in reduced cost of operation.

items.statement: Writing & printing paper demand growing at 6-7% CAGR, specialty segment (food wrapping) potential 15-20% growth
items.quote: Sure, so writing and printing the normal grades are growing at a consistent CAGR of about 6 -7% which based on the current volumes is not a small volume it's a decently large volume and it's giving a good opportunity for the industry players to grow. On top of this if you add the oppor tunity that industry is sitting on from the specialty segment which is the food wrapping segment the growth could

items.statement: Expect demand pickup by Q4 FY25 with publishing season and government tenders, Q3 to remain muted
items.quote: Looking ahead we are hopeful that demand for writing and printing paper will pick up by Q4 and the resultant NSRs will improve especially with the publishing season and the anticipated release of government tenders.

items.statement: Specialty paper currently 18-20% of production, targeting 30%+ in coming years driven by single-use plastic ban opportunity
items.quote: Currently our specialty paper which is about 18-20% of our entire production, we are targeting that it will increase to 30% and beyond in the coming years.

items.statement: Imports increasing above 5-year average, continuing into Q3, primarily from Southeast Asia (Indonesia, China) at lower prices
items.quote: I think last five-year average if you see , the imports in the current year are more than that. Imports are showing an increasing trend over the years and the increasing trend continues for the Q3.

items.statement: Social forestry program: 20 lakh saplings planted, targeting 40 lakh by next year, 1 crore in 3 years to secure wood supply
items.quote: We've started our own social forestry program and we have already reached a level of 20 lakhs saplings and by next year we will reach 40 lakh saplings and it's only going to grow . We have targeted reaching 1 crore saplings in the next three years

items.statement: Industry 4.0 integration: Online sensors and control logic installed for wood bleach section under Project Nirman
items.quote: As par t of our project Nirman initiative focused on industry 4.O integration, we successfully installed online sensors and control logic for the wood bleach section marking a significant step forward in terms of automation, AI and efficiency.

items.statement: Specialty segment EBITDA margin 5-8% higher than writing & printing segment
items.quote: I reckon that the specialty segment will give a better margin EBITDA margin of between 5-8% as compared to writing and printing data.

items.statement: Operating at 100% capacity utilization in both Q1 and Q2, volumes maintained despite price pressure
items.quote: Yes, you are right there our volumes are the same we are already running to our one 100% capacities which was there in both Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Regulated Equity expected to reach Rs. 16,500 Crore by end of FY25 after Parbati-II commissioning
items.quote: I can share with you by end of FY ’25, after commissioning of Parbati-II, our Regulated Equity will be Rs. 16,500 Crore from the current level of Rs. 13,000 Crore.

items.statement: Regulated Equity expected to reach Rs. 17,000 Crore in FY26 after Rangit-IV commissioning
items.quote: Then in FY’26 after commissioning of Rangit-IV, the resultant Regulated Equity will be Rs. 17,000 Crore

items.statement: Regulated Equity expected to reach Rs. 25,365 Crore by FY27 after full commissioning of Subansiri and Pakal Dul
items.quote: by FY’27 after full commissioning of Subansiri and Pakal Dul (1,000 MW), the resultant Regulated Equity will be Rs. 25,365 Crore.

items.statement: Regulated Equity expected to reach Rs. 28,590 Crore by FY28 after commissioning of Teesta-VI, Kwar and Ratle
items.quote: by FY’28 which is a major year from the commissioning pe rspective, we are going to commission three projects, Teesta-VI (500 MW), Kwar (540 MW) and Ratle (850 MW). So, Regulated Equity will be Rs. 28,590 Crore

items.statement: CAPEX of Rs. 4,812 Crore incurred in H1 FY25 against full year target of Rs. 11,762 Crore
items.quote: CAPEX of Rs. 4,812 Crore has been incurred during Half Year FY’25 against target CAPEX of Rs. 11,762 Crore for the whole Financial Year 2024-25 on Consolidated basis.

items.statement: PPAs signed or consent received for all under-construction projects of NHPC and subsidiaries
items.quote: PPAs for all under construction projects of NHPC including its subsidiaries have been signed or consent has been received from the discoms for the same.

items.statement: Teesta-V Power Station expected to commence generation by December 2025 after second incident in August 2024
items.quote: As per our latest estimate, this plant will commence generation by December’25. Reason being, this plant suffered a second inciden t in August'24

items.statement: Parbati-II HE Project: 98% physical progress, targeting commissioning by February 2025
items.quote: We are trying our best to complete the remaining overt lining and invert lining of HRT and commission the project by February'25.

items.statement: Dibang Multipurpose Project: 5 of 7 packages awarded, Dam package tendering underway, scheduled completion February 2032
items.quote: Presently, we are in the process of tendering the Dam Contract and we are hopeful that by another 2-3 months, we will be able to award the Dam Package.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue growth guided at 10-12%
items.quote: We anticipate our revenue growth to be in the range of between 10% to 12% for H2 FY ' 25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11%
items.quote: Our EBITDA guidance will be in the range of 10% to 11% for FY '25.

items.statement: Routine capex of INR 15-20 crores for FY25; solar plant on opex model
items.quote: There is no major capex plan as such for FY '25. There will be a routine capex of around INR 15 - 20 crores.

items.statement: Thermal segment Q2 weak due to season shift; expect recovery in Q3
items.quote: Q2 thermal performance was not so good because the season has shifted. So we expect this quarter to be better than as compared to last year, because Q2 was not so encouraging.

items.statement: Gross margin drop in Q2 due to economy segment mix; expect improvement in Q3
items.quote: This gross margin is all a play of the product mix. So, as you would see that our economic segment grew higher than the company's volume growth that's why the gross margins were low. So but this will even out in the next quarter, I think.

items.statement: Yarn prices unstable, not rising as expected, forcing guidance revision
items.quote: You see the primary reason for this revision is, we expected the yarn prices to go up, but yarn prices even today also, it is not stable. It is the mood is like very, very towards a down trend, but it's not going down, it's not going up.

items.statement: Q2 demand shifted to Q3 due to excessive rainfall and regional disruptions
items.quote: Other factors like excessive rainfall in the month of August and September in certain parts and other regional disruptions impacted discretionary spending this quarter and therefore, demand usually associated with Q2 has partially been shifted to Q3.

items.statement: Economy segment grew 12% in H1; mid-premium and premium volumes declined
items.quote: For H1, the volume growth for the economy segment is around 12%, for mid -premium it degrew by 2% and for premiu m it degrew by 3%.

items.statement: Bangladesh subsidiary has no business operations yet
items.quote: We have opened a subsidiary in Bangladesh, it's been running for the last 4 years, but there is no business in that company.

items.statement: Net debt at INR 20 crores as of H1 FY25
items.quote: Our net debt stands on H1 FY '25 is INR20 crores.

items.statement: EBO count at 31, targeting 50 by end of FY25; mostly franchisee-owned without MG
items.quote: On the EBO front, the EBO count has reached around 31 and we hopefully should reach around 50 EBOs this fiscal.

items.statement: Modern trade revenue grew ~35% in H1, contributing 7% of revenue; target 12-15% contribution in 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect that the modern trade to continues to contribute around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Export expected to contribute 6-7% of revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: And apart from modern trade, we expect export to contribute at least 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Ad spend at 6.5% of revenue in H1; full-year guidance 7-7.5%
items.quote: Yearly guidance will be in the range of around 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Aspire to grow at 12-15% CAGR over 2-3 years driven by modern trade, women's wear, athleisure, exports
items.quote: For a company like us, we always aspire to grow with a 12% to 15% CAGR growth.

items.statement: Pragati scheme expanded to Rajasthan (Jaipur), Haryana, Punjab next; Chhattisgarh stabilizing
items.quote: So the last time, we must have said Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh and some part of UP. So Rajasthan, there is a good response in some cities we have started like in Jaipur and a few other cities, the response has been very good.

items.statement: Revised FY25 operating revenue guidance to at least Rs.4250 crore for PG Electroplast and Rs.600 crore for Goodworth Electronics JV, implying Rs.4850 crore consolidated, ~77% YoY growth
items.quote: For FY25 our revised operating revenue guidance is at least Rs.4250 crore in PG Electroplast and another Rs.600 crore in our JV company, Goodworth Electronics implying Rs.4850 crore of operating revenue as a growth, which is a growth of around 77% growth on F Y24 numbers.

items.statement: Revised FY25 net profit guidance to at least Rs.250 crore, ~83% growth over FY24 net profit of Rs.137 crore
items.quote: We are also revising our guidance for net profit to at least Rs.250 crore which is a growth of around 83% over FY24 net profit of Rs.137 crore.

items.statement: Product business revenue (washing machine, room AC, air cooler) expected to grow ~78% from Rs.1668 crore to ~Rs.2975 crore in FY25
items.quote: The growth in product businesses that is washing machine, room air conditioners and air coolers is expected to be around 78% from Rs.1668 crore to around Rs.2,975 crore.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX guidance at Rs.370-380 crore; ~Rs.165 crore for product capacity expansion, ~Rs.185 crore for land and buildings, ~Rs.20 crore for maintenance and sanitary ware
items.quote: CAPEX guidance stands at around Rs.370 to Rs.380 crore and the progress on all infra and capacity expansion is going on as planned.

items.statement: Order book and visibility for product business remains very robust; company on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in FY25
items.quote: Order, book and visibility for product business remains very robust and the company is on the track to accelerate product business growth significantly in FY25.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain stable in absolute per-unit terms; percentage margins optically vary with commodity pass-through
items.quote: Margin should be in the similar range as they are today. And as I have been explaining actually, for us the percentage margin is not the key driver. Typically, it is the per unit margin in absolute amount that we actually get.

items.statement: ASPs in RAC, washing machine and coolers down due to lower commodity prices; commodity prices are pass-through with monthly/quarterly resets
items.quote: The ASPs in RAC, washing machine and coolers were down due to lower commodity price during the period and availability of critical component was also a challenge due to import supply chain becoming more onerous.

items.statement: Strong order book visibility till March 2025; monsoon and supply chain will determine growth trajectory thereafter
items.quote: We see a strong momentum continuing at least till March and after that actually, how the monsoon season pans out and how things happen will decide the course of growth.

items.statement: Product business contributed 54% of operating revenue in Q2 FY25; room AC Rs.1118 crore (143% YoY), washing machine 41% YoY, air cooler 267% YoY in H1 FY25
items.quote: In first half of FY25 the company has posted industry leading growth in the product businesses and operating revenues for the product businesses worth Rs.1355 crore with 119% growth. The room AC business contributed Rs.1118 crore which is a 143% growth on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Supply chain challenges from BIS certification delays for component factories likely to aggravate in FY26; secured supplies till March 2025
items.quote: The government of India of late has been actually putting quality control orders, basically making the BI S certification mandatory for component factories also, which supply the components to India. And some of the key component factories have been had their BIS certification getting over and they are not getting renewed easily. And that is leading to some supply chain challenges this year and is

items.statement: Board and shareholder approval sought for up to Rs.1500 crore QIP for organic CAPEX and working capital; no inorganic plans
items.quote: We are seeing some very significant growth opportunities coming our way. And if as and when they kind of material ize, we will be utilizing that money for CAPEX and working capital.

items.statement: PLI income booked at Rs.30 crore in FY25, expected Rs.37.5 crore in FY26; included in net profit guidance
items.quote: So, that will be just 30 crores.

items.statement: Net asset turnover target maintained at 4.5x-5x despite CAPEX capitalization increasing asset base
items.quote: Overall, a similar number as it is today, which is about 4.5x to 5x on the net asset side. That should be the range which we should be able to maintain for the net fixed asset turn in our company.

items.statement: TV business confident of maintaining strong momentum in FY26; working on new platforms and client acquisition
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining that momentum going forward as well in FY26 as well. And we are already working on certain new platforms in television and we are in process of acquiring more clients.

items.statement: IT hardware PLI (laptop manufacturing) seeing no industry movement yet; awaiting government import restriction policy; preparing infrastructure
items.quote: Regarding IT hardware on the laptop manufacturing. As of now, we are not seeing any kind of movement happening among all the players of IT hardware and that is mainly because the government is still not able to figure out the way to, how to restrict the import of IT hardware into India.

items.statement: Electronics (ex-TV) business grew ~700% YoY in Q2 FY25; margins low at 2-4% EBITDA
items.quote: In fact, this quarter, if you see our electronic business grew almost 700% on a year-on-year basis apart from TV. So, TV, business has actually gone into Goodworth, the 50% JV and the ex of TV business, we are seeing a very strong traction.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Overall demand environment remained subdued in Q2 FY25, but festive and wedding-related shopping provided positive indicators; expect improved conditions in H2 FY25.
items.quote: This quarter, the overall demand environment continued to remain subdued, consistent with trends observed in previous quarters. However, there were some positive indicators , primarily driven by festive spending and an increase in wedding-related shopping activities as we approach the wedding season for this year . These positive optics are in line with the

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 11.2% in Q2 FY25, up 11% YoY in absolute terms; established businesses delivered robust margins while high-growth segments improved margins on higher scale.
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA stood at Rs. 410 crores, growing 11% Y-o-Y in absolute terms, with 11.2% margin. This includes the TCNS business this quarter, which was not there in the base last year. Our established businesses continue to drive deliver y of robust margins, while high growth segments like Ethnic and TMRW achieved substantial revenue increases with marked improvement in margins

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin expanded 560 bps YoY to 15% in Q2 FY25, with EBITDA of Rs. 162 crores, up 65% YoY.
items.quote: improved financials. It recorded revenue of Rs. 1,082 crores, growing 3% Y-o-Year, with a like-to-like growth of 1.3% . EBITDA margin expanded by notable 560 basis point s to reach 15%. In absolute terms, it delivered EBITDA of Rs. 162 crores, a 65% increase Y-o-Y

items.statement: Demerged ABFRL segment EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps to 8.1% in Q2 FY25, with EBITDA growing 66% YoY.
items.quote: This segment has grown by 31% to Rs. 1,838 crores in Q2 FY ‘25, validating our portfolio expansion strategy to build meaningful size businesses in large consumer spaces of the future. EBITDA for the segment grew by 66% with margin expanding by 170 basis point s to reach 8.1% this quarter

items.statement: Expect net debt to reduce by Rs. 400-500 crores in H2 FY25 due to seasonal sales pickup in wedding and festival periods.
items.quote: So, we expect that debt to come down by Rs. 400-odd crores to Rs. 500 crores in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Plan to open about 100 stores in H2 FY25 across Lifestyle brands, focused on urban and midtown India; small town expansion to remain guarded.
items.quote: In our business, sometimes a few months slip in the way network comes. But my sense is about 100 stores is the kind of number that we should look at in H2.

items.statement: Pantaloons plans to open about 20-25 stores per year, focused on metros, mini-metros and Class 1 towns with larger format stores.
items.quote: We are now looking at 20, 25 stores, more urban-centric, more ready markets because the effect of productivity etc. we have found is much higher here.

items.statement: TCNS brands recorded 13% growth with 3% like-for-like increase in Q2 FY25, marking third consecutive quarter of positive L2L growth driven by product upgrades and synergy benefits.
items.quote: The TCNS brands recorded a solid 13% growth with a 3% like-for-like increase, marking the third consecutive quarter of positive L2L growth. This has been achieved with significant product upgrade, harnessing synergy benefits with larger ABFRL, and focusing on retail productivity.

items.statement: Board approved fundraise for demerged ABFRL entity; timing and size to be decided later to adequately fund high-growth segments.
items.quote: At the time of the demerger announcement, the Board had also approved a fundraiser exercise. And as we go forward, at an appropriate time we would look to raise capital, which we had announced even at the time of demerger itself. We wanted to look at how the merger process is going and then time the fundraise. So, we will do that and we will fund it adequately to sort of drive the growth of the hi

items.statement: Franchisee health under pressure due to prolonged weak demand, leading to slower small-town expansion; management views this as normal cycle.
items.quote: Most of our expansion, at least in Lifestyle brands, is driven through franchisee business. And therefore, our slower expansion is reflective of the franchisee situation today. items.quote: Whatever the number is being shown that has been lesser 1.25 per quarter in terms of profitability. Actual profitability post-Ind-AS is (+2) crores.

items.statement: Inventory days to remain ~120 days, winter inventory piled up in H1

items.statement: Management expects to maintain margins in the 25% region and aims for at least 20% margin level.
items.quote: we aim to maintain at least a 20% margin level, and now we're ending up with margin level somewhere in the 25 % such level.

items.statement: Gross margin target is 52-54% region for coming quarters.
