items.statement: Board approval sought for capacity expansion capex of ₹70-80 crore annually over FY26-FY27.
items.quote: It would be somewhere in the region of about ₹70 crores, ₹80 crores, I would imagine.

items.statement: Closing order book at ₹17.96 billion as of Sept 30, 2024, up 22% YoY with exports at 61%.
items.quote: The total outstanding order book position, which stands at ₹17.96 billion as of the 30th of September 2024, which is higher by 22% compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Domestic market expected to grow 15-20% YoY sustainably driven by cement, steel, MSW, biomass and energy efficiency.
items.quote: we anticipate this growth in the total market to be along our expected lines or may be a 15% to 20% growth year -on-year in the total market domestically.

items.statement: Export order booking grew 50% YoY in Q2 and 63% in H1; export share of closing order book is 61%.
items.quote: export order book stands at ₹10.87 billion, which is a growth of 71% year -over-year and contributing to a robust 61% of the closing order book.

items.statement: No formal revenue guidance given; order booking translates to revenue visibility.
items.quote: sorry, we don't provide guidance. But I think you can hear our previous conference calls and ultimately, our order booking translates into revenue.

items.statement: US subsidiary expected to post full-year loss >₹25 crore in FY25; contribution not expected this year.
items.quote: we would anticipate a full -year loss from th at entity in excess of ₹25 -odd crore . But that has been factored into consideration, and a proportionate amount is already includ ed in our H1 results.

items.statement: CO2 turbine for battery storage commercialised; 20 MW project in Italy with results expected April-May next year.
items.quote: We have already commercialised our carbon dioxide-based turbines and which is for a battery storage application, quite similar to pumped hydro storage. And this is for a 20 MW application in Italy.

items.statement: Enquiry book flat for H1 but domestic recovery in Q2; international enquiry book robust and sufficient for growth.
items.quote: our enquiry book for overall level is somewhat flat. If you have to remember that the domestic order booking in the previous financial year, Q4 FY 24 as well as Q1 FY 25 has been muted due to the election situation.

items.statement: Aftermarket contributes 33% of H1 turnover; refurbishment gaining traction with utility OEMs and new segments.
items.quote: the aftermarket contributes a very healthy 33% to the total turnover of H1 FY 25 with the high contribution of aftermarket to turnover as well as a robust and healthy growth in our order booking for the export segment.

items.statement: R&D spend reported at 1.2-1.3% of turnover but actual spend significantly higher due to commercialised projects.
items.quote: We typically, as far as what is reported on ou r balance sheets, have spent anywhere between 1.2 -1.3 odd percent of turnover in R&D. But that really doesn't capture the full number because most of our R&D projects are end up getting sold.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue target raised to INR13,000 crores with PAT margin 6-7%
items.quote: We're going to achieve the top line around INR13,000 crores on consol. Bottom line, it will be already we have achieved INR232 crores PAT. So it will be more than that, whatever we have targeted, we're going to achieve more.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR84,400 crores with 55% PMC/EPC and 45% redevelopment
items.quote: Total order book in consolidated level, INR84,400 crores, out of which NBCC around INR70,403 crores, HSCL INR8,093 crores, HSCL INR5,915 crores and NSL INR200 crores. So this is our consolidated order book INR84,400 crores, so out of which P MC/EPC around 55% and 45% in redevelopment

items.statement: Target to reach INR1 lakh crore consolidated order book by FY25 end
items.quote: During this year, we are going to achieve INR l lakh crore order book, that is our target. So that will be easily , I think it is

items.statement: INR15,000 crores contract awards targeted for FY25, INR10,000-15,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: Already awarded around INR3,600 crore. But targets for this year -end, around INR14,000 crores, we're going to award. INR8,600 crores of Amrapali is on sale and another INR2,000 crores, INR3,000 crores work also in pipeline only. S o during this year around INR15,000 crore work we're going to award

items.statement: PAT margin target 6-7% and EBITDA margin 5.5-6% for FY25
items.quote: Currently, our PAT margin is around 6%, 6.6%. So whatever we have committed 6% to 7%, definitely, we're going to reach out that margin. And EBITDA, 5.5% to 6%.

items.statement: Expect at least 20% execution growth in FY26 driven by Amrapali Phase 2 and 7 GPRA projects
items.quote: Yes definitely, at least 20%, we can because Amrapali work Phase 2 will be awarded by next month. So from next year 1st quarter, we're going to get the revenue from Amrapali. And 7 GPRA also, we'll go into start our commercial activities. So definitely.

items.statement: Ghitorni land project GDV INR4,000 crores with phased launch starting FY26
items.quote: It will be built and after built we're going to sell the FAR. So that around INR4,000 crores. This will be INR4,000 crores. And the profit will be more because it is our own land.

items.statement: Supertech project INR10,000-15,000 crores opportunity pending NCLT order
items.quote: Supertech is a stalled project, and it is having 50,000 units. Amrapali, has 38,000 units, whereas Supertech around 50,000 units yet to be handed over by the builder. It is also costing about around INR10,000 crores to INR15,000 crores construction work.

items.statement: INR18,000 crores of NBCC standalone order book currently under execution
items.quote: Currently only INR18,000 crores in execution at the NBCC level. Consolidated level, around INR22,000 crores.

items.statement: Seed money INR400 crores invested in Amrapali with INR190 crores interest receivable from ministry
items.quote: So seed money, we received from MoHUA. We have infused the seed money in Amrapali, around INR400 crores we have invested in Amrapali and interest, INR190 crores we have to receive from ministry.

items.statement: Standalone cash INR723 crores and consolidated cash INR1,600 crores as of 30/09/2024
items.quote: Stand-alone cash flow is INR723 crores as far as NBCC is concerned. And in consol level, it is INR1,600 crores as of 30/09/2024.

items.statement: Border fencing INR440 crores awarded for Indo-Bangladesh with more orders expected
items.quote: Recently, we got around INR440 crores worth from Indo-Bangla border fencing. So future also, there will be a scope for us.

items.statement: Sarojini Nagar commercial property sales INR1,400 crores completed
items.quote: In Sarojini, we have sold downtown. Commercial property we have sold in INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Disbursement guidance maintained at INR3,600-3,800 crores for FY25
items.quote: We have told between INR3,600 to INR3,800 crores. We still maintain that number as far as disbursement is concerned.

items.statement: AUM guidance may fall short by INR100-200 crores from INR15,000 crores target for FY25
items.quote: Maybe instead of INR15,000 crores, we may be around INR14,800 or something. This is our expectation.

items.statement: GNPA target maintained at INR450 crores for FY25
items.quote: GNPA, we have total INR450 crores as a GNPA number, we'll still maintain that.

items.statement: Outlet guidance of 250 by March 2025 maintained
items.quote: As far as number of outlets are concerned, we have given a guidance of INR250 crores. I think we have already have 227 outlets.

items.statement: INR27 crores spent on new software implementation so far
items.quote: A total of approximately INR27 crores have been spent so far on the new software.

items.statement: NIM at 5.1% in Q2 FY25 with spread maintained at 3.4%
items.quote: Our NIM for Q2 FY '25 was at 5.1% against 5.4% in Q2 FY '24. The company has been able to maintain a spread of 3.4% by raising yields to 12%.

items.statement: MLR increased by 20 bps in current year (10 bps in May, 10 bps this month)
items.quote: In fact, we have increased our MLR by 10 bps from this month. So already one increase we have done in the month of May. So 20 bps, we have already increased in the current year.

items.statement: Second half disbursements expected around INR2,000 crores, historically stronger than first half
items.quote: based on th at and based on the new initiatives that the management has taken, we are quite confident that we will be able to do around INR2000-odd crores of disbursement in the second half

items.statement: Repayment rate increased to ~INR200 crores/month from INR150 crores, driven by balance transfer outs to banks
items.quote: We are now getting a repayment of around INR200 crores approximately per month. I t was around INR150 crores one year back something per month

items.statement: Stage 2 assets at ~10-11% of AUM, focus on reduction with enhanced collection team
items.quote: So Stage 2 is our focus area. Whatever reduction has happened, in fact, personally, we want to do -- the team wants to do still better. So we a re focused. And the 10%, we are confident that we will be able to achieve this 10% of AUM

items.statement: NHB loan proposal in pipeline, NCD approvals in place, no fixed securitization plans
items.quote: Maybe as of now, liability, we are also approaching NHB. So the NHB proposal is in the pipeline. So maybe we may get some NHB loans during this current year. We are also – we are tapping the market as to our NCD routes and all. We have got approvals from AGM as well as our

items.statement: Non-housing (home equity) at 26% of loan book, housing at 74%
items.quote: The share of non-housing loan that is home equity stood at about 26% of the loan book and housing loans contributed about 74% of the book.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be marginal/negligible with estimated INR50 crores write-back for FY25
items.quote: Credit cost will be marginal or almost nil. It will be very much negligible because of the recoveries we are making. In fact, write-backs will be more this time because we have already estimated a write-back of INR50 crores for the current year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 slippages INR37 crores, recoveries INR67 crores
items.quote: For the current quarter, I can tell INR37 crores was the slippage, INR67crores was the recovery.

items.statement: Incremental lending rates: home loan 11.2%, home equity 13.8%, average 11.8% in September
items.quote: Home loan is 11.2% in September, home equity 13.8%. Average is 11.8%.

items.statement: DSA/Connector share in disbursements increased to ~40% from ~30% last year
items.quote: month, it was 40%. But overall, I think it's -- but we may end up around 40% by year-end... Rajiv Mehta: For the whole year. K. Swaminathan: Yes. For the current year, we may have because that percentage is going up because Connectors we have added in the current

items.statement: Won U.S. export order for commercial vehicle emission components with $7M annual and $40M+ lifetime revenue, SOP January 2026
items.quote: I'm also very happy to announce that we have won an export order for emission components to the U.S. market with annual business of approximately $7 million and lifetime business of $40 million plus. The SOP for the order is expected by January 2026.

items.statement: Will continue to outperform industry; gross profit is the right barometer rather than sales due to catalyst accounting
items.quote: So we have just guided that we will continue to outperform the industry and gross profit is the right barometer rather than sales in our case, the way catalyst accounting is done.

items.statement: EBITDA margins benefit from catalyst accounting removal and FOC model mix; hard to guide specific number
items.quote: So definitely, that is -- and in fact also when you see in terms of the improving EBITDA margins, the way they're calculated, so it's hard to guide on a number.

items.statement: INR 50 crore capex for new suspension plant with SOP mid-December to early January, 280,000 controls capacity
items.quote: We have indicated a capex of INR50 crores. Some is already done and some will be done over this quarter. We have a capacity of 280,000 controls on site.

items.statement: New suspension plant for control arms on platform usable for EV and ICE; new customer business small initially but hopeful for larger wallet share
items.quote: The current volumes that we have, there will be a gradual ramp-up. Hence, at least for Q4 of this year, there will only be marginal revenues for this plant.

items.statement: Construction equipment emission norms from Jan 2025; won temperature control tube business, mature volumes from June 2025, not significant initially
items.quote: We have received good business and we expect some revenues to be coming, starting next year and we expect maybe mature volumes to start more towards June '25 onwards.

items.statement: TREM 5 timeline intact on development readiness; any delay would be government-driven, no communication of delay so far
items.quote: So it is hard to predict in terms of any government delay. However, in terms of development and in terms of readiness, it's fully there and if there is any delay, it should be in due to government, delays in norms.

items.statement: JV with Purem awarded localization program for international customer, expected to kick in mid-2026, will boost JV above breakeven
items.quote: And once that's added, that's going to give some boost to the JV and we're expecting somewhere around the middle of 2026 for that to kick in, but that's a good program that the JV has won.

items.statement: CV 3-4 liter segment: competitor has 90% share, Sharda has product ready but no platform awarded yet, targeting niche profitable segment
items.quote: As of now, we've not been awarded any platform in that segment. That's one of our target segments where we have ready with the product and we are in the business development cycle for that.

items.statement: Export margins generally better but working capital higher; net ROCE similar to domestic business
items.quote: However, what we've guided in general about exports, that generally margins are better in exports, however working capital is also more in exports. So on a net ROCbasis, it generally works out to be the same as our domestic business

items.statement: Core emission capacity augmentation incremental only; similar capex trajectory as last 2 years; light-weighting vertical will require additional capital
items.quote: It will all be incremental capex only. It is not going to be some substantial capex, right? And we would continue on a very similar capex trajectory that we've had last 2 years.

items.statement: Substantially increasing shareholder payback via buyback and established dividend policy; will become more efficient in surplus cash usage
items.quote: At the same time, we are also substantially increasing our payback to shareholders. So I think the buyback was the first part of the journey. At the same time, we also now have a dividend policy that is established and we will continue to do that.

items.statement: Filed ~10 IPs in last couple years focused on emission competitive advantage and exportable adjacencies; too early for licensing or business results
items.quote: Regarding the IPs, we have focused on 2 areas. One is which strengthens our competitive advantage within emissions and especially, there are a few technologies that we anticipate in the next emission norms.

items.statement: Export focus on 4 core areas: CV emission components, temperature control tubes, stationary engine gensets, sub-100HP tractors; light-weighting exports later
items.quote: So these are 4 core areas where we want to focus our export business. However, in the future, definitely, these products are also exportable.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 14.4% (+258 bps YoY); Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 14.8% (+178 bps YoY)
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the half year grew by 258 basis points from 11.8% in H1 FY '24 to 14.4% in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: AUM guidance of INR 1,300 crores for FY26 maintained; may reach INR 1,250-1,275 crores depending on environment
items.quote: So to all the banks in this year starting from day one we gave guidance to them in terms of AUM of INR1,300 crores. So it depends also on how the environment if the environment gets better and better we can still reach that number of 1250, 1275 kind of number.

items.statement: Target minimum doubling of net worth and tripling of AUM over 18 months from last equity raise
items.quote: So what, from an investor perspective, we are saying a minimum doubling of net worth and tripling of AUM over an 18-month period from the last equity raise.

items.statement: Secured loan book increased to 32% of AUM; target over 40% by end of 2025; incremental secured disbursements at 47%
items.quote: The secured loan represented only 12% of our AUM, while this has now increased to 32% as of September 24. By the end of 2025, we maintain our outlook that we will have over 40% of our loan book in the secured segment.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 141 branches (up 36% QoQ); 37 branches added last quarter including 28 in September alone
items.quote: Our branch network continues to expand, now totalling 141 branches up from 104 last quarter. We are now active in 12 states with new branches recently opened in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana which has strengthened our diversification.

items.statement: Yield stable at 29%, spread stable at 15.5%, NIM stable at 16.5%; opex at 13% of AUM vs 12.7% in FY24
items.quote: Evidently, the yield and spread continue to remain stable at 29% and 15.5% respectively for the quarter, which you have noticed in our investor presentation as well. So despite low yield on secured book our spreads remain stable and NIM has remained stable as well.

items.statement: Collection efficiency dipped to 93.2% in Q2 (vs 97.6% YoY); 30+ DPD at 5.45%; credit cost at 3.85% (highest since inception); gross NPA 2.78%, net NPA 1.41%
items.quote: For September quarter, the collection efficiency was at 93.2% comparing with 97.6% in second quarter last year and 30 plus DPD stood at 5.45%. We have mentioned in our presentation that collection efficiency in secured loans is significantly higher at around 97%. While the credit cost stood at3.85% for the quarter, which is – we agree that it has been highest since inception.

items.statement: Internal target: 30+ PAR should not exceed 3%; expect improvement in current quarter and further next quarter
items.quote: Exactly at this point of time if you ask me in terms of guidelines, I feel anything more than 3% PAR in a 30% is not acceptable to us. That is what we will say should be the highest number. Having said that, it is high, looking high in this quarter which we really feel will settle down. We will see some improvement in this quarter and definitely next quarter again should see the improvement.

items.statement: Equity raise of INR 176 crores completed (INR 63 cr equity + INR 113 cr warrants); INR 91 cr received in Q2, balance INR 85 cr receivable by March 2026
items.quote: We also reached equity of INR176 crores which is more than double our net worth in Q1, out of which INR63 crores equity and 113 was warrants and INR91 crores is already received in second quarter and balance INR85 crores is receivable before March 26.

items.statement: Secured loan pricing 100-150 bps below peers in up to INR 5 lakh ticket; incremental borrowing cost at 11-12% (HDFC at 11%); average borrowing cost 13.5%
items.quote: So while the incremental has been 12% the last loan we got from HDFC bank was at 11% in this kind of market. What I believe is there is absolutely no reason that in coming years we will have borrowing cost which is more than our peers.

items.statement: Dedicated collection team built from zero (Aug 31) to 40 people (Sep 30); three large collection agencies engaged; cash collections down from 40% to 20%
items.quote: 31st of August we just had zero collection, dedicated collection team because in all our presentations, we have said that it is a sale and collect model. End of September, we had 40 people internal. And we have also started with agencies and we can already see the change which is coming

items.statement: ROE target of 12% for FY25 uncertain; aim to at least maintain last year's ROE; first target 15% ROE as soon as possible
items.quote: For this year I would not say I am not sure for this year we will be able to do 12% let's see how times shape up. We at least we should maintain what we did last year maybe improve upon it let's see so time will tell.

items.statement: Provision policy: 50% at 90 days, 100% write-off at 360 days; only 9 legal cases filed in 5.5 years; new strategy to pursue maximum recovery
items.quote: I think we are never less on provisions. See we have a policy that for all 90 day cases we make a 50% provision so this is without any exception and in a 360 day 1 year period we take a complete write off. There are many players who keep the book for 3 years before writing it off.

items.statement: Targeting 12% EBITDA margin with consistent delivery; confident of double-digit sales growth
items.quote: So yes, we are going to achieve towards 12%, but most important for us is consistency and which is what we are delivering. So in the process of building our core, I am very confident that achieving the double-digit sales growth number is just for us a very easy.

items.statement: Capex of INR 300-350 crores per annum for next 2-3 years, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: we feel that we should be doing capex of about INR 300 crores INR 350 crores per annum. And given our internal accrual and cash flow generation, largely this should be funded through internal accruals only.

items.statement: H1 FY25 lifetime order book INR 4,750 crores; EV platforms 25% of Q2 wins; annual peak revenue ~INR 1,100 crores from 18-24 months
items.quote: In the first six months of FY25, the company's order book exceeded INR 4,750 crores, reflecting our expanding product portfolio, product premiumization and rising demand for ICE and EV products across segments and geographies.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.4%, up 38 bps YoY; fifth straight quarter above 11%; targeting 12%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 11.4%, increased by 38 basis points. Total lifetime order book won was INR 2,400 crores with EV constituting to about 25% of the total order book.

items.statement: EV products ~10% of revenue; wiring harness 32%, lockset 23%, die casting 18%, instrument cluster 17%; 2W/3W 46-47%, CV 26%, PV 15%, aftermarket 11-12%
items.quote: wiring harness continues to be about 30% to 35% and this quarter is 32%. Lockset and vehicle access is about 23%, die casting division, which is DCD stands for about 18% as this segment is growing as well as our instrument cluster business is also continuing to grow, which is now contributing to about 17% and other new products, which is the EV products and other products such as the sensors are a

items.statement: 2-wheeler demand strong with premiumization; PV slightly declined but UV robust; CV challenged by high base and monsoon; tractor recovery expected
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, industry growth has been moderate with the 2-wheeler segment leading in demand. The passenger vehicle segment experienced a slight decline, reflecting softer market demand. While the utility vehicle category showed robust performance, underscoring strong consumer interest in the SUVs and multifunctional vehicles. The commercial vehicle segment faced challenges due to a high base effect

items.statement: Sanco TLA addresses high-voltage connectors, charging guns, bus bars, cell contact systems, PDU, BDU; localization roadmap aligned with customers; target >10% export revenue share mid-term
items.quote: This partnership will deliver comprehensive and customized electrical distribution systems for the electric vehicle market and there will be various new products, w hich will bring into the portfolio of Minda Corporation such as the connectors, charging gun assemblies, sockets, bus bars, cell contact systems for batteries, power distribution systems and Battery Distribution Unit

items.statement: Export demand subdued in Europe; US election uncertainty; CV recovery dependent on government infra spend; some EV OEM orders not yet in production
items.quote: Of course, the order intake continues. However, we do not see a hig her uptake in the next six months when it comes to the exports, primarily in Europe region, various macroeconomic factors. And now with the new elections in the US, we have to really see on how this market pans

items.statement: Four new facilities: two diecasting, one instrument cluster, one wiring harness component; 24-acre land acquired in UP for future expansion
items.quote: To meet this growing demand, the company is coming up with four new facilities, two in diecasting, one in the instrument cluster division and one in the wiring harness component division. In line with our strategic vision, Minda Corporation has also acquired a 24 -acre land in Uttar Pradesh for future expansion.

items.statement: Export revenue target 10-15% of total (from ~7% currently) in mid to long term; order book already in place
items.quote: in the midterm to long term from current about 7% in our growth on the exports, we expect it to be,and our target rather is to be about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Sanco TLA potential >INR 1,000 crores immediate TAM for phase 1 products; RFQs received, nearing nomination
items.quote: this can increase our business potential to more than INR 1,000 crores in the current products that are offered in the first phase.

items.statement: ROCE floor 20% for any inorganic acquisition; capital allocation policy board-approved
items.quote: Absolutely. Parag ji, we have very strong financial footings metrics internally approved by Board of Directors on capital allocation, and any kind of inorganic or capital allocation cannot dilute our ROCE. So ROCE above 20% is our prime capital allocation financial prudence.

items.statement: Sunroof/closure JV with HCMF: plant commissioning Q1 FY26 (possible 1-2 month delay); advanced discussions with OEMs for SOP in 2 years
items.quote: So yes, we are in line with the Q1. Of course, there could be maybe a month or two delay, but yes, we are in line in order to move forward and set up the facility.

items.statement: Order book mix: 2W/3W ~40%, 4W ~20%, rest CV and offroad; 60% new business, 40% replacement
items.quote: So it is in line with our current revenues. So again, 2-wheelers and 3-wheeler continues to be, I think, about 40% of the total order book, and 4 -wheelers is over about 20%, and the rest is the commercial vehicles and offroad.

items.statement: Smart key penetration on track; SOP started for Japanese OEMs in Q2; new segments launching soon
items.quote: Smart key orders continue to get deeper penetration. And depending on the SOPs of the customers that are there. Of course, in Q1 we had sales to the 2-wheeler OEMs, but in Q2, our sales to Japanese OEMs have also started.

items.statement: Net debt INR 160 crores, net debt/net worth 0.08x; ROCE 21%, targeting 25%; long-term borrowing reduced to INR 170 crores
items.quote: Our gross debt has come down by about INR 14 crores, making our total net debt to INR 160 crores and net-debt to net-worth is about 0.08x. Capital employed at INR 1,873 crores and our ROCE is about 21% with our focus to increase this to about 25%.

items.statement: Implemented freight rate hikes across all sectors and geographies; realization per ton increased ~8% YoY to INR7,241
items.quote: As communicated during the last call about the increase in freight rates, we have successfully implemented the freight rate hikes across all the sectors and geography.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 14% YoY, driven by rate hikes, fuel cost control, and lower hired vehicle dependency
items.quote: The EBITDA has increased by 39% from INR98 crores to INR135 crores, and percentage to revenues increased from 14% to 17%.

items.statement: Expect 4-5% tonnage growth in H2 FY25 at current realizations; better tonnage growth in FY26; EBITDA margin of 16%+ sustainable
items.quote: Going forward, also in next half year, we're expecting at least around 4% to 5% growth in the tonnage with the current realizations what we are having.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex ~INR350 cr including INR240-250 cr for Bangalore facility, INR20-22 cr for Mysore, INR30-40 cr/quarter for vehicles, plus INR44 cr dividend
items.quote: With that, the total investment in next half year, if these projects are going to be invested, then total investment will be around INR350 crores.

items.statement: Industry demand muted; VRL grew volumes 4% YoY via 82 new branches added YoY (2.5% contribution) and existing customer share gains
items.quote: Even though we saw muted growth in quarter 2 by most of the companies across the sectors, we are still in a position to show growth in volumes.

items.statement: LTL ~90%, FTL ~10%; textiles 16-18%, agri commodities 9-10%, others 5-6% each; door-to-door 35-38% of business
items.quote: Yes, LTL is around 90%. FTL is around 10%.

items.statement: Cautious on fleet addition; will add own vehicles only if sustained demand, else use hired vehicles; branch expansion focused on East/North/Northeast
items.quote: No, basically, it will be a cautious decision. See always what we do, we add the vehicle only if the vehicles are required for our operations.

items.statement: Fuel procurement from refineries at 35% of consumption (optimum); saving INR2-2.5/litre vs retail; bulk purchase increased from 30% to 35%
items.quote: The refinery is now we can say it is at the optimum level. There are 1% or 2% changes will be there.

items.statement: FY26 capex predominantly for vehicles; capacity addition ~3-4% per year matching 4-5% tonnage growth
items.quote: In 2016, again, predominantly, the capex will be towards vehicle itself. Based on the quantity improvements, we will decide on the investment into the vehicles.

items.statement: Fixed costs ~30-35% of revenue (employee, rent, insurance, taxes); grow ~8% annually; operating leverage to improve margins with volume growth
items.quote: See, almost around 30%, 35% of our costs are fixed in nature, especially the employee cost is fixed in nature.

items.statement: Pemetrexed RTU received K-code approval in Q2 enabling premium pricing and profit share revenue
items.quote: So, the main reason why we are seeing increase in US sales is with Pemetrexed, we are seeing the profit share revenue started kicking in from the current quarter, and it will start growing in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Slow quarter-on-quarter uptake recovery from major oncology API customer Intas after FDA warning letter remediation
items.quote: And now we are seeing quarter-on-quarter a slow uptake from them. And I think in the upcoming quarters, we should see good traction with Intas also.

items.statement: Multiple complex product filings and approvals across oncology, non-oncology, peptides, biologics and formulations
items.quote: It has been a very exciting quarter for us, full of excitement where we had multiple complex product filings and few approvals, which gives us confidence that we are in the right path for monetizing our assets.

items.statement: USFDA remediation activity expected to complete by end of Q3 FY25
items.quote: On USFDA remediation, the company is seriously working as mentioned in the previous quarter, and our remediation activity is expected to complete by end of Q3.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR430 crores fully utilized for debt repayment and working capital
items.quote: So, as we speak, entire QIP proceeds have been utilized for the purpose for which it was raised, and our monitoring agency also has given us a report specifying that it's been closed now.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to reach 35% region by H2 FY26 or earlier
items.quote: Once we restructure these things, we should be in the region of 35% tax rate overall.

items.statement: Albumin therapeutic grade filing and approval expected sometime in FY27 after Phase III study
items.quote: So, sometime in FY27 is something we should be able to file and get approval for the launch.

items.statement: Unicycive Therapeutics received NDA acceptance with US FDA in Q3 FY25, approval expected next financial year
items.quote: In the Q3 FY25, they have received NDA acceptance with the US FDA, which we have recently announced, which is very important milestone for the company, and we are expecting approval in next financial year.

items.statement: Tranxemic Acid expansion validation batches from Q3 FY25, commercial supplies from Q4 FY25
items.quote: And from the Q3 onwards, we are planning to start the validation batches, and we will start having commercial supplies from Q4.

items.statement: Nilotinib Europe DMF approved, Lenvatinib Europe DMF submitted, 2 new product validations to finish by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Nilotinib which was first DMF with our captive formulation with a non-infringing strategy. The European DMF, it received approval in the current quarter. Lenvatinib, Europe DMF also we have submitted in the current quarter.

items.statement: Bortezomib RTU NDA approval received in Q2 FY25, only US company with ready-to-use subcutaneous injection
items.quote: Second NDA product, which is Bortezomib RTU, which is a subcutaneous injection, for which we are the only company currently in the US to offer ready-to-use subcutaneous injection. We received NDA approval in current quarter.

items.statement: Semaglutide lab development completed, plant validation planned Q4 FY25; Liraglutide formulation validation batches Q4 FY25
items.quote: Semaglutide lab development is completed in current quarter. And we are planning to take this product for the plant validation in Q4 FY25. Teriparatide, which is the product peptide, which we had developed for osteoporosis, the product lab validation is completed in current quarters.

items.statement: Promoter share pledge for small personal requirement, expected to clear in 6-9 months
items.quote: This was for some of their personal requirements, a very small requirement for which they had placed a small percentage as pledge.

items.statement: Expect modest growth for full year FY25, exiting H2 at enhanced levels with positive margin impact
items.quote: Overall, we see a year of modest growth for the full year but exiting the second half at far more enhanced levels with a positive impact on margins.

items.statement: Alkaline battery multi-product facility planned; location decision by mid-December, commercialization targeted by October 2025
items.quote: we should be able to take a call by the middle of December or thereabouts. A final decision. While you know our wor k on machine building and on many other parameter or other equipments has already started and they are in fairly advanced stage of progress

items.statement: Peak debt expected around INR 400 crore after adding INR 150 crore for alkaline plant to current INR 256 crore
items.quote: So, while the existing debt will be keep reducing as per normal repayment schedule and there will be additional INR150 crore added to that. So, you can fairly see it will be a INR400 crore at a peak.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 13.2%, H1 FY25 13.7%; PAT margins 8.1% and 8.3% respectively
items.quote: EBITDA reached 13.2% and 13.7% of revenue for the quarter and the half-year respectively. Similarly, PAT stood at 8.1% and 8.3% respectively.

items.statement: Battery segment H1 EBITDA margin 17.5%, flashlight 11.5%, lighting 2.5%
items.quote: The percentage for H1 will be 17.5 for the battery, 11.5 for the flashlight and 2.5 for the lighting business.

items.statement: Battery segment saw modest contraction due to weak rural demand; alkaline batteries grew 62% in value
items.quote: The overall segment saw modest contraction, primarily arising out of weak demand from the rural segment. However, our diversification within battery types showed positive momentum. Our alkaline battery segment saw an impressive 62% growth in value.

items.statement: Flashlight revenue grew 16% in Q2 and 7% in H1; rechargeable segment now 50% of mix
items.quote: Backed by these tailwinds, the category had a decent 16% revenue growth during the quarter and 7% for the half year.

items.statement: Alkaline battery manufacturing facility to be multi-product; may include carbon zinc and flashlights
items.quote: We are planning for this facility to be a multi-product facility and eventually other categories will also be produced here.

items.statement: KKR arbitration status unchanged; matter moved to InCred and now NBFC companies, awaiting next hearing
items.quote: So, the status remains the same. So, there is no further update on the KKR th ing. As we have said that in the past that from the KKR it has moved to some other party called Incred and from InCred it has now moved to some NBFC companies. So, we are waiting for the next hearing

items.statement: Lighting business targets INR 400 crore revenue for sustained break-even; 5% EBITDA margin at INR 500-600 crore
items.quote: We have maintained the annual level. We said that INR400 crore is a very good number to become a break-even for our organization, seeing the past trend.

items.statement: RTM benefits expected from Q3 FY25 onwards, full scale in Q4; focused on revenue growth via efficiency not cost reduction
items.quote: I have already told that from the Q3 onwards, the benefit will start reaping on and of course, Q3 starts showing that and Q4 will have the full scale here. So, H2 will have the benefit and what intended objective of the RTM exercise.

items.statement: Alternate channels (modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce, electrical) contribute 16% of revenue (~INR 60 crore in Q2)
items.quote: Alternate channel basically constitutes 16% of the total revenue. So, around INR60 crore in the total mix.

items.statement: New product launches: Siren torch with panic button, Bheemlite for farmers; power banks coming soon
items.quote: One was called the Siren with a panic button for the vulnerable at times of distress. Bheemlite is the other one with a differentiated offering designed for farmers who need to keep night vigil to protect their crop.

items.statement: H1 FY25 segment revenue: Batteries INR 456 crore, Flashlights INR 108 crore, Lighting INR 166 crore
items.quote: So, segment wise revenue for H1. Batteries for us is a INR 456 crore, flashlight INR108 crore and lighting is INR166 crore.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR300 crores may be delayed to FY26, with a potential shortfall of INR50 crores plus or minus
items.quote: I think INR300 crores guideline e ffect in May June which we are going to start in Bangaram that happened in December. items.statement: H2 FY25 capex expected to be INR40-50 crores
items.quote: In H2 we will invest around INR40 crores to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Expect 8-9 months good occupancy at Bangaram and Thinnakara, exceeding EBITDA margin expectations; strong travel agent enquiries from South India
items.quote: We are very much confident that Bangaram out of 12 months and Thinnakara out of 12 months we will host 8 months, 9 months good occupancy which will go ab ove EBITDA margin expectation

items.quote: No, there is no update from the government for the Varanasi property. items.statement: NSE listing targeted after March 2025 balance sheet finalization, once 3-year reserve surplus and capital criteria of INR75 crores each year is met
items.quote: We are going to achieve these norms in March 2025. As soon as the balance sheet for March 2025 is final, we will list to the NSE also. So we are already under process to register to list before NSE.

items.statement: Transitioning to half-yearly earnings calls instead of quarterly; next call after annual results release
items.quote: In line with this approach, we have decided to transition to ho lding earnings calls on a half- yearly basis instead of quarterly. This revised schedule ensure s a more meaningful discussion of our achievements and initiati ves, avoiding the short-term fo cus often associated with quarterly updates. The next earnings call will be conducted fol lowing the release of our annual results

items.statement: H2 FY25 will outperform H1 with aerospace and defence as key growth drivers for revenue and profitability
items.quote: We guide that the H2 will outperform H1 with our main growth drivers of aerospace and defenc e, which will be key drivers for this performance, both in terms of revenue and

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA guidance of INR160-170 crores may be impacted by INR5-6 crores due to automotive losses
items.quote: the guidance that what we gave perhaps may be impacted in totalit y by about, you know, maybe about INR5 -6 crores

items.quote: right now, Sameer, it's in a single-digit range. I think it will go to low double digit.

items.statement: Aerospace outlook bullish with steady revenue growth; won $15 million aerostructures work package
items.quote: We are optimistic about maintaining strong growth in this vertical. This is backed by the fact that the company has won a critical work package on aerostructures. The contract value is about $15 million.

items.statement: Repaid INR52 crores from QIP proceeds in Q2 FY25 to retire long-term debt; refinancing OCD of INR67 crores
items.quote: In Q2 of FY '25, the company has repaid a further amount of INR52 crores from the QIP proceeds to retire long-term debt. The company is in the process of refinancing an existing OCD of INR67 crores.

Dr. Ravinarayanan's extensive 4 decades association in the Indian aerospace and defence sectors equips him with a deep understanding of government policies.

So, around 1% comes from the price realization improvement, and around 1% comes from the price which we have been negotiating with the raw material suppliers and also the softening of the prices. Rest is the addition of the value-added product at the consumption improvement.

items.quote: I think the kind of numbers which Maruti is declaring now , t hose were expected from the beginning , and that ha ve already been expected it to whatever we are planning for this

items.quote: Our lithium-ion business continues to be challenging. However, we are able to see green shoots in the pivot that was done earlier this year, and we are very hopeful that good results will be expected soon.

items.quote: As of September 30, 2024, the company has total order book position of INR4,406 crores, which can be bifurcated as 52% of the EPC road project and HAM project, whereas 23% of the total order book is for irrigation project and balance 25% is for pipeline project.

items.quote: With a recent election behind us and clear government emphasis on the road and highway development, we anticipate an increase in new order work. We are aiming for order inflow of approximately INR6,000 crores to INR8,000 crores for the next year.

items.statement: Standalone revenue guidance for FY25 is INR3,500-3,600 crores
items.quote: Overall, we are definitely last year we did INR4,000 crores. So this year we are targeting because there may be some shortfall. So we may touch somewhere around INR3,500 crores to INR3,600 crores turnover in this year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 13-14%; aiming to exceed guidance
items.quote: Because our guidance is always actually between 13% to 14%. We will try to achieve more than our guidance only.

items.quote: Actually, so-far we did in Q2, we did around INR4 crores only. So first-six months, we did around INR13 crores only. So definitely next this year, we are not really seeing any capex we are going to incur.

items.quote: So the gap is a little bit building up there. We just ask them why the delays that is happen ing. They say that the acquisition of land is not adequate. So until they achieve the 80% land position, they would like to hold these tenders

items.quote: Actually this year they have targeted, it's around INR5 lakh crore actually in the current financial year. That is a MoRTH target. And out of that, around they have sanctions for INR2 lakh crores by end of December.

items.quote: EPC is very, very worse now today. So we have to focus more on this HAM project as well on BOT. So and second thing -- another irrigation due. If all t hat comes, we will be comfortably running the company without any hassles and without taking additional debt or anything

items.quote: I think if they resolve that loan issue, then these things will be resolved. I am hoping, sir, very uncertain it is. I can say within two months it can be solved.

items.quote: The additional equity requirement of INR436 crores to be infused as INR200 crores INR120 crores and INR116 crores for H2 FY '25, FY '26 and FY '27 respectively.

items.statement: Pricing depends on cost of funding; will increase if cost of funding goes up, reduce if it comes down
items.quote: The pricing is depending on the cost of funding. If the cost of funding goes up, we will increase, if the cost of funding is coming down, we will reduce that.

items.statement: Good demand for gold loans across all geographies, not restricted to any region
items.quote: As I said earlier, we feel that there is more than an opportunity, we feel that we are serving people by being able to give loans. So there is a demand coming from all over the country, everywhere, it's not restricted to Northeast, West, etcetera.

items.statement: Unsecured loans becoming difficult to obtain, creating opportunity for gold loan business
items.quote: In otherwise, we see good uptick, I said earlier also, non-gold loans or unsecured loans are little difficult these days, in the last 2, 3 months. And that is definitely an opportunity for gold loan business.

items.statement: No regulatory overhang perceived; positive attitude maintained on compliance
items.quote: Yes. That's always our desire and our hope also. So, I think we should have a positive attitude on that, sir.

items.statement: NPA increased to 4.3% from 3.98% due to giving more time to genuine customers; credit costs not rising as loans are in the money
items.quote: Sometimes the NPA numbers go up, last time it was 3.98. Today it is 4.3. But since we are in the money, and we are not losing any money on that, we are not very much concerned with that.

items.statement: Credit cost roughly 1% of gross loan assets; write-offs INR16 crores in Q2, INR12 crores in Q1, rest ECL provisions

items.quote: We have branches with maybe INR10 crores, INR12 crores, INR17 crores, INR25 crores, INR30 crores and INR40 crores, INR50 crores also. So it only means that a branch can take INR30 crores, INR40 crores also.

items.statement: Standalone AUM INR90,197 crores, consolidated AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore; gold loan portfolio grew 18% to INR13,285 crores in H1

items.statement: Highest ever gold loan disbursements to new customers: INR10,687 crores to 996,000 new customers in H1
items.quote: This half year, we also saw the highest ever gold loan disbursements to new customers of INR10,687 crores that is to 9 96,000 new customers.

items.statement: Personal loan book INR1,200 crores, up from INR800 crores a year ago; sourced through 40 dedicated branches, not digital
items.quote: So I think we had today a book of about INR1,200 crores, personal loan. Probably, a year back, it could have been about INR800 crores.

items.statement: Home Finance AUM up 55% YoY to INR2,441 crores; disbursements up 90% to INR529 crores; PAT INR17 crores
items.quote: Home Finance also increased its loan AUM and 55% growth year -on-year and now stands at INR2,441 crores. There is also an increase in the loan disbursement of 90% year -on-year at INR529 crores.

items.quote: First quarter, it is INR69 crores. This quarter, it is INR250 crores. So total put together, it will be around INR320 crores.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth of 5% to 7% for FY25

items.statement: Envisage early teens revenue growth for FY26 and FY27
