items.statement: Q3 and Q4 expected to be strong due to pent-up demand from Q2 inauspicious periods, festive season, and stable pricing
items.quote: With the impact of deferred decisions from Q2, as well as stable pricing (Prices have not gone up significantly). So, stable pricing, deferred demand or pent-up demand from Q2, as well as the traditional strong seasonal activities, should give a strong boost to not only launches, but more importantly on the volumes during the second half.

items.statement: Mid-market products now averaging INR 6,700/sq ft vs pre-COVID sub-INR 5,000 levels due to conscious portfolio quality improvement
items.quote: Our mid-market products are now averaging around INR6,700 per square feet compared to less than the sub-INR5,000 levels we saw in the pre-COVID level. Clearly, it's not just a market improvement. It is also a conscious effort taken to raise the project mix curve or quality of our project portfolio with a better product offering and better market mix.

items.statement: ED search related to FIR against former minister; company not involved as alleged, cooperated fully, process ended smoothly
items.quote: The Company is not involved as alleged and is not related to Shriram Properties. The FIR was filed during Sep'24. In this regard, the Enforcement Directorate carried search operations at the premises of Shriram Properties and certain management personnel. The company has cooperated with the ED on their document requirements, and provided all the documents as required.

items.statement: H2 FY25 handover target of 3,300-3,500 homes; Q3 alone targeting ~1,000 handovers
items.quote: 3,300 homes is what I would say the target for ourselves. In last 2, 3 years, we have done nearly two-thirds of handovers happened during second half. And therefore, we remain confident and optimistic about reaching this range of 3,300 to 3,500 homes to be delivered in second half.

items.statement: Pune project launch expected by late November or early December 2024 post municipal clearance after Maharashtra elections
items.quote: We think we'll launch during this quarter, we will launch either by late November or early December we should be able to kick off. We want to launch this before the Christmas season starts.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue recognition deferred by INR 150 crores due to OC delays in three projects; expected to be recognized in Q3/Q4
items.quote: Three project revenue recognition deferred to Q3, our second half. As a result, our Q2 revenues were only INR155 crores. That took a toll, even though the gross margin was still okay. 30% margins were still there.

items.statement: Expect more than 20% to 25% volume CAGR growth over the next 3 years
items.quote: We believe on quantity and other parameter, there should be always a growth of more than 20% to 25% volume CAGR growth.

items.statement: FY25 total capex expected at Rs 150 crores, with Rs 115 crores for expansion project and Rs 35 crores for routine capex and land
items.quote: The total CAPEX for the year should be in the range of 150. Out of that 115 would be towards this project and the balance left over 35 include few of the routine CAPEX and few of the pilgers of small dia and the land cost which we have also acquired in the last quarter.

items.statement: First phase of expansion project set to launch by March 31, 2025
items.quote: Our capital investment in the expansion business is progressing with the first phase set to launch in March 2025.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 340 crores with execution cycle of roughly more than 120 days
items.quote: Our order book remained robust at Rs. 340 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for Q2 FY25 at 17.9%, H1 FY25 at 19%; expect current margin levels for next 3-4 quarters before improvement
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 17.9%. On H1FY25 basis EBITDA showed a growth of 42.5% standing at Rs. 88.9 crores with margin at 19%.

items.statement: Management expects present margin levels for at least 3-4 quarters due to market penetration and manpower investments
items.quote: So, for at least three to 4 Quarter we can expect the same level of margin which we have right now, or we look forward for the better margin.

items.statement: Realization dip of 5% versus March 2024 and 8-10% versus internal budget due to steel price correction
items.quote: We are in 8% to 10% then the internal budget which is primarily due to realization dip of 5% versus March 2024 and also 8% to 10% versus our internal budgets.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 2.7x YoY, now 33% of total revenue; expect export share to remain above 25% in coming quarters
items.quote: Venus has delivered impressive export performance this quarter with export revenue growing by 2.7X despite high freight rates, export now make up one third of our total revenue, which is a strong milestone for us.

items.statement: Domestic demand remains solid with healthy order inflow from oil & gas, engineering, chemicals and power sectors
items.quote: We see a major opportunity in sectors such as oil and gas , engineering, chemicals and power with the healthy inflow of orders.

items.statement: Seamless pipes grew 21% YoY in Q2 and H1; welded pipes declined 2% in Q2 but grew 13% in H1; both segments achieved over 30% volume growth in H1
items.quote: Sales from seamless pipes showed strong growth increasing by 21% year-on-year for both the quarter and the first half of FY25 . Welded pipe however show ed a slight dip of the 2% in Q2 though for H1FY25 sales grew by 13

items.statement: Targeting low double-digit market share in coming years driven by fittings and value-added pipes
items.quote: We are confident of increasing our market share to low double digits in coming years given our foray into fittings and value-added pipe and tubes.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates increased significantly in Q2, softening margins; expect rates to subsidize going forward
items.quote: there had been good export growth but in the last quarter there was a hefty increase on the side of ocean freights being paid on while you export the goods to various part of the world. That has rose by quite significant number. So, that is slightly soft en the margins

items.statement: Aramco and other major oil & gas approvals under process; expect most approvals within 6-9 months
items.quote: Hopefully every month or every quarter we are getting some of the approval from the some of the new company. So, I believe that most of the oil and gas companies, or particular what segment we are operating, what sizes we are manufacturing right now will able to get in the period of 6 to 9 months with most of the oil and gas companies.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: seamless >85%, welded ~60%; targeting 85-90% seamless and 70% welded by year-end
items.quote: It's more than 85% on the front of seamless and around 60% on the side of welded.

items.statement: Inventory days around 120 days; intend to maintain similar levels
items.quote: Inventory days are around 120 days sort of.

items.statement: Oil & gas sector currently not double-digit in mix; expect to touch double digits in coming year with approvals
items.quote: it's not currently double digit for oil and gas. But we believe going forward with many of the approvals coming in and again supplying to the larger pla yer in the country also we should be touching double digit in coming year to come

items.statement: Aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons of bromine for the year including captive use
items.quote: We aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons for the year of bromine, including requirements for our own use.

items.statement: Expect more than 1 million ton volume run rate for industrial salt in coming quarters
items.quote: H2 is generally better for our business, and we expect more than a million ton volume run rate in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect meaningful contributions from SOP next year
items.quote: At present, there's a work-in-progress, and we expect meaningful contributions in the next year.

items.statement: Expect healthy contribution from Clear Brine Fluids in coming quarters
items.quote: We have seen some favorable progress in these products and expect a healthy contribution in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect two Oren Hydrocarbons plants fully operational within next few weeks with meaningful business contributions from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Investing GBP 15 million for 21.33% equity in Clas-SIC Wafer Fab Limited UK
items.quote: Our company will be investing to the tune of GBP 15 million for a 21.33% equity share capital with a primary subscription of GBP 10 million and secondary purchase of GBP 5 million.

items.statement: Investing nearly USD 12 million in Offgrid Energy Labs for 21% stake
items.quote: We will invest nearly USD12 million in series A fund for the subscription of 21% stake.

items.statement: Capex of INR 50-75 crores over next 6 months for existing initiatives including Oren Hydrocarbons and derivatives
items.quote: I think our initial year after this outflow of investment on the equity side, for the next 6 months, we don't see too much of capex apart from what we're doing with Oren, I think maybe I would broadly put with existing initiatives, probably we will probably be between INR50 crores to INR75 crores over the next 6 months at the very most.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 36%
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR898 million for this quarter, Q2, with a margin of 36% and net profit stood at around INR219 million.

items.statement: H1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 37%
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR1,747 million for the 6 months period with a margin at 37%.

items.statement: Bromine demand recovering domestically, export market soft; China stimulus expected to gradually improve demand
items.quote: We expect steady demand in the bromine business with end-use applications either stable or recovering. With the recent stimulus in the Chinese market, we foresee China economy to pick up gradually and the demand for our key products recover as well.

items.statement: Producing second grade of Sulphate of Potash with encouraging inquiries from global and domestic markets
items.quote: We have also taken steps to produce a second grade of Sulphate of Potash, which we're seeing encouraging inquiries from both global and domestic markets.

items.statement: Cyclone Asna caused loss of 472,000 metric tons of industrial salt worth INR 40.18 crores; insurance claim initiated
items.quote: We reported an exceptional item due to the impact of Asna cyclone in Gujarat that occurred in the month of August and in the beginning of September. So almost it prevailed for more than a week or so, which resulted in a loss of 472,000 metric tons of Industrial Salt, which amounts to around INR40.18 crores. We have initiated a necessary claim process with respective insurance companies.

items.statement: Flame retardants project delayed but not derailed; taking measured approach focusing on current initiatives first
items.quote: I think it's a commercial call. It's not derailed for sure. I think it's delayed, as I mentioned, I think on the previous calls as well. It's easy to always put capital, but I think we want to take a measured approach.

items.statement: Secured technology exclusivity in India for silicon carbide MOSFETs via Clas-SIC investment; roadmap 2-3 years to commercialization
items.quote: The road map from concept to commercialization will take between 2 to 3 years as a part of the first phase of this new initiative.

items.statement: Urban discretionary demand slowdown seen as temporary blip; cautiously optimistic for H2 with structural tailwinds
items.quote: Looking ahead now, we believe that the current slowdown in the urban discretionary demand is, we believe and hope that it's more of a temporary blip and not structural. We remain cautiously optimistic for the second half of the year and should benefit from some specific structural tailwinds in H2.

items.statement: Expect return to healthy growth from Q4 FY25, particularly from December onwards
items.quote: So, in summary, we expect these expansions, along with the upcoming SulaFest, to provide a boost to our wine tourism business and contribute positively to H2 performance. And in particular, we are looking to return to healthy growth from Q4, in fact, from December onwards.

items.statement: Elite and premium portfolio grew 7% YoY; share reached all-time high of 78.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our elite and premium portfolio grew 7% year-on-year for the quarter, while economy and popular was down 18%. Share of elite and premium in our own brands improved 500 basis points, reaching an all-time high of 78.5% in quarter two.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 78 bps to 74% in Q2 FY25 driven by premium mix; EBITDA fell 24% to Rs 34 cr due to higher marketing spend
items.quote: Our gross margins stood at 74%, 78 basis points better versus last year, supported by higher share of elite and premium. Gross profit stood flat at Rs. 104 crores. Our expenses increased by around 21%, primarily due to the higher selling and distribution and marketing costs.

items.statement: Domaine Sula expansion near Bangalore to complete in Q3 FY25; 30-key resort at York Winery in FY26 to raise room capacity 30% to 134 keys
items.quote: Furthermore, the ongoing expansion of our wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore is slated to complete in Q3. So, we have a beautiful new tasting room there with a beautiful vineyard view, a bit akin to our facility in Nashik, which was a bit lacking until now.

items.statement: Telangana grew 59% in Q2; revenue ex-Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% YoY
items.quote: Telangana stood out with a growth of 59% during quarter two. Success of second force strategy, as Rajeev alluded to, also helped Sula's sales force to focus better and drive premium portfolio in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Unsustainable competitor discounting in Maharashtra impacting net sales; wine tourism hit by poor road infrastructure and outbound travel surge
items.quote: There have also been, I would say, some kind of unsustainable discounting by some of our competitors. Unfortunately, the market does not have the kind of depth to allow it to easily withstand this. So, there is a fair amount of wine that has been produced, which is unfortunately being discounted in the market.

items.statement: Reopening Andhra Pradesh after 5-year hiatus; targeting first shipment in Q3 FY25
items.quote: These include the reopening of Andhra Pradesh, which would be after a hiatus of five years for us. We had voluntarily withdrawn from the state five years ago, and we are quite pleased that it is reopening with a more progressive excise policy. So, we hope to be getting back in there pretty shortly.

items.statement: Adding four new brands to CSD, nearly doubling portfolio; CSD showed strong growth over last 18 months
items.quote: We will be seeing the introduction of four more brands in CSD. CSD, I should point out, has shown very strong growth over the last 18 months or so. And we will be introducing four new brands, including our Dindori Reserve Shiraz and also our Source Grenach e Rose, our Sula Vineyards Riesling, and our RASA Syrah

items.statement: Resuming BSF shipments after 8-month gap; BSF performed well in H1 FY24
items.quote: We are also resuming shipments to BSF after eight months. And BSF did incredibly well for us in the first half of FY '24. So, it was a shame that due to some administrative issues we were not able to be present. We are now getting back in there, and we will get the benefit of that in H2.

items.statement: SulaFest returning in February 2025 after 5 years as wine and beer festival; likely biennial event
items.quote: A word on SulaFest. We come back after five long years due to overwhelming popular demand. This was a festival that was much loved and had grown into being one of India's iconic festivals. We had to shut down due to COVID. And for various reasons, after that, we decided not to restart. But now we do believe the time is right.

items.statement: Evaluating third state for new winery; decision likely within next year
items.quote: In terms of new wineries, you are absolutely right that the time has come for us to look at other states. And in fact, we are taking a close look. And I believe that more likely than not, within the next one year or so you would see some action on that front.

items.statement: Wine tourism spend per head up 9% YoY in Q2; tastings up 6% to over 50,000, an all-time high for Q2
items.quote: Spend per head and tastings, these will be the two key metrics for us. On both fronts, we did pretty well in Q2. Spends per head, as I just said, grew 9% Y-o-Y. And pan-India tastings are up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, so an all-time high for Q2.

items.statement: Delhi excise portal migration disrupted September shipments; portal now mostly restored
items.quote: In Delhi, the excise portal was offline for much of the second half of September as they migrated from external management to in-house management of the portal, and which impacted sales during this transition. We were, in fact, unable to ship goods for most of the second half of September in this very important market.

items.statement: Karnataka excise policy changes caused temporary stocking hesitation; situation mostly stabilized with sales recovery underway
items.quote: In Karnataka, retailers were initially hesitant to stock up due to recent changes in the exercise policy, which introduced pricing uncertainty. This situation has since mostly stabilized after clarity came in from the state authorities, and we have started seeing already a recovery in sales there.

items.statement: Revenue less service cost margin target of ~20% by summer next year (next three quarters)
items.period: next three quarters / summer next year
items.quote: So by summer of next year, we should be looking at this number getting to about 20%.

items.statement: Current adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue less service cost is ~15%
items.quote: This INR13.6 crores of adjusted EBITDA margin is on INR93 crores of revenue less service cost, which is almost a 15% margin.

items.statement: Hotel & packages gross margin expected to rationalize to ~10% long-term (9-10% range over next 3 years)
items.quote: Over the next three years, given that the business would be largely focused on corporate and mice, I would expect this number to be range bound between nin e and 10

items.statement: Synergies from Globe acquisition expected slightly ahead of initial INR60M/year target
items.quote: As part of the combination of Yatra and Globe, we had identified synergies of approximately INR60 million per year. And as we move forward, we expect that we should be able to realize synergies slightly ahead of this initial target.

items.statement: Onboarded 29 new corporate clients in Q2 FY25 with INR1.2B annual billing potential
items.quote: In the second quarter of FY25, we onboarded 29 new corporate clients, collectively adding an annual billing potential of INR1.2 billion.

items.statement: Corporate air volumes show healthy double-digit growth; B2C air volumes stabilized and gradually increasing
items.quote: We continue to see healthy double-digit plus kind of volume growth on the air ticketing side on the corporate front. On the B2C front as well, as I mentioned, we've reached a point where we've been able to stabilize the volumes and the last couple of months we've started seeing a

items.statement: B2B now ~60% of gross bookings; hotels & packages ~65% B2B; Globe adds 360 corporate clients
items.quote: So in terms of gross bookings, now almost 60% of our gross bookings are coming from the corporate travel business, from the B2B business.

items.statement: International air ticket prices easing, expected to soften further in Q4
items.quote: The part which is getting a bit impacted on that, and this is not a negative thing, is just that the international air ticket prices are finally beginning to ease off a little bit and we would expect them to soften a bit more in the fourth quarter of the year.

items.statement: Globe acquisition: INR1.28B cash; Globe FY24 adj revenue ~INR470M, adj EBITDA margin >30%; 60% air / 40% hotels gross bookings split
items.quote: Globe Travels last year reporting adjusted revenue of approximately INR470 million and adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 30%.

items.statement: Q3 underlying earnings expected to remain range-bound vs Q2 reported levels
items.quote: As of now, the trending seems to indicate that they shouldn't come off. They should remain range bound to what we had just reported.

items.statement: Management expects recovery to be gradual over next few quarters, not sudden, with focus on offline scale-up and Mamaearth experiments
items.quote: So, our entire focus is on that. That's said we expect the recovery to be gradual and not sudden when it comes to sort of getting back on the growth path that you talked about.

items.statement: Medium-term target of high double-digit EBITDA margin remains unchanged despite short-term investment skew
items.quote: But our view on being able to get to a high double -digit in the medium term for ME continues to hold strongly.

items.statement: Investing in R&D capabilities and partnerships to make hero products beat competition in blind testing across focus categories
items.quote: Our objective here would be that we build capabilities that in all our focus categories, our hero products actually beat the competition in blind testing and that's an area where a few of our products are already ther e but it's a constant journey through dedicated investment that we are going to continue to be on from an organization perspective

items.statement: Focus categories (face cleansing, serum, sunscreen) grew 28% in H1; aim to extend to 5-6 categories over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Our three strongest categories where we have the best shares and ambition also is the strongest in those 2-3 categories which is face cleansing, serum, and sunscreen have actually demonstrated 28% growth in half one and we want to make sure that this focus category approach we are able to extend that to five to six categories over the next three to four quarters

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin impacted ~10.7% YoY due to Rs. 63 cr inventory returns, gross margin loss, inventory and trade provisions
items.quote: So, there's a loss of gross margin, there's an inventory provision and also, we provided certain, trade loss related provision on top of it, which is impacting this close to 10.7% impact from a year-on-year perspective on our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Urban consumption patterns changing; structural shift recognized but not yet fully understood
items.quote: There clearly seems to be some form or change in terms of consumer buying in patterns which are visible, but we genuinely want to see that and understand that as a structural change.

items.statement: Mamaearth top 10 SKUs contribute 40-45% vs 75-80% for mature offline brands; need to narrow focus to hero SKUs
items.quote: For most others, top 10 SKUs would probably, especially in the offline kind of environment, contribute to 75%, 80%, while for Mamaearth, it will be about 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Dubai distribution case ongoing; favorable India High Court judgment but unfavorable first appeal in Dubai; appeal filed in Dubai High Court
items.quote: We have a favorable judgment in Indian High Court, but in the first appeal in Dubai, the judgment has not been as favorable. That said, our lawyers are very confident on the construct of our case.

items.statement: Offline GTM overhaul (Project Neev): 70% ward cells have distributors deployed; remaining 30% to be covered in 3-4 months
items.quote: Currently, in about 70% of them, we have been able to deploy distributors but there are at least 30% of the ward cells where we are still deploying distributors and that will happen over the next three to four months

items.statement: Young brands (ex-Mamaearth) grew 30%+ in H1; Derma Co. doing phenomenally well with face wash entry scaling
items.quote: The young brands continue to demonstrate very healthy growth. And each one of them at H1 and quarter two level also have grown at 30% +, which is a great sign for the company as they scale and become much larger.

items.statement: Staze (color cosmetics) at Rs. 25 cr+ ARR run rate; early days in new category and mass-plus price point
items.quote: And it actually is already at a Rs. 25 crores plus run rate ARR. And we believe we will continue to learn on it and get our basics even stronger to win that category in early days, but yes, good signs.

items.statement: Inventory correction impact higher than estimated (Rs. 63 cr vs Rs. 40-50 cr guided) due to sub-stockist and trade inventory not initially accounted for
items.quote: But during the same period when we have actually executed this, they've also taken inventory from sub-stockists which owed them money, as well as to some extent in certain cases trade. And all of that has resulted in a higher net inventory take back compared to what we had estimated it to be.

items.statement: Offline ASPs 20-25% higher than mass market; offers retailers higher bill value and margins to drive adoption
items.quote: One, of course, as you premiumize a category in our ASPs, in almost all categories are higher by 20% to 25%. And that gives the retailer higher bill value per transaction and if your margins are higher compared to what they've been selling in the past, for the retailer, there is a much higher opportunity to sort of, make better money.

items.statement: Online consumer proclivity shifting toward actives/derma vs naturals; naturals seen as long-term consistent proposition
items.quote: in a ch annel like online, the proclivity towards actives and derma brands is far higher compared to naturals and we have different brands to play on to those different propositions and we need to invest accordingly to win in the category

items.statement: Media strategy overhaul: shifting from impulse/seasonality to always-on deployment; media mix modeling with internal and external data science teams
items.quote: The changes are not only towards the type of media, but also how we deploy media, where we were very impulse and seasonality-focused, instead of which we need to be far more always-on, in terms of our spread of media on these focus categories.

items.statement: Mamaearth pilots for new playbook starting in Q4 FY25 across 8-10 test cells (state/subcategory) with Bain partnership
items.quote: Now, what we are trying to do as part of pilots is taking cells like, a one state and or one subcategory and implementing a very different kind of a playbook on the same, getting into all of that is work is planned, starting now in Q4 and then seeing if it generates disproportionate results in that cell. And there are 8 to 10 such pieces which we want to activate in action

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 50%+ for FY25 with EBITDA margin around 8%
items.quote: In terms of overall current financial spending, as we have been mentioning in the past also, is to maintain the same spend that the company will be growing at 50% plus for the current year as compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Target ROE/ROCE of minimum 15% within 2-3 years and 17% in next 3 years
items.quote: So, first of all, the company is extremely confident and positive that we will achieve ROE, ROCE of minimum 15% in time to come, very shortly, within a span of two to three years, for sure.

items.statement: INR 240 crores capex over 3 years for Hisense AC facility (1.5M units capacity)
items.quote: And the estimated capex over next three years for AC business is around INR 240-odd crores. So we said $30 million, so that's almost INR 240 crores is what we are estimating in investment to create a capacity of 1.5 million air conditions over next 3 years.

items.statement: INR 40-50 crores capex for existing facilities over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So a max of INR 40-odd crores, INR 50 odd crores is what we're looking at in terms of investment in the existing facilities.

items.statement: Hisense partnership targets $1B revenue over 5 years across AC, washing machines, refrigerators
items.quote: This alliance aims to generate $1 billion revenue over next five years serv ing both India and global markets and leveraging our manufacturing expertise to drive innovation in home appliances

items.statement: Gross margin decline in Q2 due to AC mix shift (70% vs traditional 40%); H1 margins stable YoY
items.quote: So like, although we are not reporting on a segmented basis, but at the same time, the margins in small home appliances is comparatively better, or slightly more as compared to AC. So when the overall revenue mix has changed, this has led to the decline in margins on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at ~8% for FY25 (vs 8.12% last year)
items.quote: The guidance on margin remains the same. We have been maintaining that last year we achieved a margin of 8.12% the EBITDA margins and we are targeting to achieve similar kind of margins around 8% for the current year as well.

items.statement: AC 70%+ of Q2 revenue (vs 40% traditionally); small home appliances lines starting Q4; washing machine pilot done in Q2
items.quote: So Bhoomika, the mix for the current quarter is, AC contributing almost again, it's 70% plus in this quarter and non-AC, nearly 30%.

items.statement: Sricity plant capacity utilization target: 30% by FY25 end, 60%+ in FY26
items.quote: So, by end of this year, the overall capitalization what we are targeting should be a minimum of 30 percent from Sri City in this year. And next year onwards, we definitely look to further improve it to at least 60% onwards.

items.statement: Industry AC growth expected at 35-40%; company to outpace market; 17-18% CAGR over 3-4 years
items.quote: Even industry we can see is now talking about a growth of minimum 35% to 40%. So definitely that's one area.

items.statement: Commodity and forex fluctuations fully passed through to key customers (95% revenue) with ~1 quarter lag
items.quote: So, any change in commodity forex is a complete pass-through to most of the larger brands. So, all the key customers, if we talk about who contribute on the 95% of overall revenue, we have an arrangement whereby all the commodity fluctuations and forex fluctuations are passed on.

items.statement: Plain copper BIS certification (effective Oct 17) creates short-term supply challenge; domestic production expected from December
items.quote: Especially, I think the industry is talking about BIS on plain copper, which has become effective as of 17th of October this year. So, definitely, to certain extent, because the current capacities in India are not enoug h to meet the industry requirement, there is definitely a challenge

items.statement: INR 230 crores IPO proceeds in fixed deposits to fund Hisense capex and growth
items.quote: So actually, Mr. Amarnath, in terms of funding the upcoming new projects that the company is planning, the company already has a kitty from the IPO proceeds, which currently lies unutilized. Hence, we have a fixed deposit of INR 230 crores with us lying in the bank, which will be used towards funding the new upcoming projects.

items.statement: Exports grew 300% YoY; targeting US/other markets pending certifications by end of Q3
items.quote: So, there is almost 300% growth in our exports last year, but still the overall contribution is small. So, exports needs a lot of new products, I'll say additional product development.

items.statement: Asset turnover target: 4.5x consolidated, 5-6x for Hisense JV (current 3.25-3.5x)
items.quote: With the way we are diversifying into new product segments, we are targeting an asset turn of minimum 4.5. And this new company, because this will not be investing into a lot of backward integration, which will be catered by our existing investment. And the new company's asset turn would be anywhere between 5 to 6.

items.statement: Cost of capital 8.75-9%; working capital debt increase due to intentional non-discounting of invoices
items.quote: Cost of capital is 8.75% to 9%.

items.statement: Expect sustained double-digit growth in business in quarters ahead
items.quote: We expect sustained double-digit growth in our business in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Expect ARR growth in excess of 10% and double-digit ARR growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, based on these statistics, we strongly feel that our growth rate will be in excess of 10% in terms of ARRs. Another very significant point is that we are now entering the festive and wedding season . This will also help in terms of the business and in terms of the ARRs going up. Last year, the ARR during H2 actually increased by close to 15%. And this year also , we expect that the ARRs would

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 remains Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 160 crore
items.quote: We have said the CAPEX will remain in the range of Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 160 crore. That will remain the same.

items.statement: Well booked on all wedding dates in hotels for season through March
items.quote: We are well booked on all the wedding dates in our hotel.

items.statement: Tea room EBITDA margin around 35%, cafe above 20%, kiosk about 10%
items.quote: In case of tearoom, as we opened in Mumbai, near the Gateway of India; so overall, the margin is 20% and for that tearoom margin will be around 35%. The cafe margin is also higher. Kiosk margin is on the lower side.

items.statement: Plan to add 250 new Flurys outlets over next five years, targeting 350 total
items.quote: Over the next five years, we aim to approximately add 250 new Flurys outlets, significantly enhancing our presence and market share in the fast-growing bakery and confectionery sector.

items.statement: Shift Flurys mix toward cafes and tea rooms from kiosks; plan 40-50 new outlets per year
items.quote: We are going to be more focused on opening more cafes and tea rooms. Our earlier strategy was to have a blend of kiosk cafes and tea rooms. There is a slight change in strategy. We are going to be opening more cafes and more tea rooms.

items.statement: Expect hospitality super cycle to last over a decade driven by connectivity, business travel, FTA recovery, middle-income expansion, spiritual tourism, weddings, MICE, wildlife, de-leisure
items.quote: We are in the starting phase of the hospitality sector super cycle and expect this cycle to last for over a decade, if not more. The industry's growth will be driven by improved connectivity, increased business travel, recovery of FTAs and the expansion of the middle-income segment. Spiritual tourism, weddings, MICE, events and wildlife tourism and a new segment of de-leisure are also expected to

items.statement: Plan to more than double keys from 2,410 to 5,048 over next five years including 830 owned keys
items.quote: Currently, we operate 34 hotels totaling 2,410 keys and over the next five years, we plan to more than double the number of keys, taking the total number of keys to 5,048. This inventory of 5,048 rooms will include 830 keys, which we will build on our own and will be owned by us.

items.statement: The Park Pune to open April 2027, Park Vizag additional 100 rooms by October 2027, Park EM Bypass Kolkata by April 2028
items.quote: The 200-room, The Park Pune, is now on course to open in April 2027. The Park Vizag additional 100 rooms by October 2027 and the Park EM Bypass Kolkata by April 2028.

items.statement: Expect ROCE to rise from 12.5% to over 20% in coming years
items.quote: We expect ROC E to go up from the present level of 12.5% to over 20% in the years to come.

items.statement: Lotus Palace Chettinad opening rates Rs. 12,000-20,000; Ran Baas Patiala Rs. 35,000-40,000, expected to reach Rs. 40,000-50,000+ by year end
items.value: Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 20,000 and at Ran Baas The Palace at Patiala in the range of Rs. 35,000 to Rs. 40,000
items.quote: Opening rates and bookings at the Lotus Palace Chettinad are in the range of Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 20,000 and at Ran Baas The Palace at Patiala in the range of Rs. 35,000 to Rs. 40,000. During this season between October and March, we feel that this range is expected to go up further.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic acquisition and lease opportunities; Ranthambore 50-room lease concluded for Dec/Jan opening
items.quote: We are exploring inorganic opportunities, which are acquisition including lease. One lease we have just specified, 50 room on lease, which has been concluded at the stage, which is the Ranthambore property. So, ready-made rooms now will be available from December or early January . We are trying additional lease properties also and, acquisition opportunities. But they are under discussion.

items.statement: Target waste neutrality by 2025, water neutrality by 2028, carbon neutrality by 2032
items.quote: We plan to achieve waste management neutrality by '25, water neutrality by '28 and carbon neutrality by '32.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant 70-75% installed; tube mills and slitting line ready, awaiting power connection expected within one month
items.quote: The plant is I would say is 70%-75% already installed in Jharsuguda. Once the power line which is also very close government contractors are working at it.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected in Q3 and Q4 FY25 from pipe volumes, new products, and Jharsuguda contribution starting in December
items.quote: So now we are expecting in quarter 3 and quarter 4 there will be a revenue growth. The reason for revenue growth will be one market has come back to normal, the election time is over although there was election going on Maharashtra, but now that is also over and plus this is the end quarter 3, quarter 4 always see all the targets has to be completed, so the growth will always be higher.

items.statement: Crash barriers averaging 500-800 tons per month; transmission line orders of 650 tons in Hyderabad; monopole machinery ordered for April arrival, production start by June FY26
items.quote: Crash Barriers, the new product has also already hit up we are hitting a constant average of anywhere between 500 tons to 800 tons in a month and we are expecting this to increase because now more and more road contractors are getting aware of our presence in the market and they are getting aware of the products that we are making and our quality.

items.statement: New products (transmission, crash barriers, poles) expected to contribute at least 2% higher margins than pipe business; GI pipe saves Rs 3/kg, transmission saves Rs 5-7/kg
items.quote: In terms of how much it is variable, but you can consider as at least 2% higher than what it generally reflects in Pipes more than that. But at this point in time you can consider 2%.

items.statement: Demand recovery seen in October after election slowdown; steel pipe prices rising; Q3 and Q4 expected to be strong due to project completion timelines
items.quote: Our sales have picked up in October and that has been reflected in our production also production value, production quantity and our dispatched value and dispatched quantity as well. So we are hopeful and we are positive that the demand is now going to be very steady for our Steel Pipe and Black and Galvanized for quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Monopole machinery order placed; plasma cutter and pole closing machine arriving, press brake ordered from China expected April arrival, production start by May-June FY26
items.quote: We have just placed the order for it. We are expecting this machine to arrive India in April, so we can say that by May or June this domain we should be able to enter successfully.

items.statement: Hyderabad transmission line orders total 650 tons; crash barriers steady at 500-800 tons/month; monopole attracting contractor interest at exhibitions
items.quote: There are 2 orders that we have procured the total order at this point in time in Hyderabad is 650 tons for transmission line.

items.statement: H1 FY25 degrowth due to central elections slowing government projects; Maharashtra elections also impacted Q2
items.quote: This year because of the central elections the demand, the projects and the government everything has been slow which has reflected in quarter 1 and quarter 2.

items.statement: FY26 expected to be a game changer for both revenue and margins with new product lines and Jharsuguda plant fully operational
items.quote: Absolutely, we are very positive on that because we have seen a lot of positive response from the market and we have really entered into this domain. So yes, what you have understood and I am glad that we have been able to translate it to you and I think you have understood exactly what we are doing and how we are implementing it.

items.statement: Jharsuguda to start crash barriers, power transmission lines, octagonal poles, and high mast poles by end of December alongside steel pipes
items.quote: By the end of December in Jharsuguda besides Steel Pipes and Galvanized Pipe, Highway Crash Barrier, Power Transmission and Pole all of them shall start at the same time.

items.statement: Export GI pipe volume increased by 300-400 tons
items.quote: Exports, we increased by 300 tons – 400 tons for increase of export GI Pipe.

items.statement: Overall TAM will be close to $120 billion in next four to five years with significant headroom for growth across all four business segments
items.quote: in next four to five years, our 14 overall TAM will be close to $120 billion. So we have a significant headroom even in our India multi -channel core business

items.statement: Plan to open a couple of EBO stores in international market next year
items.quote: I think you should see a couple of stores in the next year.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved 100 bps year-on-year to 37.3% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Gross margins in Q2, it has improved by 100 basis points from 36.3% to 37.3%.

items.statement: India Multi-channel Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.6% in Q2 FY25 from 7.4% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA is improving year on year from 7.4% in Q2FY24, we have reached to 8.6% in Q2 FY 25.

items.statement: International business EBITDA loss narrowed to 18.9% in Q2 FY25 from 22.8% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA performance, on a year on year basis, i s clearly improvin g from 22.8% negative in Q2 FY24, we have brought this down to 18.9% in Q2FY25

items.statement: GlobalBees Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 2% in Q2 FY25 from 1.2% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA performance is improving quarter on quarter and year on year and there is 2.5x jump in EBITDA in Q2 FY25. So from 1.2%, we ha ve improved this to 2% in Q2 FY 25

items.statement: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 4.2% in Q2 FY25 from 3.2% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: Consol EBITDA as well, its improving every year. From 3.2% in Q2FY24, w e have improved this by 100 basis point to 4.2

items.statement: Annual unique transacting customers increased 16.5% year-on-year to 9.4 million as of Sep'24
items.quote: Annual unique transacting customers have improved. It increased by 16.5% from Sep'23 to Sep '24 ending.

items.statement: Total store count including modern stores is 1,124 as of 30th September
items.quote: Total store count that we have including all modern stores is 1,124 as of 30th September of this year.

items.statement: Education business has 300+ schools as of end of September
items.quote: End of Septembe r, we are already sitting on the , number of schools are already 300

items.statement: Online GMV split 77% vs 23% offline in India Multi-channel as of Q2
items.quote: As of Quarter 2, our online GMV split and offline GMV split in India Multi-channel has been 77% vs 23%.

items.statement: Online-offline mix expected to remain stable around 76-77% online historically
items.quote: If you see the historical trends as well, if you see a disclosure we have made in the prospectus also, for last 3-4 years, the mix between online and offline, it remains in the same trajectory, probably 1% here and there.

items.statement: GST search and seizure operation at Pune corporate office and warehouse from Nov 6-10; paid INR 1.74 Cr including interest for four assessment years
items.quote: we have paid a total amount of INR 1.74 Cr t o the GST authorities, which includes the mismatch amount as well as the interest component for four years which is AY18 -19, AY 19-20, AY 20-21 and AY22-23

items.statement: Invested INR 85 Cr of committed INR 170 Cr in GlobalBees as convertible equity; hold 50.73% stake
items.value: INR 85 Cr invested of INR 170 Cr committed
items.quote: Out of INR 170 Cr, we have already invested around INR 85 Cr in GlobalBees for them to increase their stake as per what we have agreed in prospectus. In terms of our shareholding in GlobalBees today, we hold around 50.73% shareholding in GlobalBees.

items.statement: Category growth driven by shift from unorganized to organized; only 16% organized currently
items.quote: We are in a category, its 16%, I would say only organized. A lot of industry is getting from unorganized to organized and we are the largest player, so we'll continue to gain and benefit from that.

items.statement: Expect CCR to keep doing better in H2 FY25 and aim to make up for H1 weakness with higher CCR growth
items.quote: We expect our CCR to keep doing better over the H2. There's a factor of seasonality of course, but due to elections and limited business travel, as a result of that this year the effect has been a little higher in H1. But we are hoping to make up for it with a higher CCR growth in H2.

items.statement: EBITDA margin decreased 307 bps to 14.8% in Q2 FY25 due to higher ETS mix and operating costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin decreased by 307 bps to 14.8% in Q2 FY '25 as against 17.8% in Q2 FY '24. This was mainly on accounts of the increase in cost of operations and service.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 14.4% vs 17.4% in H1 FY24 due to higher ETS operating costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was at 14.4% and H1 FY '25 as against 17.4% in H1 FY '24. This decline was mainly on account of the increase in cost of operation and service.

items.statement: CCR demand picked up from September onwards with 15% Q2 vs Q1 revenue growth
items.quote: So, if you look between Q1 and Q2, there's been a growth of CCR of almost 15% in Q2 versus Q1.

items.statement: ETS revenue grew ~40% YoY in H1 FY25 to Rs. 191 crores from Rs. 130 crores
items.quote: So, ETS has grown in the first half, the ETS business was around Rs. 191 crores, this grew from last H1 was around Rs. 130 odd crores.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue split: ETS 62%, CCR 38% vs 51% ETS and 49% CCR in H1 FY24
items.quote: So, between the two businesses, between CCR and ETS, as of this H1 our breakup is 62% with ETS where we have seen larger growth and larger demand that was there in ETS. So, that is right now 62%, while the CCR is 38%. At the same time last year H1 it was 51% was ETS and 49% was CCR.

items.statement: Margin compression driven by higher ETS operating costs, not pricing pressure or contract inability
items.quote: So, the entire effect is due to a higher operating cost of ETS per se. So, when a section of the business, which is a higher operating cost, that increases more than the other business, that is the only effect, it has nothing to do with any kind of price pressure that we are facing from clients in either of the segments.

items.statement: Reduced debt by 50% from Rs. 21.7 crores to Rs. 11.5 crores; debt-to-equity from 0.12 to 0.06
items.quote: During this period, we have reduced our debts by 50% from Rs. 21.7 crores in FY '24 to Rs. 11.5 crores in H1 FY '25. This reduced our debt-to-equity from 0.12 to 0.06 during the same period.

items.statement: Added 59 cars in H1 FY25 including hybrids and EVs
items.quote: During the H1 we have added 59 cars in total which comprise some hybrid cars and some EVs.

items.statement: Aspire to sustain 20%+ CAGR revenue growth; focus on wallet share expansion and sales team scaling
items.quote: I think we have grown 20-plus-percent CAGR over the last 20 years. And we can aspire to keep increasing this. items.statement: Owned fleet maintained at 5-10% of total; future capex opportunistic based on client demand
items.quote: For next year, again, you see, we would always keep our owned fleet between 5% to 10%, which is something that has shown us to get the maximum and the most wisest return on capital employeed into our own assets. Beyond this, if we see opportunities which makes sense, so we would be opportunistic on that.

items.statement: Expect to grow ahead of the industry driven by demand continuity, rural and urban recovery, 125cc ramp-up, new launches, and brand building
items.quote: We are optimistic about the growth prospects of two-wheeler industry and with the continuity of demand and recovery in the broader two-wheeler market for us, both rural and urban, ramp-up of 125cc portfolio, new product launches and strong investment behind building power brands, we expect to grow ahead of the industry.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin guided at 14% to 16% range despite continued growth investments
items.quote: As far as our margin is concerned, we always maintain the overall tramline of 14% to 16%. And of course, our financials allowing flexibility.

items.statement: ICE EBITDA margin improved 160 bps to 16.5% in Q2 FY25 due to mix improvement, lower material costs, and LEAP savings
items.quote: The EBITDA margin during the quarter for ICE business improved by 160 basis points to 16.5%, driven by mix improvement, lower material costs and LEAP savings, while we continue to invest behind brand building and new business.

items.statement: Will continue investing aggressively behind EV and Premium growth priorities including brand building and new model launches
items.quote: And that allows us the flexibility to, and the headroom, to invest even more aggressively behind our growth priorities, which we have talked about earlier, namely EV and Premium specifically.

items.statement: Premium portfolio expanding with Xpulse 210, Xtreme 250R, Karizma XMR 250, and ICE scooter refresh with Destini, Xoom 125, Xoom 160 within next 6 months
items.quote: So what we're going to do is we're going to come out with Xpulse 210, which is liquid cooled, and you talked about EICMA, we unveiled there. So you have the details there. Xtreme, as I sa id, power brand keeps getting bolstered where Xtreme 160, we then launched 125R, which has done very well. And we want to launch Xtreme 250R

items.statement: EV scooter portfolio expansion covering all price points by end of calendar year and further expansion within 6 months
items.quote: On the scooter side, while we are selling the 2 models right now, you will see addition happening and expansion to other price segments happening by the -- within -- before the end of this year, calendar year. And within 6 months of that, you'll see even further expansion going into other user segments.

items.statement: Festive season saw balanced double-digit growth in both rural and urban markets with strong consumer buying behavior continuing
items.quote: Both are double digits, yes.

items.statement: Positive medium-term outlook as bottom-of-pyramid participation increases supported by government capex, monsoon benefits, and wedding season
items.quote: I would actually say as we move forward the next 4 to 6 to 8 quarters, as the b ottom of pyramid starts participating more, this would actually benefit the economy, of course, and the -- but auto sector, in particular, and especially whichever is arising out of the rural

items.statement: Highest-ever festival sales of 1.6 million units in 32 days with 16% revenue growth and Vahan market share of 31.6%
items.quote: We clocked the highest-ever festival sales of 1.6 million units this festive season, 16% revenue growth in the festive period of 32 days, reiterating the confidence customers have with Hero.

items.statement: EV retail volumes scaled to 11,600 units during festive with 20% market share in 5 cities and 10% in 10 cities
items.quote: We further scaled up to 11,600 units during the festive and gained 20% market share in 5 cities and 10% in 10 cities during the festive period.

items.statement: Realization per unit improved by ₹2,700 QoQ driven by two-wheeler mix (₹1,400) and parts business, expected to continue improving
items.quote: Our realization during this quarter compared to Quarter 1 has improved by almost ₹2,700, right. That's two-wheelers actually contributing ₹1,400 out of which and the balance coming from the parts business.

items.statement: Hero FinCorp saw delinquencies and collections slow in H1 FY25 impacting profitability; taking steps to improve collections in H2
items.quote: In the first half of this financial year, we've seen the delinquencies and the collections slowing down. And so as a result of that, that has really impacted the profitability of HFCL, right.

items.statement: PLI benefits for EV products expected to start accruing from FY26 as products become compliant
items.quote: So in FY'26, you'll see our products getting compliant with PLI, and those benefits will start to accrue.

items.statement: Premia store expansion at 58 activated stores targeting breakeven within 12-18 months with strong dealer interest and NPS improvement
items.quote: We already activated 58. And there is a path forward to even accelerate that.

items.statement: Global business grew 30% YoY in H1 FY25 vs industry 16%, market share up 60 bps to 6.1% in Q2, with Colombia turning EBITDA positive
items.quote: if you look at the firs t half, we did grow 30% versus the industry growth of 16% as far as the global business is concerned. And therefore that led to an increase in the market share to 6.1% in Quarter 2, which you compare sequentially is up by almost 60 basis points

items.statement: Sold close to 30,000 vehicles to institutional buyers including quick commerce and food delivery segments during festive season
items.quote: And in fact, to these segments in this festive, we would have probably sold close to around 30,000 vehicles with big buyers being the usual ones who do quick commerce and food deliveries.

items.statement: Engineering division order book stood at INR 3,580 crores at end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: At the end of the Q2 financial year '25, the total order book for the engineering division stood at INR 3,580 crores.

items.statement: Expect roughly 15% to 20% growth during current year on full year basis for engineering division
items.quote: We expect roughly between 15% to 20% growth during the current year on a full year basis.

items.statement: Roha plant expansion CAPEX of roughly 275 crores for primary production facility
items.quote: Well, we are expecting the plant to deliver somewhere around 2.5 times asset turn to the total CAPEX of roughly 275 crores which is on the primary production facility.

items.statement: Expect commercial production at Roha plant to commence in first quarter of FY25-26
items.quote: The expansion of the Roha plant for the manufacturing is in advanced stage and we expect the commercial production to commence in the first quarter of FY'25-26.

items.statement: Chemicals division expected to close year at roughly 15% growth standalone and 12% to 14% consolidated
items.quote: So for the year as a whole, we are expecting to close on a standalone basis at roughly around 15% growth, and on a consolidated basis, growth of roughly between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Engineering segment margins suppressed by 150-200 basis points due to one adverse project
items.quote: Well, we've not really spoken about specific numbers, but I can tell you that the impact of this on our engineering segment margins is significantly upward of 150-200 basis points.

items.statement: Overall company operating profit margin likely to be around last year's level due to adverse contract impact
items.quote: Therefore, we are likely to be at around the last year's margin percentage.

items.statement: Domestic enquiry remains robust and hopeful for finalization of large value opportunities in next few months
items.quote: The domestic enquiry remains robust and we are hopeful for the finalization of some large value opportunities in the next few months.

items.statement: Order inflow for first half was around 726 crores, Q2 inflow of 578 crores nearly double previous year
items.quote: The order inflow for the first half was around 726 crores.

items.statement: Consumer products division expecting roughly 30% growth by end of current year and aspiring to reach 500 crores revenue
items.quote: We are expecting the business to grow by roughly around 30% level by the end of the current year and the size of the business is in the range of around 10 %- 11% of our revenues at the moment and it has been at roughly that level for quite a while. But we do see that the current trends are quite favorable and we are aspiring to reach a figure of 500 crores in the near future.

items.statement: Membrane facility recently expanded and planning further expansion, announcement to come when plans finalize
items.quote: We've just expanded capacity on our membrane facility and we are planning to expand that further. We will make an announcement once those plans take full shape.

items.statement: Sri Lanka contract has significant uncertainty on fund allocation, roughly 10% invoicing remains
items.quote: But roughly around 10% or so of the invoicing still remains to be made. We can only say that there is a significant degree of uncertainty about when the funds will get allocated to it and how much.

items.statement: UP contract execution dependent on government fund flow and approvals, not fully predictable
items.quote: However, the execution of the contract is quite dependent upon the flow of funds which are allocated and approved for our contract, as well as the various approvals that we receive from the government and that's not unfortunately a very predictable thing.

items.statement: H2 FY25 will be significantly better than H1 for UP contract execution
items.quote: Yes, H2 will be significantly better than the first half.

items.statement: Chemicals capacity utilization at 65-70% based on nameplate capacity, actual varies by product mix for optimum revenue and profitability
items.quote: The nameplate capacity is based on a particular product mix and the actual product mix can vary based on considerations of optimum revenue and profitability. Which is why you don't really see that the nameplate capacity being achieved.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin was 13.6% in Q2 FY25, down 70 bps sequentially due to raw material cost pressures.
items.quote: Consolidated operating margin for the quarter stood at 13.6% down about 70 basis points sequentially mainly on account of RM cost pressures.

items.statement: Price increases of 2% in truck segment and larger quantum in PCR segment taken in domestic replacement; under-recovery from last year is about 6%.
items.quote: So, broadly we have taken price increase ranging from 2-odd percent in the truck segment to a larger quantum in the PCR segment. The under-recovery from last year is about 6-odd percent.

items.quote: There is no change in our CapEx guidance for FY25 and we will continue to focus on profitability, free cash flow generation and improvement in the return ratios as we go ahead.

items.statement: Expect demand momentum to improve in H2 FY25; RM cost to slightly increase in Q3 then decline from Q4 onwards.
items.quote: In terms of demand outlook, we expect the demand momentum to get better in H2. We expect the RM cost to slightly increase in Q3 and then start coming down from Q4 onwards.

items.statement: Ultra High Performance segment accounted for 47% of PCT volumes in Europe in Q2 FY25 vs 39% in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: Ultra High performance segment accounted for about 47% of PCT volumes in Quarter 2 of FY25 compared to 39% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: India Operations EBITDA margin was 12.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 13.8% in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 5.4 billion, a margin of 12.1% compared to 13.8% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Europe Operations EBITDA margin was 14.8% in Q2 FY25 vs 13.7% in Q1 FY25 and 14.1% in Q2 FY24.

items.quote: So both for TBR and PCR full year the replacement should be around a double-digit growth. Right now, in near term, the signs of recovery from OE are not there. So in near term, it will continue to be probably in the same zone.

items.statement: Other expenses elevated due to freight costs, EPR implementation, and advertising; freight rates hard to predict, advertising controllable, EPR constant.
items.quote: The increase in the other cost is on account of freight costs where the freight rates went up. Secondly on account of the EPR which was not there last year and thirdly on account of advertising.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement over time; Q3 RM still strong with 3-month lag, volume growth positive; Q4 margin increase if RM keeps falling.
items.quote: I don't see it springing back in Quarter 3, but I'm very positive on my volume growth in Quarter 3. And that should release some margin. Going forward, if all goes well and RM still keeps coming down, there will be a margin increase in Quarter 4.

items.statement: RM cost up ~8% sequentially in Q2; expect ~1% increase in Q3 then decline from Q4.
items.period: Q2 FY25, Q3 FY25, Q4 FY25
items.quote: So Raghu, the RM went up by about 8% sequentially. Our expectation going forward is just about a 1 percent-plus increase for Q3. And then as per current expectations the RM should start coming down.

items.statement: Truck price hike 2% half reflected in Q2, rest in Q3; PCR hike ~3% half reflected in Q2, rest in Q3.
items.quote: On the truck side, we've taken about half of the price increase of the 2% in the current quarter which will flow through, and on the passenger car side, a larger chunk, about 3% has been taken in the current quarter which would only have reflected partially in the current quarter.

items.statement: Energy costs in Europe hedged 60-70% for next one year.
items.quote: So, I would say over the next one year, our energy cost would be hedged about to the extent of 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Europe winter tyre demand sensing decent for current quarter; growing over last year.
items.quote: As of now it seems to be a decent quarter. We are growing over last year. Still don't have the figures of the market, but the current sensing is we feel good about the quarter

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue target of INR2,200 crores despite current slowdown

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin sustainable around 16% plus
items.quote: I think for the less -- we should look at a number around 16% , then it will be done. That is not an issue. And margins, sometimes it's an impact of some marginal price increases, sometimes is the impact of freight, et cetera. It's a mix impact. Sometimes it go by 0.5%, 0.2% here and there. But it should be around 16% plus, it should be around that in the long term.

items.statement: New order book announcement expected within 15-20 days
items.quote: Yes, we are working on that. Hopefully, within the next 15, 20 days, we will announce the new order book we have got. We are waiting for one more order. If it comes, then it w ill be a decent amount to

items.quote: And this total will be around order book of around INR60 crores per annum and plus hopefully, very, I think, within next 15, 20 days, we are expecting a huge order from them. And again, a fourth phase we are getting with them.

items.quote: And in the joint venture of Marelli, as you are aware, we have got INR1,000 crores order from them. The supply -- there are some design changes and the new samples are in progress. items.statement: Pune Phase 2 plant to be completed by March 2025, targeting INR60-70 crores revenue next year
items.quote: next year, I'm targeting a business of INR60 crores to INR70 crores from this plant, number 2 plant
