items.quote: As of September 2024, our consolidated order book stands at a robust INR 602 crores, representing sequential growth of 27%.

items.statement: Current order backlog around INR 600 crores; India business 5 months, international business 8 months to fulfill
items.quote: Yeah, so current order backlog is around INR 600 crores and for India business, it would be around five months and for international business, it would be around eight months.

items.statement: No capex project planned for upcoming year; only replacement capex
items.quote: For upcoming year, as such, no capex project is planned. We will stick to the replacement capex only.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margins for GLE business seen at 17-20% long term; current margins reflect recent order book downtick
items.quote: I think the sustainable EBITDA margins in the GLE business range between 17% and 20% in the longer term.

items.statement: Filtration and drying business sustainable margins at 16-18% long term; historically over 15-17%
items.quote: We believe that sustainable margins are in the 16% to 18% range, even with the current economics and dynamics.

items.statement: Thaletec standalone sustainable margins expected at 15-17% long term
items.quote: The margins, as we believe, on a long-term sustainable basis will be in between the 15% to 17% range for Thaletech standalone.

items.statement: Pharma driving uptick in GLE segment; chemical inquiries building but not yet converting to orders
items.quote: We are seeing that pharma is showing a stronger growth and we are seeing more interest from our pharma customers than we are seeing from the chemical.

items.statement: Filtration and drying seeing good uptake from pharma; healthier order book will reflect in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We are seeing a good uptake and encouraging demand coming in from the pharma industry, and especially during the recent quarters.

items.statement: Pharma share of revenue historically 35-60%; currently at lower end, expected to rise; agrochemicals and fine chemicals share to reduce
items.quote: Historically, pharma has ranged from a low of 35% to a high of almost 60% in our overall revenues. We believe that that end will be retained and will of course, it's a pretty wide range, but it will be within that range is what we expect.

items.statement: No plans to enter Chinese market; market fragmented with 20-30 players, not a priority
items.quote: So, we don't have a plan to venture into the Chinese market. Predominantly, the Chinese glasslined equipment market, especially, while this is true for the entire process equipment market, but this stands especially true for glasslined equipment. So, it's a very, very fragmented market with something like 20, 30 different players within the Chinese glasslined equipment market.

items.statement: Joint venture with Clean Max Enviro Energy by acquiring 26% stake in Clean Max Anchorage for up to INR 3.36 crores for captive solar (2.31 MWp) and wind (3.30 MW) in Gujarat
items.quote: We are excited to announce the joint venture with Clean Max Enviro Energy Private Limited by acquisition of 26% stake in Clean Max Anchorage Private Limited for a total investment up to INR 3.36 crores.

items.statement: Debt repaid INR 35 crores in H1 FY25; expect to double to ~INR 70 crores for full year
items.quote: I think to answer it very simplistically, we did INR 35 crores in half a year. So I would assume we should double it for the whole entire year.

items.statement: Thaletec range launched in India two quarters ago; ~25 equipment sold or under execution; doing better than expectations
items.quote: We launched the Thaletech range of solutions in India about two quarters ago. And over the last two quarters, we have made significant effort in promoting these products, as well as we have generated not just a strong interest, so in terms of order pipeline, but also we have now close to 25 odd equipment, which are either sold or currently under different stages of execution.

items.statement: Kinam integration phase 3 underway; NCLT filing for amalgamation in progress; breakthrough order in oil & gas
items.quote: We have received stock exchange approval for scheme of amalgamation of Kinam Enterprise Private Limited with HLE Glascoat Limited and are now in the process of filing the application with NCLT.

items.statement: Service revenue currently 5-7% of sales; pure after-sales may reach 10% optimal; automation and retrofit packages also serve service orientation
items.quote: So while service has, so strictly speaking, service in the traditional sense, it constitutes between 5% and 7% of our, or maybe roughly, let's say closer to 7% of our sales.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guidance revised to around INR80 crores from earlier INR100 crores
items.quote: I don't think we'll be able to achieve INR100 crores, but let's say, ballpark is about INR80 crores EBITDA level.

items.statement: Panoli plant commercial production expected within 3-4 months, full revenue potential INR200-250 crores over 3 years
items.quote: Over a period of 3 years, INR200 crores to INR250 crores is what we are looking at achieving from Panoli plant.

items.statement: New API products at Panoli include Ticagrelor, Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Lacosamide, Riociguat, Edoxaban
items.quote: These products include Ticagrelor, Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, and some new products like Lacosamide, and we are targeting to complete another new product, Riociguat in quarter 3.

items.statement: Penem vial filling line to take 1-1.5 years for hardware plus 6-8 months sterile validation, ideal target 2 years
items.quote: So the Penem vial facility is a sterile facility. We may take 1 year to do the hardware. But between 6 to 8 months, it requires for sterile validation, the environmental validation because this is a product which is a lifesaving used in hospitals, and then we need to get regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Penem API prices down ~25% in last 6 months due to Chinese capacity expansion and internal competition
items.quote: Penems prices have, I mean, gone down by about 25%.

items.statement: Penem volumes increased despite price pressure
items.quote: Volumes have increased, but prices are low.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 divisional EBITDA margins: Formulations 3.68%, API ~6%
items.quote: In this quarter, division-wise margin, if I say formulations, EBITDA margin is 3.68% and API is about 6%.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis elongating supply chain cycles to Europe and UK
items.quote: Already the impact is there. Our material to Europe and U.K. are all going around the world and reaching there. So that impact is already there.

items.statement: Teva ethanol supply progressing slowly due to Israel war, next quarter business spilling to next year
items.quote: Teva is progressing for sure. We received the first order also. But time line-wise, they are moving a little slow. Mainly, it has happened due to the Israel war, so the time lines are a bit slow.

items.statement: R&D pipeline: 10+ products under development, plan to commercialize 10 products in 2 years focusing on cardiac, diabetes, CNS, newer Penems
items.quote: Apart from that, we have more than 10 products under R&D. And in the next 2 years, we plan to commercialize 10 products. Our main focus is on cardiac, diabetes and CNS, apart from the newer Penems like Tebipenem, so few Antibiotics.

items.statement: LATAM registrations expected to come through next year, Middle East GCC dossiers planned for UAE next year
items.quote: We expect many registrations of LATAM to come through next year. Regarding the Middle East, the GCC is the biggest market where registration normally takes 3 years apart from plant products. We are already working in Oman and in Yemen, and we are planning to put in dossiers next year in the UAE also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 15%+ by Q1 FY26
items.quote: we see ourselves resuming back to the 15%-plus gross EBITDA margins by Q1 end.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 15%+ expected in Q1 FY26 if export mix stays at current level
items.quote: I would say if export remains at this level that is currently going on, we will achieve 15% plus EBITDA.

items.statement: Gross margin at 23.7% in Q2 FY25 due to 7% higher basmati unit costs and 3% higher realizations
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter was at 23.7%, impacted by a 7% year- on-year increase in basmati unit costs as paddy prices were higher in the last se ason, while average sales realization in the period rose by 3

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 12.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 18.2% last year due to gross margin pressure and higher employee costs, doubtful debt provisions
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 12.1% compared to 18.2 % corresponding quarter last year, primarily reflecting the impact on gross margin as well as higher employee costs, provision for doubtful debt and other expenses.

items.statement: Domestic branded basmati volume grew 10% in Q2 FY25 and H1 FY25 despite FMCG urban volume growth of ~2.5%
items.quote: In the generally slowing FMCG market, with urban growth volumes of around 2.5% in H1, we delivered an impressive 10% volume growth in the branded basmati segment, supported by solid performance across both consumer and bulk rice segments.

items.statement: Regional rice business revenue expected at INR 275-300 crores in FY25 vs INR 200 crores last year
items.quote: So last year, we did a INR 200 crores of revenue in the regional rice business, and we're expecting it to be close to about INR 275 crores and INR 300 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Fresh orders of over 3,000 tons received from Saudi Arabia for shipment by end of December
items.quote: And we have got now fresh orders more than 3,000 tons from Saudi, which we have to export up by end of December.

items.statement: New processing plants set up in Karnataka, Gangavati, and Kandla Port for aged specialty non-basmati rice
items.quote: We have now put up a small processing plant in Karnataka also. We are putting up a plant in Gangavati also, we have already put up a plant at Kandla Port also.

items.statement: Margins under pressure for next 2 quarters due to high-cost inventory; expected to normalize by Q1 FY26
items.quote: You see we are carrying high-cost inventory. So margins will be under pressure for another 2 quarters. That is maximum. Another 2 quarters, we will be operating under 15% only, but first quarter of next financial which should come to the same glory of 15% plus.

items.statement: Inventory position by September 2025 expected to be highest ever due to aging requirements and higher procurement
items.quote: This year, our stock inventory should be higher than last year. So our inventory position in the next September '2025 should be the highest ever.

items.statement: No plans to monetize land bank; all land used for paddy storage and warehousing; buying more land instead
items.quote: We have a lot of land bank, but we don't want to sell anything. It is all in use. So we use all the land in storing our paddy and we have got about 5 million square foot of warehouses and our open land is used for storage of paddy and we are buying more land rather than selling.

items.statement: Management expects credit cycle to take at least a year to improve; sees potential improvement by Q4 FY25 if cycle started in April
items.quote: once a credit cycle starts, it takes at least a year for things to start getting back on track. And so if I say get this credit cycle started in April, which is when, it really kind of started surfacing very, very quickly. That would mean that by Q4 end we should start seeing things getting back on track or improving or getting better.

items.statement: Industry facing substantial rise in impairment costs due to overleveraging in rural retail unsecured lending and high field staff attrition affecting collections
items.quote: the industry is experiencing a substantial rise in impairment cost. This increase is largely due to over leveraging in the rural retail unsecured lending space , impacting both microfinan ce institutions and MFIs

items.statement: Company adopting cautious growth strategy prioritizing collections and portfolio health over expansion given severity of challenges
items.quote: Given these conditions, we have opted for a cautious growth strategy, emphasizing collections and portfolio health over expansion. This conservative approach is crucial to preserving the quality of our assets and maintaining a stable financial position.

items.statement: Consolidated yields at 25.4% and cost to income at 33.3% for Q2 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated yields for the quarter stood at 25.4%. Cost to income for the quarter stood at 33.3%.

items.statement: October-November collections disrupted by Diwali; rate of descent slowing but downcycle not ended
items.quote: November has been fairly disrupted due to the Diwali festival. So, as far as availability of customers and everything is concerned that became an issue. Right now, obviously its covering up and covering up very quickly, so that is good news at least. But yeah, I do not think this down cycle has ended and neither can you expect it to end. So, quick as well to be perfectly frank with you. But I woul

items.statement: MFIN guardrails being implemented; company establishing independent credit teams across all branches by end of FY25
items.quote: The MFIN guardrails have been introduced to manage overleveraging and we are currently in the process of also, establishing an independent credit teams across all branches by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 total disbursements Rs. 832 crores, down from Rs. 1,068 crores in H1 FY24 reflecting focus on asset quality over growth
items.quote: For H1 F Y ‘25 total disbursements were Rs. 832 crores, down from Rs. 1,068 crores in H1 at FY’24. This reduction reflects our decision to prioritize asset quality and to focus on collections rather than growth

items.statement: Consolidated impairment costs Rs. 99 crores for H1 FY25 reflecting current risk environment impact
items.quote: The impairment cost were at Rs. 99 crores for the first-half of FY '25, reflecting the current risk environments impact on our financia ls.

items.statement: GNPA at 3.74% and NNPA at 0.64% as of September 2024; management overlay at Rs. 114 crores with ~50% towards 31-90 day bucket
items.quote: Our assets under management as of 30th September stood at Rs. 2,465 crores, while gross non-performing assets or GNPA stood at 3.74% and net non performing assets or NNPA to that 0.64%.

items.statement: Namra plus 4 or more lenders at household level was 22.8% at origination; outstanding less than Rs. 50k for 47% of customers
items.quote: the lenders at the time of origination at household level. I mean, was 22.8%, which is Namra plus 4 or more. And Namra plus 3 would have been about 18%. Basically, if you look at the outstanding, practically none of the customers at the household level for us had a outstanding of more than two years.

items.statement: Healthy liquidity position with Rs. 281 crores in cash, bank balances, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits plus Rs. 157 crores undrawn sanctions
items.quote: As on 30th September 2024, the company has a healthy liquidity position with Rs. 281 crores in cash and bank balances, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits. In addition, the company has Rs. 157 crores of undrawn sanctions from existing lenders.

items.statement: Zero DPD collection efficiency needs to reach 98.5-99% for improvement; currently not there yet
items.quote: So, I would say things will not improve until the zero DPD bucket repayment rate goes up to at least 99%, 98.5% to 99%, which is what typically what we used to. But even if it gets back up to 98.5%, I am confident to say, okay, the worst is behind us and things will progress forward.

items.statement: Regulatory risk on high-yield MSME book (28-32% rates) being monitored; RBI discussions ongoing but no specific action against Arman/Namra
items.quote: Honestly, it is getting a bit difficult to kind of predict what is in the regulators mind at this point. And so there is a lot of guesswork involved. What they want, what their intent is, I think the intent is quite clear , d o not charge more than you want or than you should

items.statement: Customer inquiries have decreased, indicating borrowers also becoming cautious
items.quote: Even inquiries, you will be surprised, but even inquiries have gone down from the customers. Even customers are being cautious now, which is a good sign.

items.statement: Management overlay may be increased if margins and profits allow; impairment costs not expected to come down next quarter
items.quote: if our margins and profits allow, we will definitely bumper that overlay as much as we can. But that does not seem, I do not see impairment cost coming down in the next quarter or anything like that. We will just have to take it in good stride.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs. 2,900 crore by March 2027 maintained; expect high single-digit growth in FY25 and 20%+ growth in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: And that guidance which we have given for 2,900, as of now we would want to continue with that. There is no change in respect of the 2,900 by March 2027.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit revenue growth for full year FY25
items.quote: we should be ending the current year with kind of high single-digit growth kind of a situation

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 16%-17% for H2 FY25 after price hikes and volume recovery
items.quote: we should be back in that range of 16% to 17% in the coming H2

items.statement: Implemented 6% price increase for faucets and 1% for sanitaryware in September 2024 to offset 18% brass price rise
items.quote: we implemented a strategic price adjustment in September 2024, applying a 6% increase for faucets and 1% increase for sanitaryware

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at Rs. 25 crore, Rs. 11 crore deployed in H1; sanitaryware greenfield Phase 1 capex Rs. 130 crore including Rs. 25-30 crore land cost
items.quote: Our planned CAPEX for FY25 stands at Rs. 25 crore, of which we have already deployed Rs. 11 crore by H1 FY25

items.statement: Sanitaryware greenfield Phase 1 adds 1.2 million pieces per annum capacity, expected revenue Rs. 300 crore per annum, completion in 18 months from zero date
items.quote: In the 1st phase, the capacity increase would be something like 1.2 million pieces per annum. So, for that, the capital expenditure would be in the region of Rs. 130 crore

items.statement: Project business up 15% in last six months; expect strong project demand in H2 FY25 and retail pickup after elections, monsoon, heatwave headwinds ease
items.quote: If you look at the total project business, in the last six months from March to September, it has gone up by around 15%. And we anticipate a strong project demand in the coming half year also

items.statement: China imports reduced to 3% of revenue (Rs. 13 crore); most items internalized or sourced from Morbi, container rates normalized
items.quote: The total Chinese import now constitutes only 3% of our total revenue and is in the region of Rs. 13 crore only right now

items.statement: Completed Rs. 130 crore buyback of 108,333 shares at Rs. 12,000 per share; buyback tax paid by company under old regime
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully concluded the buyback of shares amounting to Rs. 130 crore. The buyback involved purchase of 108,333 fully paid-up equity shares at Rs. 12,000 per share

items.statement: Investing Rs.440 crore to add a third Bretonstone line at the Mekaguda facility, operational by March 2026, funded by Rs.300 crore debt and Rs.144 crore internal accruals.
items.quote: We are expanding our state -of-the-art quartz manufacturing facility in Telangana by adding a third Bretonstone production line. Scheduled to be operational by March 2026, this new line will significantly enhanc e our capacity while maintaining high standards of sustainable manufacturing. The investment will be funded through a mix of debt and internal accruals.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA of Rs.145-165 crore and PAT of Rs.100-110 crore from the new line once stabilized, with asset turnover of 1x-1.25x.
items.quote: profitability is typically we expect that the EBITDA from this would be in the range of Rs.145 to Rs.165 crore is what we are foreseeing at this time and PAT also we are expecting it to be in the range of Rs.100 to Rs.110 crore is what we are expecting at this time

items.statement: Believes H2 FY25 margins will be pretty close to H1 levels and targets 35% EBITDA margin sustainable with new facility.
items.quote: Yes, I think at this time, we believe that the H1 margins more or less are in line with our expectations, and we believe that H2 would also be pretty close to that.

items.statement: Product mix close to ideal 30-35% high-value, 30-35% medium, 20-25% basic plus hospitality; hospitality segment improving but not yet at target.
items.quote: So, we are pretty close to the ideal mix except for that , the hospitality has still not picked up, but it is far better than what it was in last year same time.

items.statement: US demand recovery depends on mortgage rates stabilizing below current ~6.9%; expects improvement in 12 months as Fed cuts rates and construction/remodeling picks up.
items.quote: So, I think as the mortgage rates become more stable and come down, we will see more activities happening. But then as we are positioned on a different footing compared to majority of our competition, we are focusing on mid-to-top tier products.

items.statement: Freight rates have improved significantly and are near normal levels for most US ports; ordering from distributors not impacted by freight anymore.
items.quote: Yes, so I think the freight rate situation has definitely improved compared to what we have seen in probably two to three quarters back. And of course, because this is the end of the year now, so except for that situation where distributors typically say that we want less arrivals around Christmas and New Year. Otherwise, the ordering is not impacted by the freight rate situation anymore.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty currently zero with 2.34% countervailing duty; any Trump policy changes would apply across the board, not singling out the company.
items.quote: There is already an anti -dumping duty on our product. So, we have approximately about 2.34% countervailing duty, the anti -dumping duty for this POR was set as zero. So, there is a countervailing duty of 2.34%. Now, after Trump comes back, it would be premature for me to comment as to what he's going to do. But whatever happens, it's going to happen for everybody across board.

items.statement: KREOS line commercialization in Q3 FY25 with launches in Q4 FY25; Chromia line operational by Q4 FY25 for high-definition digital printing.
items.quote: The Kreos Line is progressing toward commercialization in Q3 FY25, with exciting product launches planned for Q4 FY25. The Chromia Line, designed for high-definition digital printing, is expected to be operational by Q4 FY25, enabling us to deliver unique and differentiated products.

items.statement: Expects quarterly revenue run-rate of Rs.200-225 crore from existing capacity subject to market conditions.
items.quote: I think we expect that the numbers should be in the range of Rs.200 to Rs.225 crore subject to of course the market conditions and the situations out there.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs.228 crore at 9% cost as of Sep 2024; next 12-month repayment Rs.60 crore; peak debt expected around Rs.350 crore after new Capex debt.
items.quote: Gross debt as on 30th September, it is Rs.228 crore, and the cost of funds is around close to 9%. Regarding the additional space availability for future expansion, we do have still some space available for further expansion.

items.statement: Targeting 25% revenue from rest of world (Canada, France, Mexico, Russia) and 75% from North America over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: Now coming to the market share, yes, of course, next three to five years, our idea is also that we have a good amount of rest of the world coming in. So, whether it would be 25% or 20%, I think time would say, but definitely our target is that we have 25% definitely coming from the rest of the world and 75 % from probably. North America.

items.statement: Domestic India revenue currently minuscule; aims to reach 10% of turnover from domestic market after identifying right distribution partners within a year.
items.quote: Our focus is that always has been export market. Now looking at the Indian market and Indian growth story, we feel that the market is now right to accept our kind of product in the market. So, let's hope that we at least achieve 10% of our turnover on the domestic front. That's the first target.

items.statement: Granite business near-term outlook remains cautious; implementing cost-control measures and exploring revenue opportunities.
items.quote: Turning to our granite business, the environment continues to pose challenges, as reflected in this quarter's results. We are implementing cost -control measures and exploring opportunities to increase revenue in this division. While the near-term outlook remains cautious, we are committed to addressing these challenges with a focused and measured approach.

items.statement: KREOS technology expected to help sustain or improve margins and realizations; Chromia line more for decoration and new segments.
items.quote: So, we expect that KREOS typically would help us sustain or improve our margins and realization and CHROMIA is more of a decoration and also looking to service some other segments.

items.statement: New line ramp-up to optimal capacity expected in 12-15 months; large part of revenues visible in first 12 months; internal target to maintain 35%+ consolidated EBITDA margin.
items.quote: See, the ramp up as we have had in the first line as well, we expect that the full optimal capacity would take at least 12 to 15 months to come , because then we will have to test several things.

items.statement: Expects full-year tax rate of 25%.
items.quote: So, we are expecting 25% also for the full year.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement in profitability over coming quarters
items.quote: I would ref rain from a specific guidance. But like I would have mentioned over the last two quarters and we have delivered on that guidance is that we would see sequential improvement.

items.statement: Net debt expected to be around 20% lower by year end
items.quote: Broadly, my personal estimate would be around 20% lower than where we sit today.

items.statement: No significant capex beyond ordinary; investing in people instead of acquisitions
items.quote: There are no significant Cap ex plans. Even on the expansion one significant change which has happened, I would say, in a way in our strate gy is that we are now investing in people in a way rather than acquiring companies.

items.statement: Latin America initiatives doubled business in two months; six markets acted upon
items.quote: It is already doing well in the first two months of operations, having grown the business significantly, almost doubling the business in two months itself.

items.statement: Express business price increase announced to improve revenue and profit margins
items.quote: We have recently announced a general price increase which will align us to improve the revenues and therefore improve the profit m argins.

items.statement: International business EBITDA impacted by severance costs (~$1M) and bonus payments
items.quote: Deepal Shah: And just to add, Ravi, the severance cost is $1 million for this quarter, almost $1 million, exact number.

items.statement: Global trade strengthening; Europe may take 6+ months to revive; strong demand in select countries
items.quote: I already answered that we expect the strong demand environment in some of the select countries to continue, and Europe may take more than two quarters to revive. But globally, there's a better momentum in the market.

items.statement: Contract logistics: e-commerce largest segment; chemical logistics down to 23% of revenue
items.quote: And today when we look at the split of business , we are very pleased to note that despite continued growth, chemical logistics today comprises only 23% of our business.

items.statement: Freight rates expected to remain range-bound; capacity additions offset by scrapping
items.quote: So, we believe that freight rates will remain range bound. There are various things pointing towards an upward movement and things pointing towards downward.

items.statement: Non-core asset monetization estimated at Rs. 75-100 crores across Allcargo and Gati
items.quote: So, across Allcargo, on a consolidated basis, which includes Allcargo and Gati as well, broadly there could be non-core cash flows coming into the extent of Rs. 75 crores to Rs. 100 crores, that's the broad estimate.

items.statement: Demerger of international and domestic businesses expected by April 2025
items.quote: And by April 2025 we should have the international domestic businesses demerged and listed separately.

items.statement: Expect passenger vehicle industry to register low single-digit growth for full year
items.quote: Overall, as noted previously, we expect the passenger vehicle segment to register a low single-digit growth for the full year as an industry.

items.statement: Expect commercial vehicle demand to rebound in second half as government spending resumes
items.quote: However, we are hopeful that the demand for CVs will rebound in the second half of the year as government spending resumes and infrastructure projects regain momentum.

items.statement: Expect aftermarket to achieve high single-digit growth for full year with double-digit growth in H2
items.quote: And hence, as I mentioned in my opening remarks, for the full year, we still expect a high single-digit growth rate for aftermarket in the current financial.

items.statement: Expect consolidated EBITDA margin to sustain at 14% for full year despite headwinds
items.quote: The same is already achieved in Q1 as well as Q2 at 14%, and we expect this margin to continue in Q3 and Q4 for the remaining part of the fiscal despite headwinds.

items.statement: Target organic growth 50% above industry rate, aiming for 12-15% organic growth if industry grows 8-10%
items.quote: So if the industry grows, let's say, at around 8% to 10%, we should easily be looking at a 12% to 15% growth organically.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to expand from 14% to 15% over next 3 years with scaling subsidiaries
items.quote: And for that, with that organic growth with better operational efficiencies with the new subsidiaries scaling up, we should be able to expand those EBITDA margins further, perhaps from 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Capex outlay for FY25 estimated at INR120-140 crores with INR32 crores spent in H1
items.quote: The Capex outlay during H1 '25 has been INR32 crores. However, with many SOPs planned for the second half of the year, the Capex outlay for the whole year is estimated to be around INR120 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Incremental capex of INR60 crores over last year, targeting INR120-150 crores total for FY25
items.quote: So Capex, if you look at last year to this year, there should be an incremental Capex of about INR60 crores. Last year was around INR80 crores. This year, we are looking at anywhere between INR120 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR1,050 crores with 90% new business and 40% EV contribution
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product and domain categories is INR1,050 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 15% of the order value will mature in the current financial year FY '25, 40% in FY '26, 30% in FY '27 and the remaining residual 15% in FY '28. EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book.

items.statement: IAC India EBITDA margins expected to maintain 16-18% range in near future
items.quote: So I think we have been able to maintain EBITDA margin of roughly between, let's say, 16% to 18%. And in the near future, let's say, specifically for H2, we do expect a similar margin to be maintained.

items.statement: Stand-alone EBITDA margins improved 150 bps in H1 due to OEM scale and price corrections from Bajaj and HMSI
items.quote: So if you see the stand-alone margins with respect to the H1 last year, it has grew almost by 150 basis points and which basically includes certain economies of scale due to the higher revenue in OEM and as well as certain, you can say, the price corrections from our major OEMs, namely Bajaj and HMSI, which were basically the carry forward from the last financial year.

items.statement: GreenFuel acquisition expected to close in Q3, targeting INR300-350 crores annualized revenue with stronger EBITDA margins
items.quote: So for, let's say, on a full year basis, we are expecting anywhere between INR300 crores to INR350-odd crores of revenues with a stronger EBITDA margin than what we are looking at currently across the most of our subsidiaries and joint ventures.

items.statement: Mechatronics revenue to more than double in FY26, targeting INR200+ crores with 70-80% growth in FY25
items.quote: And mechatronics, as was explained earlier, will grow at almost close to 70% to 80% this year. And next year also, we expect the revenues of mechatronics domain to double, maybe crossing the INR200 crores mark.

items.statement: Alps Alpine targeting INR50 crores revenue in FY25 (50% growth) and INR100+ crores in FY26 driven by throttle position sensor and infotainment launches
items.quote: We should be close to INR50 crores revenue, although on a small base for the current fiscal. But as I mentioned, we have almost more than INR100 crores of order book on Alps Alpine. A significant part of this comes in FY '26, largely driven by the throttle position sensor and the in-vehicle infotainment system for 2-wheelers. And next year, we are looking to perhaps cross the INR100 crore revenue

items.statement: Tata Motors shifted from plastic to metal fuel tanks, delaying plastic fuel tank business; pivoting to roto-moulding for roofing and other applications
items.quote: I think Tata Motors has gone back to using from plastic fuel tanks back to metal fuel tanks on a lot of their models. And that's the reason the offtake of plastic fuel tanks from our perspective has, let's say, hit some sense of a back burner.

items.statement: Two-wheeler segment growth momentum to persist driven by rural economy, premium models and consumer preferences
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate this upward trend to persist, fueled by a stronger rural economy, continued introduction of premium models and evolving consumer preferences.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 13.6 billion invested in Q2FY25; expect Rs 80 billion in H2FY25
items.quote: Our capex investments are gaining momentum post fund raise and in Q2FY25 we invested Rs. 13.6 billion. We expect capex spends of Rs. 80billion in H2FY25.

items.statement: Three-year capex plan of Rs 500-550 billion; mega deals worth Rs 300 billion signed with Nokia, Ericsson, Samsung
items.quote: At the cost of repetition, I am pleased to share that in September, we concluded deals worth about Rs. 300 billion or USD3.6 billion with the three global partners, namely Nokia, Ericsson, and Samsung, for supply of network equipment over a period of three years. This is one of the key steps towards the rollout of the company's transformative three-year capex plan of Rs. 500 to 550 billion.

items.statement: Target 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025; 5G rollout starts Q4FY25
items.quote: The 4G expansion is in progress and our target is to achieve 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025. The rollout of 5G in key geographies will start in Q4FY25.

items.statement: EBITDA ex-Ind AS 116 at Rs 23.2 billion, up 10.5% QoQ; margin improved to 21.3%, highest since merger
items.quote: The EBITDA excluding Ind AS 116 for a quarter was at Rs. 23.2 billion, improving by 10.5% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. This is the highest quarterly EBITDA since merger and the margin has improved to 21.3%.

items.statement: Customer ARPU ex-M2M increased 7.8% QoQ; blended price increase ~16% but only ~8% ARPU realized due to segments with no hike and consumption downgrades
items.quote: Our customer ARPU ex M2M has increased by 7.8% QoQ. There is no tariff increase in the Enterprise post paid segment as well as M2M tariffs during the quarter.

items.statement: Entry-level tariff hike room limited; future hikes to focus on higher consumption tiers with differential pricing up to 20% at high end
items.quote: Going forward, while tariff increases are required and they will happen, I don't think there is too much of room to increase the tariff at the entry level. That then by implication means that the tariffs have to increase more at the higher consumption levels.

items.statement: Lost 5.1 million subscribers with increased port-outs to BSNL (which did not hike tariffs); port-outs declining post-August per MNP data
items.quote: We registered a loss of 5.1 million subscribers with increased port outs to one operator which has not participated in the tariff hike. We have also seen a slight dip in our 4G /5G subscribers. However, basis the latest MNP data available till October, port-outs to this operator are declining post August.

items.statement: Expect subscriber loss trajectory to turn around by end of FY25 as network investments and tariff benefits materialize
items.quote: my gut feel would be that by the end of this financial year, we should have turned around the trajectory. But this is just an expectation. I don't think it is possible to give you an exact timeline on when this could turn around.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs 136.2 billion sufficient for H2FY25 capex of Rs 80 billion; actively engaged with lenders for debt funding alongside promoters
items.quote: Post equity funding via FPO and Preferential issuance to one promoter group, we have cash and bank balance of Rs. 136.2 billion which is more than sufficient to execute our balance capex plans for H2FY25 of Rs. 80 billion.

items.statement: AGR curative petition dismissed; engaged with government for solution; conversion to equity provided in reforms package if payment shortfall arises post-moratorium
items.quote: On the AGR matter, the Honorable Supreme Court has dismissed the curative petition filed b y telecom companies. We addressed this topic in detail in the investor call held on September 23. The Government remains unequivocally supportive of 3 private player market and we are engaged with them in finding a solution

items.statement: Bank guarantees of ~Rs 24,000 crore due over one year; not factored in funding plan; seeking government waiver as industry-wide request
items.quote: The quantum of bank guarantees is disclosed in our financials i.e. about 24,000 crores over a period of one year. So, that is the first figure to be given. In our plan of things, we have not considered provision of bank guarantee as a part of a plan because from a bank's point of view, whether it is a bank guarantee or a debt funding, the facility has to come from the banks.

items.statement: Postpaid customer base grew QoQ and YoY driven by M2M and retail; prepaid offers Night Free Data, Weekend Data Rollover, Vi Guarantee 130GB extra data
items.quote: I am pleased to report that in the postpaid segment, we have been able to increase our customer base on QoQ as well as YoY ba sis. While a larger part of this increase is from M2M segment, we have seen consistent increase in retail postpaid customers over last one year

items.statement: Vi One converged broadband+mobile+OTT bundle expanded to Kerala via Asianet partnership; available in Mumbai, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Kerala
items.quote: In July, we signed a strategic partnership with Asianet, a leading broadband player in Kerala, and launched Vi One additionally across entire Kerala – one of Vi's leadership markets. We would be expanding this to other important markets as well going forward.

items.statement: Enterprise transforming to Techco with SD-WAN, IoT, CCaaS, cybersecurity; partnerships with PayU, Genesys, Infinity Labs for digital solutions
items.quote: We are transforming our offerings from a Telco into a Techco, significantly expanding our enterprise solutions beyond our core connectivity offerings. This transformation includes advanced offerings such as hybrid SD-WAN, SIP, IoT, IIoT and cloud services.

items.statement: Expect strong revenue growth in FY26 and even stronger bottom-line growth due to cost cutting measures
items.quote: I think that for financial year 26, I think as the penetration of lab-grown diamonds increases, we see revenue growth accelerating, and this coupled with the cost cutting measures that we have taken in our Customer Brand segment, we expect strong revenue growth in FY '26 and even stronger growth in bottom line because of our cost cutting measures.

items.statement: Expect net debt to reduce by 150-180 crore by end of FY25 and reach zero net debt by end of FY26
items.quote: So, as I mentioned earlier, we expect it to be significantly lower by about 150 to 180 crore by the end of this year. So, the net debt which is currently at 328 should be closer to 100 crore of net debt and subsequently by FY '26, the plan would be to be zero net debt.

items.statement: Allocated around 30 crore for infrastructure upgradation from preferential fund raise
items.quote: There is, however, some amount of upgradation of infrastructure that will take place which we have allocated I think around 30 crore for.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin from continuing operations reached 10.3% in Q2 FY25, up from 7.5% last year
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA expanded by 42% at Rs. 40 crore in Q2 of FY '25 versus Rs. 28 crore in the same period last year with adjusted EBITDA margins of 10.3% versus 7.5% last year.

items.statement: Owned Brands EBITDA margin reached 10.3% in Q2, a 575 bps year-over-year improvement
items.quote: In Owned Brands, our revenue grew by 7% year-over-year in Q2, while the EBITDA margin in this segment reached 10.3%, reflecting a substantial year-over-year improvement of 575 basis points.

items.statement: Customer Brands EBITDA margin improved 295 bps to 9.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In the Customer Brands division, revenue in Q2 stood at 293 crore with an EBITDA margin of 9.4%, making an impressive 295 basis point improvement.

items.statement: Licensed Brand business maintained stable revenues at Rs. 57 crore with EBITDA margin of 16.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 of FY '25, our Licensed Brand business maintained stable revenues at Rs. 57 crore on account of healthy flow of orders from our retail partners as well as the Direct-to-Consumer segment. It had an EBITDA margin of 16.5%

items.statement: Launched cost optimization initiative expected to deliver annual savings of 40-50 crore starting Q3 FY25
items.quote: We have launched an extensive cost optimization initiative towards the end of Q2, which will extend into Q3 and is expected to deliver annual savings of 40 to 50 crore.

items.statement: Expect strong consumer demand in Owned Brands segment during holiday season
items.quote: As we approach the holiday season, we expect strong consumer demand in this segment, setting us up for a promising end to the year.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond penetration in B2B business currently 6%, expected to grow meaningfully in coming quarters and years
items.quote: Currently the penetration is only 6%, which we expect to grow meaningfully in the coming quarters and the years to come.

items.statement: Plan to launch Owned Brands in UK in February 2025 for geographic expansion
items.quote: Currently, a large part of our brands is in the US. We plan to launch in February in the UK, and there will be some geographic expansion, which will lead to growth.

items.statement: Inflation pressures in US abating, expecting revenue growth acceleration in licensed and customer brand segments
items.quote: we have been through a two-year period where inflation in the U.S. was extremely high, and consumer demand was very subdued. I think we are seeing a lot of those pressures abating and going away

items.statement: Completed preferential fund raise of around 168 crore, proceeds to be used for debt reduction and infrastructure upgradation
items.quote: So, our intention is that we have currently obviously done a preferential fund raise of around 168 crore. So, this coupled with cash flow emerging from our business during Q3 and Q4 because as you know, seasonally our largest quarters are Q3 and a lot of the receivables go down afterwards. So, we expect a meaningful reduction in debt at the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance 25%-30% and EBITDA margin 17%-18%
items.quote: We are sticking to our guidance because we are expecting increase in the volumes of ductile iron pipes which are the major contributors to our topline and the bottomline.

items.statement: Target to become net term debt free within next 12 months; FY25 term debt guidance Rs. 225-250 crores
items.quote: Our FY25 guidance is to reduce the term debt to Rs. 225-Rs. 250 crores of which we are very optimistic of achieving.

items.statement: Total capex plan Rs. 1,000 crores; Rs. 700 crores incurred; balance Rs. 300 crores over next 9 months
items.quote: Out of this, approximately Rs. 700 crores has already been incurred and the balance Rs. 300 crores is expected to be incurred over the next 9 months.

items.statement: No new capex plan announced; future plans on drawing board, finalization by end of financial year
items.quote: Right now, there is no CAPEX plan which we have announced, but definitely we are looking at certain opportunities, but it will take time.

items.statement: DI pipe order book covers next 6 months; bid pipeline extremely robust
items.quote: Regarding DI we expect the relations to be at similar levels, maybe plus minus 2%-3% rather because we have the order booked for the coming 6 months.

items.statement: Value-added products (DI pipes + ferro alloys) revenue share to reach 65% by end FY25, 75%-80% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Then it should reach to 65% by the end of the current financial year, and then once the second part III of the ductile expansion is completed and it is fully operationalized, we will be north of 75, that is broad idea.

items.statement: DI pipe demand robust driven by JJM, AMRUT 2.0, irrigation schemes; specialized ferro alloy growth slow and steady
items.quote: The demand for ductile pipes, it is robust and we expect it to be robust because not only are we looking at the compression of the JIM scheme, we are also looking at the AMRUT 2.0.

items.statement: H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 17% vs 14% H1 FY24; Q2 FY25 segment EBITDA/t: DI pipe Rs. 22,000, ferro alloy Rs. 25,000, pig iron Rs. 5,000, TMT Rs. 4,000, sponge iron Rs. 3,000
items.quote: I am also very happy to share that the adjusted EBITDA margin for HI FY25 has been increased to 17% compared to 14% in H1 FY24.

items.statement: DI pipe realizations +8% YoY H1; Q2 YoY: ferro alloy +3%, DI pipe +7%; other products -5% to -7%; coking coal prices substantially down, chrome ore up
items.quote: On the realization front, realization for ferro alloys was similar to H1 FY24 and for ductile iron pipes, it increased by 8% whereas for all other products there was a drop-in realizations in the range of 5%-7%.

items.statement: DI pipe volume target 4 lakh tons FY25; H1 achieved ~1.5 lakh tons; run rate ~35,000-40,000 tons/month H2
items.quote: The total tonnage envisaged for this particular year it is around 4 lakh tons. In the first 6 months, we have achieved around 1,50,000 tons.

items.statement: Fund release from government schemes slower post-election; expect robust spending in next 4-5 months
items.quote: fund release in this quarter has been slower, but this again this post-election this phenomena we are seeing not only from the Jal Jeevan Mission scheme, but we are seeing actoss all these

items.statement: Deferred tax asset consumption ~Rs. 70-75 crores in Q3 FY25; carry forward losses ~Rs. 500 crores remaining
items.quote: As far as deferred tax assets, which were in our books, we have consumed it in last 3 quarters and the pending which I think in the third quarter will be consumed is around Rs. 70-Rs. 75 crores.

items.statement: Revenue may be flattish for FY25; EBITDA margin expected to improve by 50 bps in H2 FY25; double-digit margins seen only in Q1-Q2 FY26
items.quote: we believe that the revenue top line may be flattish for this year, so what we have said or thought in the last quarter. As far as EBITDA concerned, we expect at least it should improve by 0.5% for the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected at 10-15% based on current and new order book
items.quote: FY '26, based on this order book, and maybe next order book, we should definitely look at after getting new orders, to grow by 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Order book INR11,104 cr as of Sep 30, 2024; plus INR4,320 cr new orders post Sep and INR265 cr L1; total INR15,424 cr
items.quote: As on September 30, 2024, our balance order book stands at INR11,104 crores. This excludes additional orders received from projects post September '24 worth INR4,320 crores and also excludes L1 of INR265 crores. The total of curren t order book stands at INR15,424 crores

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 11% in Q2 FY25; H1 FY25 margin 9.1% (+60 bps YoY); consolidated EBITDA margin not explicitly stated
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR160 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11%.

items.statement: Double-digit standalone margins expected only in Q1-Q2 FY26 as new higher-margin projects (11-12% bid margins) ramp up
items.quote: The double-digit numbers would be seen only in Q1, Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex ~INR33 cr; H2 FY25 capex planned INR35-40 cr
items.quote: So in H1, we did capex of approximately INR33 crores. And in H2, we may prepare another INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Acquiring 34% of ACL plus CCDs from Macquarie/SBI for INR1,526 cr; long stop date June 2025, expected completion Mar-May 2025
items.quote: We expect this transaction the long stop date for this transaction is June '25, and we expect to get that done somewhere in the month of March -- April, May '25.

items.statement: Divestment of 5 BOT subsidiaries to Indian Highways Concessions Trust at enterprise value INR5,718 cr (equity value INR2,539 cr)
items.quote: The aggregate enterprise value of the transaction is either INR5,718 crores, subject to adjustment of cash and debt, translating into an equity value of INR2,539 crores.

items.statement: Land monetization by Viva Highways at Hinjewadi, Pune for INR453 cr (book value ~INR65 cr, profit ~INR370 cr); proceeds upstreamed to ABL
items.quote: Land owned by Viva Highways Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, under its real estate portfolio situated at Hinjewadi, Pune, has been monetized for a total consideration of INR453 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR6,881 cr as of Sep 30, 2024; expect INR3,000-3,500 cr reduction by Mar 2025 from BOT/HAM asset sales
items.quote: we expect that at least of INR3,000 crores, INR3,500-odd crores of debt definitely will go down before March.

items.statement: NHAI bid pipeline ~INR1 lakh cr; Ashoka participating in ~INR65,000 cr; bids to be opened ~INR9,000 cr
items.quote: Around INR1 lakh crore bidding is there from NHAI. Out of which, INR65,000, we'll be participating. There are bids to be opened of around INR9,000 crores which we already bid.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue mix: Road EPC/HAM 49%, Power EPC 28%, Railways 12%, Buildings/others 11%
items.quote: Road EPC and road HAM contributed 49%. Power EPC contributed 28%. Railways stood at 12%. And other segments, like building EPC and others, contributed to 11%.

items.statement: Impairment reversal expected: ~INR800 cr at ACL level and ~INR250-300 cr at ABL level post BOT asset sale
items.quote: So there will be impairment at ACL level which will be reversed once these assets are sold off, which is almost -- at ACL balance sheet of almost INR800 crores. And at ABL balance sheet, there could be a reversal of approximately INR250 crores to INR300 crores post sale.

items.statement: Target 5,000 tenancies in FY25 and another 5,000 in FY26, reaching 15,000 total by FY26 end
items.quote: We are 100% sure we will deliver 5,000 tenancies in FY '25 and same in FY '26.

items.statement: Revenue growth projected around 30% for FY25
items.quote: The revenue for '24, '25 projection -- percentage wise around 30% of growth overall.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 70-75% and PAT margin around 35% for FY26 and beyond
items.quote: We'll do another 5,000 tenancies for FY '25, 5,000 tenancies in FY '26 with the same EBITDA percentage of around 70 %, 75% and PAT of around 35%.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at ₹400-450 cr, funded by internal accruals and debt
items.quote: Again, CapEx in FY '26 would be around ₹400 crores, ₹450 crores, out of which maximum will come from internal accruals.

items.statement: Preferential issue of up to ₹350 cr (₹250 cr from investors, ₹100 cr from promoters) targeted for completion by December
items.quote: In terms of ₹350 crores CapEx, what we are planning around ₹250 crores will be done with the investors , plus ₹100 crores will do warrant with the promoter.

items.statement: Current visibility: 3,000-3,500 towers from Vodafone Idea and 2,500+ from BSNL; targeting 4,500-5,000 tenancies in H2 FY25
items.quote: We are on 3,000, 3,500 towers loaded by Vodafone and another 2,500 towers loaded by BSNL. That's in current visibility, which keep adding month-on-month basis.

items.statement: Vodafone Idea rolling out aggressively with 50,000 small cell and full-size sites ordered; BSNL rollout accelerating
items.quote: Vodafone Idea has already ordered for 4G and 5G for Nokia Siemens 50,000 small cell and full size. So, looking to the second round of investment, it's coming to VIL.

items.statement: Fibre opportunity: targeting 5 lakh km in 2-3 years; FTTH targeting 5 lakh home passes in 3-4 years; IP-1 model for fibre
items.quote: We are planning to add another 5 lacs kilometre of fibre network in next two years to three years.

items.statement: Average revenue per tower per month ₹35,000-40,000; macro tower tenancy 1.8x, small cell 1.1x
items.quote: It should be around 35,000, but it will vary from subject to subject. Bombay, I would get around 40, 45. Rest of the India can be around 25,000, 27,000.

items.statement: Trade receivables elevated due to electricity reimbursements (~₹4 cr/month, 90-day cycle) and Vodafone Idea paying in 90 days vs monthly advance
items.quote: Approximately, ₹4 Cr per month. Around ₹4 Cr minimum per month minimum is my reimbursement. Which I get in next 90 days which by default gets added to Debtors

items.statement: Inorganic growth: targeting companies with Airtel/Jio tenancy in weak circles; advanced negotiations with 4-5 targets; likely closure next quarter
items.quote: We are in advanced stages of negotiation. As and when we're able to acquire some company, it will give you notification on exchanges.

items.statement: Tower deployment timeline: 15-20 days for RTT, 30 days for GBT after service order; 9,000 towers expected by March 2025
items.quote: In overall portfolio, yes. We'll have around 9,000 towers by March.

items.statement: Management reiterates guidance of flat to single-digit revenue growth for FY25 and expects improved margins versus last year.
items.quote: We stick to our guidance of flat revenue growth to single-digit revenue growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Management expects better margins in FY25 versus FY24 due to resolved inventory issues and lower discounting.
items.quote: And we've also reiterated that the margin would be better in this financial year in this quarter as well as in the next quarter as compared to last financial year because the inventory issue which affected us last year majorly in margins has already been sorted out.

items.statement: Winter season started late but sales have picked up in the last week; management expects winter sales at par with last year with less discounting.
items.quote: It should be at par with last year, not muted. And we'll - because there's less pressure of inventory on us, so this will - that gives us headroom to offer lesser discounts.

items.statement: Management expects inventory levels to drastically come down by 31st December compared to last year.
items.quote: But one thing which I can guarantee you with surety is that once we end this quarter, 31st December, you would sce that inventory level has drastically come down as compared to last year's levels

items.statement: Company plans to open 40-50 EBOs in FY25 and targets a blend of 10-15% company-owned stores.
items.quote: We are already given a guidance of around 40 to 50 EBO stores in this financial year.

items.statement: Online sales contribute ~7.5% of revenue; quick commerce partnerships with Blinkit, Swiggy, Zepto are being tested.
items.quote: So around 7.5% of company's revenue comes from online sales as a whole, And looking at quick commerce specifically, we've just closed 2 deliverics to Blinkit and Swiggy, respectively

items.statement: Management anticipates double-digit revenue growth in FY26 as inventory and discounting issues are resolved.
items.quote: And we anticipate going forward that we could have a double-digit growth next financial year, because whatever problems have been there last year's imventory levels, this year's inventory levels and other things, they have been taken care of

items.statement: Management confident of ~100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY25 despite H1 decline, citing ad spend normalization and better winter dispatches.
items.quote: So we are very confident that whatever we have stated carlier in our con call that there can be 100 basis points of margin improvement

items.statement: Like-for-like sales declined 3-4% in H1; EBO additions and online growth expected to offset weakness in MBO/SIS/LFS channels.
items.quote: So we sec that there could be a decline of around 3% to 4% as far as like-to-like growth is concerned

items.statement: Footwear pilot sold 150-200 pairs/day online; H1 revenue INR3.4 cr; target INR10 cr for FY26, not FY25.
items.quote: Yes. So year-to-date, we've done around INR3.4 crores of revenue from footwear.

items.statement: MBO count fell from 1,774 to 1,611 due to conversion to shop-in-shops and closure of 50-60 stores for payment issues; further reduction expected.
items.quote: Also, there are around 50 to 60 MBOs that the company closes because of bad payment issues or the business being too small.

items.statement: Ad spend front-loaded in H1 due to new campaign production and summer promotion; annual target maintained at 3% of revenue.
items.quote: First is that we've produced a new campaign for our winter collection as well as our summer collection. So all the cost of that production has been added into our first quarter.

items.statement: Even in a pessimistic flat-demand scenario, management expects ~10% revenue growth in FY26 from internal efforts.
items.quote: Even though with a lot of pessimistic view, if we have that, everything remains same, still we'll be able to grow around 10% next year.

items.statement: Receivables higher in MBO/SIS (90-day terms); online/LFS/EBO are sales-based with faster collection; margin difference across channels only 100-200 bps.
items.quote: The receivables are basically more in MBO and SIS segment because we have a 90-day payment basis. But in case of online, LFS and EBO are sales-based. So as the sales happens, the recsivables comes first

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue guidance: 15-20% decline; FY26 revenue guidance: up to 30%+ growth over FY25
items.quote: The given the situation, the revised guidance for the FY '25 would be 15% to 20% decline, and accordingly FY '26 would be up to 30% plus growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance: 12-12.5% for FY25, around 13% for FY26
items.quote: EBIDTA Margins will be around 12% to 12.5% in FY'25 and around 13% in FY'26.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands over Rs 19,900 crore as of 30 Sep 2024, including Rs 6,670 crore of new EPC contracts secured in FY25
items.quote: As of 30 th September 2024, the company’s unexecuted order book stands over Rs. 19,900 crores, which includes 3 EPC contracts secured by the Company for aggregate contract value of Rs. 6,670 Crore

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY25 maintained at Rs 13,000-15,000 crore; Rs 6,700 crore already secured, expecting another Rs 6,000-8,000 crore from non-MoRTH authorities
items.quote: With regard to order book we still maintain, as I mentioned in the beginning of the year that our order book for the current financial year guidance will between INR13,000 crores to INR15,000 crores. Already we secured around INR6,700 crores of orders. So remaining we are expecting another INR6,000 crores to INR8000 crores orders from authorities and proponents other than MoRTH.

items.statement: Capex revised down to Rs 30-40 crore for FY25 from earlier Rs 80-100 crore; FY26 capex estimated at Rs 100-120 crore
items.quote: This year, capex, we want to revise from INR80 -100 crores to INR30-40 crores sir. And next year it will be around INR100-120 crores.

items.statement: Diversifying into area development (CIDCO NAINA project 90% share), railways, industrial corridors, and water treatment beyond Jal Jeevan Mission
items.quote: Apart from railway projects, as you know, we got the area development project, major area development project from CI DCO. It is certainly a diversification because it is not a highway project, it is not a railway project, it is a development project.

items.statement: MoRTH debarment order from 18 Oct 2024; writ petition rejected; evaluating appeal options; existing LOAs and signed concession agreements unaffected
items.quote: That Writ Petition have been not been allowed by the single bench of honorable high court. We are evaluating options, including file of an appeal against the order of the MoRTH as well as the order of the single bench.

items.statement: Asset monetization: 10 HAM assets (equity invested Rs 1,490 cr, enterprise value ~Rs 7,690 cr) to close by end FY25; remaining 2 assets by H1 FY26
items.quote: Out of total assets for which we had entered into a master security purchase agreement in the month of January, we expect to close 10 mandates, 10 assets before the end of the current financial year. And the remaining two assets will be in the next financial year

items.statement: H1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin 25.1% includes arbitration award; core EBITDA margin without external income ~12%
items.quote: No. Actually, H1, it includes the arbitration award. So it is 25%. Otherwise, the EBITDA margin without considering the arbitration award, what we have received, it would be around 12% without external income.

items.statement: JJM revenue guidance revised down to Rs 1,200 crore for FY25 from Rs 1,500 crore due to heavy monsoon impacting underground works
items.quote: The revised guidance is INR1,200 crores. And this is basically essentially due to the active monsoon, many of the works affected at the site.

items.statement: Equity investment of Rs 872 crore remaining for HAM projects over next 2-3 years: Rs 486 cr in FY25 (Oct-Mar), Rs 256 cr in FY26, Rs 132 cr in FY27
items.quote: In case we receive the appointed of all the BOT HAM projects by end of calendar year this year (Oct-March'25) we have to infuse around INR486 crores and FY2026 INR256 crores and FY2027 INR132 crores.

items.statement: Received Rs 170 crore from Andhra Pradesh for canal project (Rs 62 cr in Aug, Rs 108 cr in Oct); balance outstanding ~Rs 55 crore; execution to resume Dec/Jan targeting Rs 200-300 cr in FY25 and Rs 400 cr in FY26
items.quote: Company has received Rs. 62 crores in the month of August 24 and Rs.108.0 crores in the month of October 24, totalling to Rs. 170.00 crores out of the total outstanding of 222.0 crores from the Government of Andhra Pradesh towards work done in the Canal Upgradation Project in AP.

items.statement: Eight new projects worth over Rs 11,000 crore (5 earlier awarded + 3 recent MSRDC/CIDCO) expected to get appointed dates by end CY2024; meaningful revenue from Q4 FY25, significant from FY26
items.quote: These eight mandates will have a value of over INR11,000 crores for which we are expecting our appointed dates before end of this calendar year. And we are quite hopeful that we'll commence construction and preconstruction activity right now.

items.statement: Credit rating reaffirmed at AA+ long-term by rating agencies post MoRTH debarment order; no change in rating

items.quote: Then, whatever we had earlier said that we will be aiming to achieve 14 -15% EBITDA margin, we will be again well on course to achieving that kind of margin of 14-15%.

The custom duty on dimer acid import remained the same and so the company had to absorb higher raw material cost - both to stay competitive as well as retain its market share in the domestic market.

items.quote: We believe that the copper demand shall be increasing due to a combination of three key themes that is traditional economic growth and the newer themes of energy transition and digital, that is primarily the data centers.

items.quote: Earlier we had given an estimate of June, July of the next financial year. So we currently think we should be able to have the construction complete.

items.quote: I totally agree with you, we have seen in our case the incentive out of the total salary is around 25%, 30% only. It has never gone beyond that. Just to give example, if RO gets around 15,000, so around 4000, 3500 to 4000 has been our average incentive over the years

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex was INR 370 crores including INR 131 crores for Mumbai land acquisition
items.quote: In the first half of FY2025, INR 370 crores of capex were incurred, including INR 131 crores related to the acquisition of land in Mumbai.

items.statement: Existing units capex INR 470 crores; Noida capex INR 500 crores to be spent in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26; other projects over next 3-4 years
items.quote: If you see that what we are maintaining here is that there will be about INR 470 crores of capex on the existing units. And then the INR 500 crores on the Noida which will be spend in the somewhere Q4FY25 and Q1 of the next financial year when we order major medical equipment, etcetera.

items.statement: Signed O&M agreement for 750-bed super specialty hospital in Pitampura, New Delhi to be developed over 4 years
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that last week we signed an Operation and Management Agreement to operate and management a state-of-the-art 750 bed super specialty hospital in Pitampura, New Delhi.

items.statement: Noida facility construction progressing well, anticipated opening in Q1 FY2026
items.quote: Construction of our Noida facility is progressing well and we anticipate opening in Q1 FY2026.

items.statement: Plan to add 50 beds in Patna in coming months; capacity for 200 more beds in Lucknow and 150 in Patna to be brought online in near future
items.quote: We are also planning an additional 50 beds in Patna, which we hope to come on board in the next coming months. Furthermore, we have capacity within our current infrastructure to add 200 more beds in Lucknow and approximately 150 beds in Patna, which we will bring online in the near future.

items.statement: Mature hospital EBITDA margins stable around 25.3%; management believes slow and steady approach better than aggressive tariff hikes
items.quote: So if you look at the matured one, you will see that the margins have moved around 25%, 25.5%, 25.3%. So yes, if you look at the last several quarters, it does appear that they are reasonably stable.

items.statement: Mature hospital ARPOB grew 6.2% to INR 67,059 driven by tariff increases in Gurugram and Indore and case mix changes
items.quote: ARPOB grew by 6.2% to INR 67,059 in Q2 FY25, driven by tariff increases in Gurugram and Indore and changes in our case mix.

items.statement: Developing hospital ARPOB declined 5.9% YoY to INR 53,724 due to change in payor and case mix with higher Patna share
items.quote: ARPOB declined by 5.9% year on year due to a change in payor and case mix to INR 53,724.

items.statement: Indore project delayed due to litigation; South Delhi (DLF) project delayed ~1 year due to pollution-related construction curbs but on track
items.quote: Our Indore project, as you rightly pointed out, is stuck in litigation. We are, of course, exploring all other as well as current opportunities in Indore. And our DLF project or a partnership with DLF in Delhi is very much on track. Unfortunately, given some of the pollution challenges in Delhi, we have been a little constrained on some of the construction activity.

items.statement: Pitampura O&M project: society to invest INR 200-250 crores for civil structure; Medanta to invest in medical equipment and finishing
items.quote: As far as capex, I would assume that the partner would be putting in somewhere INR 200 crores or maybe a little bit more, INR 200 - 250 crores of capex because they'll be putting up the civil structure, etcetera. And we will be putting in the services and the medical equipment and of course, the finishing to operate it.

items.statement: Guest house project at Medicity: INR 250 crores for 250 keys, timeline 3-4 years
items.quote: 250 keys is what we're planning right now. And we'll see how it goes. Like I said, we are building on less than half of the actual land. So if it is a success, maybe we need to scale it up.

items.statement: Medical college at Medicity: estimated INR 250-300 crores for 4-5 lakh sq ft build-out, starting with 100 seats
items.quote: And I think our estimate is that 4 lakhs building like that should probably also cost somewhere around INR 250 crores, maybe thereabouts INR 300 crores, let's say, if you budget.

items.statement: International patient revenue share at 6% (down from 11-12% pre-COVID) due to Lucknow/Patna dilution; expected to grow as NCR facilities expand
items.quote: As Lucknow and Patna contribute to the total pool, the share of international business will naturally reduce. And that's why you're seeing it as 6% because of the fact that Lucknow and Patna don't have any international business. Definitely as NCR facilities come on board, there should be an increase in the share of international business that comes on board.

items.statement: Geopolitical factors affect international patients (Afghanistan near zero, Bangladesh challenges); considered temporary blips
items.quote: Afghanistan was a big source of international patients. For India, that has become basically zero. These days, we see challenges in Bangladesh, which is another big source of international business. So I think that international business will be there. But given what happens across various countries that goes up and down as well.

items.statement: Lucknow developing hospital EBITDA margin improved from 24.5% in Q1 to 29.9% in Q2 FY25; recovery gradual with volume-driven model
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved from 24.5% in Q1 FY25 to 29.9% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Management expects to be very close to achieving the previously guided 40% revenue growth for FY25 and full-year EBITDA margin of 20-21%.
items.quote: We should be able, or we should be very close to achieve the number that we quoted in our last -- in revenue calls and in last investor call. And so we are hoping, and we are quite positive that we should reach to those numbers.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% for FY25, lower than prior 22-23% due to Welcome brand dilution.
items.quote: We are expecting that the EBITDA should stand -- the whole year EBITDA should stand around or between 20% to 21%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin was 17.97%, below the guided 20% range, due to muted demand and raw material pressure.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q2 F Y '25 is 17.97% compared to 20%, which is our guided range

items.statement: Implemented strategic price increase of ~3.5% across portfolio effective October; industry average hike 5-7%.
items.quote: Our price increase and average increase has been about 3.5%.

items.statement: Q2 demand muted due to prolonged monsoon; Q3 expected lower historically but offset by OEM and South/West growth; Q4 anticipated stronger.
items.quote: Historically, always Q3 has been a little down compared to Q2 and Q4 has been more or less the same or better than Q2.

items.statement: Acrylic PU share rose to 40% of core wood coating sales in H1 FY25 from 25% last year; carries 10-12% higher net margin than PU.
items.quote: the rest 40% were the acrylic and water bond, which was about 25% contribution last y ear as we talk about in H1. This year was about

items.quote: we will be doing a new capex of about INR20- odd crores in the Gujarat to set up a new facility to produce another 16,000 tons a year, whi ch can generate a revenue of economic polyurethane products of about INR400 crores

items.statement: Welcome brand acquisition contributed INR11 crores in Q2; full-year target revised to INR60 crores from earlier INR100 crores.
items.quote: For this year, we are eyeing, and we are eyeing a revenue close to INR60 crores.

items.quote: We are capping our acquisition in the range of about INR100 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Welcome brand EBITDA margin ~15%, below Sirca core margins, diluting consolidated EBITDA.
items.quote: EBITDA here is coming out to be about 15%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex of INR22 crores was entirely for Welcome brand acquisition; no other capex incurred.
items.quote: No, that is spent for the acquisition of the brand Welcome. Dishant Jain: Okay. Apoorv Agarwal: Yes. We have not done any other new capex as of now

items.statement: Inventory elevated due to demand shortfall vs planning and Red Sea shipping delays increasing import lead time by 30 days; expect normalization in 4 months.
items.quote: in the next 4 months, we will be in a much bett er position because against the top 10 products will be here and the whole imported stock will be out, where we will be working at a 30 days inventory

items.statement: Marketing spend steady at 4-5% of revenue; focused on B2B architect/contractor meets in South/West; pulled back in North due to weak demand.
items.quote: currently, again, we are more or less on the sa me percentage that we did last year, which averages between 4% to 5% of our
